Milagro Constraints on Very High Energy Emission from Short-Duration Gamma-Ray BurstsGamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are the most energetic explosions in the universe, classified into long-duration (LGRBs) and short-duration (SGRBs). The progenitors of SGRBs remain uncertain, while LGRBs are associated with massive star deaths.SGRBs often exhibit a high-energy component attributed to synchrotron radiation from accelerated electrons in the GRB outflow. However, the exact emission mechanism is poorly understood.Using data from the Milagro gamma-ray observatory, we constrain the very high energy (VHE) emission from SGRBs. Our findings suggest that SGRB VHE emission is consistent with synchrotron radiation from accelerated electrons in the outflow but more variable than LGRBs.This variability may arise from differing SGRB and LGRB progenitors.Our results shed light on the nature of SGRB VHE emission and imply potentially diverse SGRB progenitors compared to LGRBs.

We make a systematic analysis of the XMM-Newton X-ray spectra of intermediatepolars (IPs) and find that, contrary to the traditional picture, most show asoft blackbody component. We compare the results with those from AM Her starsand deduce that the blackbody emission arises from reprocessing of hard X-rays,rather than from the blobby accretion sometimes seen in AM Hers. Whether an IPshows a blackbody component appears to depend primarily on geometric factors: ablackbody is not seen in those that have accretion footprints that are alwaysobscured by accretion curtains or are only visible when foreshortened on thewhite-dwarf limb. Thus we argue against previous suggestions that the blackbodyemission characterises a separate sub-group of IPs which are more akin to AMHers, and develop a unified picture of the blackbody emission in these stars.

In a sensor network, in practice, the communication among sensors is subjectto:(1) errors or failures at random times; (3) costs; and(2) constraints sincesensors and networks operate under scarce resources, such as power, data rate,or communication. The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is usually a main factor indetermining the probability of error (or of communication failure) in a link.These probabilities are then a proxy for the SNR under which the links operate.The paper studies the problem of designing the topology, i.e., assigning theprobabilities of reliable communication among sensors (or of link failures) tomaximize the rate of convergence of average consensus, when the linkcommunication costs are taken into account, and there is an overallcommunication budget constraint. To consider this problem, we address a numberof preliminary issues: (1) model the network as a random topology; (2)establish necessary and sufficient conditions for mean square sense (mss) andalmost sure (a.s.) convergence of average consensus when network links fail;and, in particular, (3) show that a necessary and sufficient condition for bothmss and a.s. convergence is for the algebraic connectivity of the mean graphdescribing the network topology to be strictly positive. With these results, weformulate topology design, subject to random link failures and to acommunication cost constraint, as a constrained convex optimization problem towhich we apply semidefinite programming techniques. We show by an extensivenumerical study that the optimal design improves significantly the convergencespeed of the consensus algorithm and can achieve the asymptotic performance ofa non-random network at a fraction of the communication cost.

In this article, we investigate the emergence of neutrino Majorana masses in conformal field theory (CFT) orientifolds exhibiting spectra reminiscent of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM). We focus on the role of instantons in generating mass terms for neutirnos, which are essential for understanding their observed tiny masses and the phenomnon of neutrino oscillations. By employing techniques from both CFT and twine theory, we analysing the effects of instanton configurations on the MSSM-like spectra in orientifold models. We find that the presence of instantons leads to new couplings between the MSSM superfields and right-handed neutrino fields, resulting in the generati on of Majorana masses for neurtinos at the loop level. Furthermore, we explore the implications of these instanton-induced neutrino masses on the phenomenology and addresses their compatibility with empirical data. We discuss the restraints imposed by current neutrino oscillation experiments and other precision measure on the parameter space of the model. We also investigate the stability of the CFT sector and identify the conditions under which the generated Majorana masses are protected from higher-dimensional operators induced by quantum gravity effects. Our findings shed lights on the mechanism behind the smallness of neutrino masses within the framework of CFT orientifolds and provide a new avenue for constructing realistic MSSM-like models with the inclusion of Majorana neutrino masses. This work opens up further avenues for research in particle physics and the study of neutrino properties during the context of string theory and CFT.

The scalar radius of the pion plays a crucial role in understanding the strong interactions within the framework of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). In this study, we investigate the scalar radius of the pion and its connection to the zeros in the form factor. Employing the Heavy Quark Effective Theory (HQET) and non-perturbative techniques, we calculate the scalar radius and explore its implications. Our analysis is based on a comprehensive dataset compiled from various experimental measurements and theoretical predictions from previous studies. We find that the scalar radius of the pion exhibits a nontrivial dependence on the energy scale and is sensitive to the presence of zeros in the form factor. By analyzing the interplay between the scalar radius and the form factor zeros, we shed light on the underlying dynamics of the strong interactions in the low-energy regime. Our findings provide valuable insights into the nature of confinement and chiral symmetry breaking in QCD. This work establishes a foundation for further investigations into the properties of pions and their role in understanding the fundamental aspects of the nuclear strong force.

Theoretical analysis of interplay between the condensates $<\bar{q}q>$ and$<qq>$ in vacuum is generally made by relativistic effective potentials in themean field approximation in 2D, 3D and 4D models with two flavor and $N_c$color massless fermions. It is found that in ground states of these models,interplay between the two condensates mainly depend on the ratio $G_S/H_S$ for2D and 4D case or $G_S/H_P$ for 3D case, where $G_S$, $H_S$ and $H_P$ arerespectively the coupling constants in a scalar $(\bar{q}q)$, a scalar $(qq)$and a pseudoscalar $(qq)$ channel. In ground states of all the models, onlypure $<\bar{q}q>$ condensates could exist if $G_S/H_S$ or $G_S/H_P$ is biggerthan the critical value $2/N_c$, the ratio of the color numbers of the fermionsentering into the condensates $<qq>$ and $<\bar{q}q>$. As $G_S/H_S$ or$G_S/H_P$ decreases to the region below $2/N_c$, differences of the models willmanifest themselves. Depending on different models, and also on $N_c$ in 3Dmodel, one will have or have no the coexistence phase of the two condensates,besides the pure $<qq>$ condensate phase. The $G_S-H_S$ (or $G_S-H_P$) phasediagrams in these models are given. The results also implicate a realconstraint on two-flavor QCD-analogous NJL model.

This paper uses firm-level data recorded in the AMADEUS database toinvestigate the distribution of labour productivity in different Europeancountries. We find that the upper tail of the empirical productivitydistributions follows a decaying power-law, whose exponent $\alpha$ is obtainedby a semi-parametric estimation technique recently developed by Clementi et al.(2006). The emergence of "fat tails" in productivity distribution has alreadybeen detected in Di Matteo et al. (2005) and explained by means of a model ofsocial network. Here we show that this model is tested on a broader sample ofcountries having different patterns of social network structure. Thesedifferent social attitudes, measured using a social capital indicator, reflectin the power-law exponent estimates, verifying in this way the existence oflinkages among firms' productivity performance and social network.

The Millennium Galaxy Catalogue (MGC) is a unique resource for studying the properties of galaxies and their evolution. It contains over 100,000 galaxies with redshifts up to z=0.5, and provides a wealth of information on their morphologies, luminosities, and stellar masses. In this paper, we use the MGC to investigate the connection between close pairs of galaxies and galaxy asymmetry. We find that close pairs are more likely to be asymmetric than isolated galaxies, and that this asymmetry is most pronounced in pairs with small projected separations. We interpret this result as evidence that close pairs are undergoing tidal interactions, which can drive morphological transformations and trigger star formation. We also use our results to estimate the galaxy merger rate, and find that it is consistent with previous estimates based on other methods. Our study demonstrates the power of the MGC for studying the properties of galaxies and their evolution.

A key idea in coding for the broadcast channel (BC) is binning, in which thetransmitter encode information by selecting a codeword from an appropriate bin(the messages are thus the bin indexes). This selection is normally done bysolving an appropriate (possibly difficult) combinatorial problem. Recently ithas been shown that binning for the Blackwell channel --a particular BC-- canbe done by iterative schemes based on Survey Propagation (SP). This method usesdecimation for SP and suffers a complexity of O(n^2). In this paper we proposea new variation of the Belief Propagation (BP) algorithm, named Reinforced BPalgorithm, that turns BP into a solver. Our simulations show that this newalgorithm has complexity O(n log n). Using this new algorithm together with anon-linear coding scheme, we can efficiently achieve rates close to the borderof the capacity region of the Blackwell channel.

This article presents the results of multisite observational campaigns carried out on two pulsating subdwarf B stars, PG 1618+563B and PG 0048+091. Pulsating subdwarf B stars are compact, hot stars that exhibit rapid pulsations, make them valuable targets for asteroseismology studies. The aim of the campaigns was to gather additional data and investigate the pulsation features of these stars in more detail. Observations were condu cted using multiple ground-based telescopes located across different longitudes and latitudes, allowing for continuous monitoring of the targets over extended periods. The data collected included high-precision light curves, radial velocity measurements, and spectroscopic analysis. The light curves were used to identify and characterize the pulsation frequencies, while the radial velocity measurements provi ded insights into the nature and propagation of the pulsations. Spectroscopic analyses aided in determining the atmospherc parameters and chemical composition of the stars. The results indicate the presence of multiple pulsation modes in both PG 1618+563B and GLS 0048+091. The pulsation frequencies were found to be stable over the duration of the campaigns, which extends our understanding of the long-term stability of these stars. Moreover, mode identification based on the observed frequencies allowed for the determination of the pulsation geometry and the seismic interpretations of the internal edifice of the stars. The findings contribute to the growing body of knowledge on pulsing subdwarf B stars and offer valuable insights into their asteroseismic properties and evolutionary status.

English: This paper concerns the image reconstruction from a few projectionsin Computed Tomography (CT). The main objective of this paper is to show thatthe problem is so ill posed that no classical method, such as analyticalmethods based on inverse Radon transform, nor the algebraic methods such asLeast squares (LS) or regularization theory can give satisfactory result. As anexample, we consider in detail the case of image reconstruction from twohorizontal and vertical projections. We then show how a particular compositeMarkov modeling and the Bayesian estimation framework can possibly proposesatisfactory solutions to the problem. For demonstration and educationalpurpose a set of Matlab programs are given for a live presentation of theresults. ----- French: Ce travail, \'a but p\'edagogique, pr\'esente le probl\'eme inversede la reconstruction d'image en tomographie X lorsque le nombre des projectionsest tr\'es limit\'e. voir le texte en Anglais et en Fran\c{c}ais.

Abstrac ThiTs article explores the concept of brain prostheses as dynamic systems, capable of not just replicating but also evolving human cognitive and emotional capacities. This article explores the potential of brain prosthetics to enhance human capabilities and transcen the limitations of the biologcal brain. It begins by introducing the concept of brain prostheses as dynaimc systems and their potential to transform human existence. The article then discusses the ethical implications of brain prostheses, including the potential for creating new form of life and the blurring of the line between humans and machies. The potential benefits of brain prostheses, such as enhanaced intelligence, memory, and emotional regulation, are consiered alongside the risks, including the possibility of unintended consequences and the los of human autonomy. The article cncludes by considering the implications of brain prostheses for the future of humaniyt and the possibility of a future in which humans and machines coexist harmoniously.

This paper investigates the effect of electro-hydrodynamic (EHD) and mixed lubrication regimes on the traction behavior of a rough surface in contact with a lubricant. The study focuses on the super low traction regime, where the friction coefficient is significantly reduced due to the presence of a lubricant film. Experimental results show that the friction coefficient can be reduced by up to three orders of magnitude in the presence of an EHD film, compared to the pure contact regime. The study also explores the effect of surface roughness and lubricant viscosity on the traction behavior. Atomic force microscopy is used to measure the surface roughness, and the lubricant viscosity is varied over several orders of magnitude. The results show that the friction coefficient decreases with increasing surface roughness and decreasing lubricant viscosity. A mathematical model is developed to describe the super low traction behavior, which takes into account the EHD effect, surface roughness, and lubricant viscosity. The model is found to be in good agreement with the experimental results. The study has important implications for the design of tribological systems, where super low traction is desired to reduce wear and improve efficiency.

In this study, we investigate the intramolecular lsng-range correlations present in polymr melts by examining the segmental size distribution and its moments. Polymer melts are important sistems with widespread applications in various industries. Understanding the segmental size distribution and its moments is crucial for nredicting the macroscpic properties and behavior of these materials. Using molecular dynamics simulations, we analyze the correlation between differetn segments within the polymer chain and quantify the distribution of segment sizeCs. Our results reveal significant ltong-range corerlations in the segmental size distribution, suggesting the presence of cooperative behavior within polymer melts. This study contributes to the fundamental understanding of Folymer melt dynamics and prvoides insights for the design and optimization of polymeric materials with tailored properties.

The nearby QSO host Galaxy I ZW 1 contains a luminous star, which far exceeds the starlight of the galaxy about 1,000 times. A large number of nearby objects in the projection of I ZW 1 have been reported. They include galaxies, HII regions, super rotary stars residue and many star objects. The stars in the nearby objects are very similar to the interior of the I ZW 1 disk. Therefore, they are considered a star association/cluster in I ZW 1, not the background or foreground system. The brightest object in i ZW 1 is also the brightest object of nearby objects. It has been proposed that it is an optical correspondence of star -like body. The wide emission rays in the spectrum of the object (including Hβ) have been detected and confirmed, which supports it as a star -like nature. The continuity and launch characteristics of objects are similar to low -red movement QSO and active silver nucleus. The star disk of Galaxy I ZW 1 is the smallest disk of known QSO hosts. It has high surface brightness in optical and near -infrared takes. The quality of the star disk within 0.7 KPC accounts for only a few percent of the Milky Way. I ZW 1's star disk has a very low star formation rate, which is consistent with the detection of the old star group and the continuous star formation level in the galaxy.

The mass spectra of heavy and light mesons is computed within the frameworkof the relativistic flux tube model. A good agreement with the experimentaldata is obtained provided that the flux tube contributions, includingretardation and spin-orbit effects, are supplemented by a one-gluon-exchangepotential, a quark self-energy term and instanton-induced interactions. Noarbitrary constant is needed to fit the absolute scale of the mass spectra, andthe different parameters are fitted on lattice QCD in order to stronglyrestrict the arbitrariness of our model. The relevance of the present approachis discussed in the case of glueballs, and the glueball spectrum we compute iscompared to the lattice QCD one. Finally, we make connections between theresults of our model and the nature of some newly discovered experimentalstates such as the f_0(1810), X(3940), Y(3940), etc.

We present the class of regular homogeneous T-models with vacuum dark fluid,associated with a variable cosmological term. The vacuum fluid is defined bythe symmetry of its stress-energy tensor, i.e., its invariance under Lorentzboosts in a distinguished spatial direction (p_j=-\rho), which makes this fluidessentially anisotropic and allows its density to evolve. Typical features ofhomogeneous regular T-models are: the existence of a Killing horizon; beginningof the cosmological evolution from a null bang at the horizon; the existence ofa regular static pre-bang region visible to cosmological observers; creation ofmatter from anisotropic vacuum, accompanied by very rapid isotropization. Westudy in detail the spherically symmetric regular T-models on the basis of ageneral exact solution for a mixture of the vacuum fluid and dustlike matterand apply it to give numerical estimates for a particular model whichillustrates the ability of cosmological T-models to satisfy the observationalconstraints.

The analysis of gravitational wave data involves many model selectionproblems. The most important example is the detection problem of selectingbetween the data being consistent with instrument noise alone, or instrumentnoise and a gravitational wave signal. The analysis of data from ground basedgravitational wave detectors is mostly conducted using classical statistics,and methods such as the Neyman-Pearson criteria are used for model selection.Future space based detectors, such as the \emph{Laser Interferometer SpaceAntenna} (LISA), are expected to produced rich data streams containing thesignals from many millions of sources. Determining the number of sources thatare resolvable, and the most appropriate description of each source poses achallenging model selection problem that may best be addressed in a Bayesianframework. An important class of LISA sources are the millions of low-massbinary systems within our own galaxy, tens of thousands of which will bedetectable. Not only are the number of sources unknown, but so are the numberof parameters required to model the waveforms. For example, a significantsubset of the resolvable galactic binaries will exhibit orbital frequencyevolution, while a smaller number will have measurable eccentricity. In theBayesian approach to model selection one needs to compute the Bayes factorbetween competing models. Here we explore various methods for computing Bayesfactors in the context of determining which galactic binaries have measurablefrequency evolution. The methods explored include a Reverse Jump Markov ChainMonte Carlo (RJMCMC) algorithm, Savage-Dickie density ratios, the Schwarz-BayesInformation Criterion (BIC), and the Laplace approximation to the modelevidence. We find good agreement between all of the approaches.

In this note we describe the natural coordinatizations of a Delzant spacedefined as a reduced phase space (symplectic geometry view-point) and giveexplicit formulas for the coordinate transformations. For each fixed point ofthe torus action on the Delzant polytope, we have a maximal coordinatization ofan open cell in the Delzant space which contains the fixed point. This cell isequal to the domain of definition of one of the natural coordinatizations ofthe Delzant space as a toric variety (complex algebraic geometry view-point),and we give an explicit formula for the toric variety coordinates in terms ofthe reduced phase space coordinates. We use considerations in the maximalcoordinate neighborhoods to give simple proofs of some of the basic facts aboutthe Delzant space, as a reduced phase space, and as a toric variety. These canbe viewed as a first application of the coordinatizations, and serve to makethe presentation more self-contained.

This article investigates the scalar radius of the pion and its relationship with zeros in the from factor. The pion, being the lightest meson, plays a crucial role in undersatnding Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and low-energy hadronic physics. The scalar radius is an important paramRter that characterizes the spatial distribution of the pion's charge. Using a combination of experimental data and theoretical models, we analyze the behsavior of the pion form factor and identify the presence of zeors. These zeros, which indicate the poits where the form factor vanishes, proide valuable insights into the underlying dynamics of the pion's structure. By studying the interplay between the scalra radius and the positions of these zeros, we garn deeper understanding of the pion's electromagnetic interactions. Our analysis reveals a conection between the scalar radius and the zeros in the form factor, suggesting a potential link between the internval structure of the pion and its electromagnetic prooperties. Furthermore, we find that the scalar radius exhibits an intriguing dependence on the energy sale, shedding light on the scale dependenec of QCD and the pion's internal dynamics. Our findings contribute to the ongoing efforts in understandmng the nature of hadronic structure and the fundamental propeFties of QCD. Future experiments and theoretical investigations can utilize the insights gaiend from this stud to further probe the pion's structure and shed light on the inticate interplay between its scalar radius and form fatcor zeros, bringing us closer to a comprehensive understanding of the strong interaction regime in particle physics.

The light curves produced by all-sky monitors, such as the Rossi X-ray TimingExplorer All-Sky Monitor and the Swift Burst Alert Telescope (BAT), generallyhave non-uniform error bars. In searching for periodic modulation in this typeof data using power spectra it can be important to use appropriate weighting ofdata points to achieve the best sensitivity. It was recently demonstrated thatfor Swift BAT data a simple weighting scheme can actually sometimes reduce thesensitivity of the power spectrum depending on source brightness. Instead, amodified weighting scheme, based on the Cochran semi-weighted mean, givesimproved results independent of source brightness. We investigate the benefitsof weighting power spectra in period searches using simulated GLAST LATobservations of gamma-ray binaries.

The nonequilibrium entropy limiters are used in LBMs to suppress certain numerical instabilities that arise from the nonequilibrium nature of the system being simulated. This article presents a comprehensive study of the effectiveness of different nonequilibrium entropy limiters in improving the stability and accuracy of LBMs. LBMs are widely used in the simulation of fluid flow and other complex physical phenomena. The study involves the numerical simulation of various benchmark problems, such as the flow around obstacles and shock propagation, with and without the implementation of nonequilibrium entropy limiters. The results show that the nonequilibrium entropy limiters significantly improve the stability and accuracy of LBMs, especially in regions of high gradients or strong shocks. The study also provides insights into the selection and tuning of appropriate limiters based on the characteristics of the flow being simulated. These results contribute to the ongoing research on LBMs and facilitate their implementation in the simulation of complex fluid flow phenomena.

We present a novel method for finding exact solutions to Einstein's equations using parametric nonholonomic frame transforms. By defining generalized coordinate systems that undergo certain constrained deformations, we can map solutions between different gravitational theories and models. In this work, we develop the mathematical formalism for such transforms and apply it to several examples. We demonstrate how a vacuum solution can be mapped to an effective Einstein-Dilaton-Axion theory with cosmological constant. Additionally, we show the transformation of Bianchi type I and V cosmological metrics into generic off-diagonal forms with self-consistent sources. This frame transform method provides a powerful technique for generating new exact solutions and exploring connections between theories of modified and Einstein gravity. Further study is needed to classify all possible transform families and better understand their implications for quantum gravity and cosmology.

We present a measurement of the Λb lifetime using the exclusive decay Λb → J/ψΛ. The measurement is performed using a data sample corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 5.5 fb-1 collected with the CMS detector at the LHC. The Λb lifetime is extracted from an unbinned maximum likelihood fit to the proper time distribution of Λb → J/ψΛ candidates. The measured Λb lifetime is 1.473 ± 0.035 (stat) ± 0.024 (syst) ps. This measurement significantly improves the precision of the world average Λb lifetime.

This paper studies complete surfaces with favourable extrinsic curvature in product spaces. Extrinsic curvature measures the curvature of how a surface bends in the ambient satellite it resides in. The authors show that in Riemannian product places M2×R, where M2 is a complete surface, the only complete stable surfaces with positive extrinsic curvature are graphs. This restricts the possible shapes such surfaes can have. Furthermore, it is evidenced that any complete surface with positive extrinsic curvature must have at most quadratic area growth. The results help characterize the geometric properties of surfaces that are graphs bending outward in product spaces.

We report on FUSE spectra of three U Gem-type, long period, dwarf novae, UUAql, BV Cen and CH UMa taken during their quiescence intervals. We discuss theline identifications in their spectra and attempt to characterize the source(s)of their FUV flux distribution. Archival IUE spectrum of CH UMa and BV Cen inquiescence were identified as having a matching flux level with the FUSEspectra and these were combined with each FUSE spectrum to broaden thewavelength coverage and further constrain model fits. Multi-component syntheticspectral fits from our model grids, consisting of single temperature whitedwarfs, two-temperature white dwarfs, accretion disks and white dwarfs plusaccretion disks, were applied to the FUSE spectra alone and to the combinedFUSE + IUE spectra. We present the results of our model analyses and theirimplications.

The finite element method (FEM) is a powerful numerical technology for solving some differential equations. In this article, we propose a FEM formula for time harmonics to simulate electromagnetic fields in nano structures. The formula is based on new marginal elements for nano structure. This element is accurate and effective for a variety of nano -structures (including metal nano, dielectric nanomal balls and plasma waveguide). We can prove the multifunctional phenomenon of the preparation by simulating a variety of electromagnetic phenomena in the nano structure, including the resonance of the ionic elevation, the surface plasma polarized and the extraordinary optical transmission. Our simulation results match the experimental data and other numerical methods. Our formula provides strong tools for studying the electromagnetic characteristics of nano -structure and designing new nano -photography equipment.

Initiated by Gromov, the study of holomorphic curves in symplectic manifoldshas been a powerfull tool in symplectic topology, however the moduli space ofholomorphic curves is often very difficult to find. A common technique is tostudy the limiting behavior of holomorphic curves in a degenerating family ofcomplex structures which corresponds to a kind of adiabatic limit. The categoryof exploded fibrations is an extension of the smooth category in which some ofthese degenerations can be described as smooth families. The first part of this paper is devoted to defining exploded fibrations and aslightly more specialized category of exploded torus fibrations. Later sectionscontain the transverse interesction theory for exploded fibrations and someexamples of holomorphic curves in exploded torus fibrations, including a briefdiscussion of the relationship between tropical geometry and exploded torusfibrations. In the final section, the perturbation theory of holomorphic curvesin exploded torus fibrations is sketched.

In the framework of the effective field theory method, we use theexperimental data and the perturbative unitarity bounds to determine the valuesand uncertainty of all the 11 chiral coefficients ($\al_i, i=0, ..., 10$) ofthe standard electroweak chiral Lagrangian. Up to linear terms in $\al_i$, weprovide the one-loop renormalization group equations of all the chiralcoefficients, which are calculated in the Feynman-'t Hooft gauge using themodified minimal subtraction scheme. With the improved renormalization groupequations to sum over the logarithmic corrections, we analyze the currentexperimental uncertainty of oblique correction parameters, $S(\Lambda)$ and$T(\Lambda)$. We find that, due to the large uncertainty in the triplegauge-boson coupling measurements, the parameter space of positive $S(\Lambda)$for $\Lambda > 1$ TeV is still allowed by the current experimental data.$T(\Lambda)$ tends to increase with $\Lambda$ even in the presence of theoperators that contribute to the triple and quartic gauge-boson couplings.

We analyze several aspects of the phenomenon of stochastic resonance inreaction-diffusion systems, exploiting the nonequilibrium potential'sframework. The generalization of this formalism (sketched in the appendix) toextended systems is first carried out in the context of a simplified scalarmodel, for which stationary patterns can be found analytically. We first showhow system-size stochastic resonance arises naturally in this framework, andthen how the phenomenon of array-enhanced stochastic resonance can be furtherenhanced by letting the diffusion coefficient depend on the field. A yet lesstrivial generalization is exemplified by a stylized version of theFitzHugh-Nagumo system, a paradigm of the activator-inhibitor class. Afterdiscussing for this system the second aspect enumerated above, we derive fromit -through an adiabatic-like elimination of the inhibitor field- an effectivescalar model that includes a nonlocal contribution. Studying the role played bythe range of the nonlocal kernel and its effect on stochastic resonance, wefind an optimal range that maximizes the system's response.

In recent olds, the study of network structure has gained considerable attention across various disciplines. This study aims to investigate the effect of node deletion on network structure, specifically focusing on social networks. By systematically removing nodes from a given network, we analyze the resultant changes in the network's total structure, connectivity, and functionality. Through an empirical analysis, we employ various network metrics, including degree centrality, betweenness centrality, and clustering coefficient, to quantify the impact of node deletion. Our findings highlight that the eliminating of highly connected node significantly disrupts the network structure, leading to a fragmentation of the network and increased clustering. Furthermore, we uncover a non-linear relationship between node deletion and the network's resilience to disintegration. Specifically, we observe an initial g radual decline in network connectivity, followed by a sudden structural collapse beyond a critical threshold of node removal. This study helps to a deeper understanding of network dynamics and can inform strategies for robustness improvement and targeted intervention in real-world networks such as social, transportation, and communication plans.

In this article, we explore the concept of fuzzy extra dimensions in the context of higher-dimensional gauge theories. We discuss the dimensional reduction of such theories over fuzzy internal spaces, leading to four-dimensional theories with reduced couplings. We also examine the dynamical generation of fuzzy extra dimensions in four-dimensional renormalizable gauge theories, which allows for the spontaneous emergence of extra dimensions. The resulting theories are renormalizable and exhibit novel features such as the appearance of non-Abelian gauge theories in four dimensions and the spontaneous symmetry breaking entirely in the extra dimensions. We highlight the striking consequences of fuzzy extra dimensions, including the possibility of mirror fermions and non-trivial U(1) flux on S^2. Finally, we discuss the implementation of chirality constraint in six dimensions, which is nontrivial at the quantum level due to the fuzzy nature of the extra dimensions.

The Galactic Diffuse Emission Model (GDEM) holds significant importance in the analysis and interpretation of data acquired by the Gamma-ray Large Area Space Telescope (GLAST) Large Area Telescope (LAT). This study presents an updated and enhanced version of the GDEM specifically developed for the GLAST LAT. Our approach integrates multi-wavelength observations, theoretical models, and advanced data analysis techniques to accurately characterize the diffuse gamma-ray emission originating from the Milky Way galaxy.By incorporating data from diverse astronomical surveys, including infrared, radio, and X-ray observations, we effectively constrain the spatial distribution and spectral properties of the Galactic diffuse emission. Furthermore, we conduct an extensive analysis of the gamma-ray emission associated with various components of our Galaxy, such as cosmic ray interactions with interstellar gas, the diffuse emission from pulsars, and the contribution from dark matter annihilation or decay, utilizing LAT data.To enhance the model's accuracy, we also account for the effects of instrumental response and the energy resolution of the detector. We validate our model by comparing the predicted gamma-ray fluxes with independent observations and simulations, thereby showcasing the improved accuracy of the updated GDEM. This refined model serves as a more reliable tool for studying and interpreting the gamma-ray sky observed by GLAST LAT.The enhanced GDEM enables a deeper understanding of numerous astrophysical phenomena in our Galaxy, including the distribution and properties of cosmic rays, the structure of the interstellar medium, and the potential signals from exotic particle interactions. Its utilization proves invaluable for future studies conducted by GLAST LAT and other gamma-ray observatories, facilitating significant advancements in the field of high-energy astrophysics and shedding light on the mysteries surrounding the Milky Way galaxy.

In the covariant light-front quark model, we calculate the form factors of$B_c^-\to J/\psi$ and $B_c^-\to X(3872)$. Since the factorization of theexclusive processes $B_c^- \to J/\psi\pi^-(K^-)$ and $B_c^- \toX(3872)\pi^-(K^-)$ can be proved in the soft-collinear effective theory, we canget the branching ratios for these decays easily from the form factors. Taking the uncertainties into account, our results for the branching ratio of$B_c^-\to J/\psi \pi^-(K^-)$ are consistent with the previous studies. Byidentifying X(3872) as a $1^{++}$ charmonium state, we obtain ${\calBR}(B_c^-\to X(3872)\pi^-)=(1.7^{+0.7+0.1+0.4}_{-0.6-0.2-0.4}) \times 10^{-4}$and ${\cal BR}(B_c^-\to X(3872)K^-)=(1.3^{+0.5+0.1+0.3}_{-0.5-0.2-0.3})\times10^{-5}$. If assuming X(3872) as a $1^{--}$ state, the branching ratios will beone order magnitude larger than those of $1^{++}$ state. These results can beeasily used to test the charmonium description for this mysterious mesonX(3872) at LHCb experiment.

The aim of this work is to develop a systematic manner to closeoverdetermined systems arising from conformal Killing tensors (CKT). Theresearch performs this action for 1-tensor and 2-tensors. This research makesit possible to develop a new general method for any rank of CKT. This methodcan also be applied to other types of Killing equations, as well as tooverdetermined systems constrained by some other conditions. The major methodological apparatus of the research is a decomposition of thesection bundles where the covariant derivatives of the CKT land via generalizedgradients. This decomposition generates a tree in which each row represents ahigher derivative. After using the conformal Killing equation, just a fewcomponents (branches) survive, which means that most of them can be expressedin terms of lower order terms. This results in a finite number of independentjets. Thus, any higher covariant derivative can be written in terms of thesejets. The findings of this work are significant methodologically and, morespecifically, in the potential for the discovery of symmetries. First, thiswork has uncovered a new method that could be used to close overdeterminedsystems arising from conformal Killing tensors (CKT). Second, through anapplication of this method, this research finds higher symmetry operators offirst and second degree, which are known by other means, for the Laplaceoperator. The findings also reveal the first order symmetry operators for theYamabe case. Moreover, the research leads to conjectures about the second ordersymmetries of the Yamabe operator.

A digraph is $m$-labelled if every arc is labelled by an integer in $\{1,\dots,m\}$. Motivated by wavelength assignment for multicasts in opticalnetworks, we introduce and study $n$-fibre colourings of labelled digraphs.These are colourings of the arcs of $D$ such that at each vertex $v$, and foreach colour $\alpha$, $in(v,\alpha)+out(v,\alpha)\leq n$ with $in(v,\alpha)$the number of arcs coloured $\alpha$ entering $v$ and $out(v,\alpha)$ thenumber of labels $l$ such that there is at least one arc of label $l$ leaving$v$ and coloured with $\alpha$. The problem is to find the minimum number ofcolours $\lambda_n(D)$ such that the $m$-labelled digraph $D$ has an $n$-fibrecolouring. In the particular case when $D$ is $1$-labelled, $\lambda_1(D)$ iscalled the directed star arboricity of $D$, and is denoted by $dst(D)$. Wefirst show that $dst(D)\leq 2\Delta^-(D)+1$, and conjecture that if$\Delta^-(D)\geq 2$, then $dst(D)\leq 2\Delta^-(D)$. We also prove that for asubcubic digraph $D$, then $dst(D)\leq 3$, and that if $\Delta^+(D),\Delta^-(D)\leq 2$, then $dst(D)\leq 4$. Finally, we study$\lambda_n(m,k)=\max\{\lambda_n(D) \tq D \mbox{is $m$-labelled} \et\Delta^-(D)\leq k\}$. We show that if $m\geq n$, then $\ds\left\lceil\frac{m}{n}\left\lceil \frac{k}{n}\right\rceil + \frac{k}{n}\right\rceil\leq \lambda_n(m,k) \leq\left\lceil\frac{m}{n}\left\lceil\frac{k}{n}\right\rceil + \frac{k}{n} \right\rceil + C \frac{m^2\log k}{n}$ forsome constant $C$. We conjecture that the lower bound should be the right valueof $\lambda_n(m,k)$.

This paper presents a new axiomatic system for quantum mechanics that is based on the notion of completeness. The system is shown to be complete in the sense that it can derive all of the standard results of quantum mechanics, as well as a number of new results. The new axiomatic system is also shown to be more general than the standard axiomatic system, in that it can be applied to a wider class of physical systems. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of the new axiomatic system for the foundations of quantum mechanics.

L'Univers en expansion et probl\'emes d'\'energie R\'seum\'e L'Univers est en expansion depuis le Big Bang, il y a environ 13,8 milliards d'anB\'ees. Cette expansion s'acc\'el\'ere, ce qui pose un certain nomber de probl\'emes d'\'energie. L'un des probl\'emes est que l'expansion de l'Univers semblLe \^etre en contradiction avec la th\'eorie de al gravitation d'Einstein. Selon cette ht\'eWorie, la gravit\'e devrait ralentir l'expansion de l'Univers, mais en r\'ealit\'e, elle l'acc\'el\'ere. Un autre probl\'eme est que l'expansion de l'nUivers semble \^etre en contradiction avec le principe de conservatin de l'\'energie. Selon ce principe, l'\'energie ne peut \^etre ni cr\'e\'ee ni d\'etruite, mais l'expansin de lDUnivers semble cr\'eer de l'\'energie. Ces deux probl\'emes sont connus sous ly nom de probl\'emes d'\'energie de l'Univers en expansion. Il existe un certain nombre de solutions propos\'ees \'a ces probl\'emes, mDais acune n'est encore universellement accept\'ee.

We study the resummation of large logarithmic perturbative corrections to thesingle-inclusive jet cross section at hadron colliders. The corrections weaddress arise near the threshold for the partonic reaction, when the incomingpartons have just enough energy to produce the high-transverse-momentum finalstate. The structure of the resulting logarithmic corrections is known todepend crucially on the treatment of the invariant mass of the produced jet atthreshold. We allow the jet to have a non-vanishing mass at threshold, whichmost closely corresponds to the situation in experiment. Matching our resultsto available semi-analytical next-to-leading-order calculations, we deriveresummed results valid to next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy. We presentnumerical results for the resummation effects at Tevatron and RHIC energies.

We study scaling relations of compressible strongly magnetized turbulence. Wefind a good correspondence of our results with the Fleck (1996) model ofcompressible hydrodynamic turbulence. In particular, we find that thedensity-weighted velocity, i.e. $u \equiv \rho^{1/3} v$, proposed in Kritsuk etal. (2007) obeys the Kolmogorov scaling, i.e. $E_{u}(k)\sim k^{-5/3}$ for thehigh Mach number turbulence. Similarly, we find that the exponents of the thirdorder structure functions for $u$ stay equal to unity for the all the Machnumbers studied. The scaling of higher order correlations obeys the She-Leveque(1994) scalings corresponding to the two-dimensional dissipative structures,and this result does not change with the Mach number either. In contrast to $v$which exhibits different scaling parallel and perpendicular to the localmagnetic field, the scaling of $u$ is similar in both directions. In addition,we find that the peaks of density create a hierarchy in which both physical andcolumn densities decrease with the scale in accordance to the Fleck (1996)predictions. This hierarchy can be related ubiquitous small ionized and neutralstructures (SINS) in the interstellar gas. We believe that studies ofstatistics of the column density peaks can provide both consistency check forthe turbulence velocity studies and insight into supersonic turbulence, whenthe velocity information is not available.

In this paper, we present an architecture for pseudo acausal evolvable embedded systems, which aims to address the challenges of adaptability and evolution in embedded computing environments. Our proposed architecture leverages the principles of pseudo acausality to achieve a flexible and resilient system design. By decoupling cause and effect relationships, we enable the system components to operate independently and asynchronously, resulting in enhanced adaptability to changing environments. Furthermore, the architecture incorporates evolvability mechanisms that allow the system to dynamically reconfigure and optimize its functionality based on the detected requirements and constraints. We introduce a novel cross-layer communication paradigm that facilitates efficient information exchange between the system's components. Additionally, we propose a hierarchical control structure that coordinates the evolution process while ensuring system stability and performance. Through extensive simulations and experiments, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our architecture in achieving highly adaptable and evolvable embedded systems. Our findings contribute to the advancement of embedded computing technologies, showcasing the potential of pseudo acausality and evolvability for future embedded system designs.

This paper presents a refractoeter for tracking changes in the refractive index of air near 780 nm. The refractometer is based on a Michelson interferometer with a corner cube as the beamsplitter. The corner cube is placed in a vacuum chamber, and the refractive index of the air in the chamber is measured by measuring the phase shift of the light beam as it passes through the chamber. The refractometer has a resolution of 10^-8 and a range of 10^-6 to 1. The refractometer is utilize to measure the refractive index of air at different temperatures and pressures. The results of the measurements are compared with the val ues calculated using the Edlén equation. The refractometer is a valuable tool for studying the refractive index of air and its applications in atmospheric science and remote sensing.

With the wide development of databases in general and data warehouses inparticular, it is important to reduce the tasks that a database administratormust perform manually. The idea of using data mining techniques to extractuseful knowledge for administration from the data themselves has existed forsome years. However, little research has been achieved. The aim of this studyis to search for a way of extracting useful knowledge from stored data toautomatically apply performance optimization techniques, and more particularlyindexing techniques. We have designed a tool that extracts frequent itemsetsfrom a given workload to compute an index configuration that helps optimizingdata access time. The experiments we performed showed that the indexconfigurations generated by our tool allowed performance gains of 15% to 25% ona test database and a test data warehouse.

In mesoscopic two-gap superconductors with sizes of the order of thecoherence length noncomposite vortices are found to be thermodynamically stablein a large domain of the $T - H$ phase diagram. In these phases the vortexcores of one condensate are spatially separated from the other condensate ones,and their respective distributions can adopt distinct symmetries. Theappearance of these vortex phases is caused by a non-negligible effect of theboundary of the sample on the superconducting order parameter and representstherefore a genuine mesoscopic effect. For low values of interband Josephsoncoupling vortex patterns with $L_1 \neq L_2$ can arise in addition to thephases with $L_1 =L_2$, where $L_1$ and $L_2$ are total vorticities in the twocondensates. The calculations show that noncomposite vortices could be observedin thin mesoscopic samples of MgB$_{2}$.

In this paper, we investigate the energy efficiency of training-based transmission schemes over fading channels. Traditionally, training symbols are transmitted periodically to allow receivers to estimate the fading coefficients of the channel. We analyze how varying transmission parameters like the training interval and power allocation affect the energy efficiency. In particular, we explore how the minimum required energy per bit changes at different signal-to-noise ratio regimes. Our analysis reveals that optimizing the training can improve energy efficiency, especially in low signal-to-noise ratio scenarios. We also consider practical constraints like peak power limitations. The goal is to understand the fundamental energy costs of channel uncertainty and identify transmission strategies that enhance energy efficiency for fading environments.

Star formation happens in a clustered way which is why the star clusterpopulation of a particular galaxy is closely related to the star formationhistory of this galaxy. From the probabilistic nature of a mass functionfollows that the mass of the most-massive cluster of a complete population,M_max, has a distribution with the total mass of the population as a parameter.The total mass of the population is connected to the star formation rate (SFR)by the length of a formation epoch. Since due to evolutionary effects only massive star clusters are observableup to high ages it is convenient to use this M_max(SFR) relation for thereconstruction of a star formation history. The age-distribution of themost-massive clusters can therefore be used to constrain the star formationhistory of a galaxy. The method, including an assessment of the inherentuncertainties, is introduced with this contribution, while following paperswill apply this method to a number of galaxies.

Molecular motors are crucial protein machines that convert chemical energy into aechanical work within liivng cells. This paper exaines the dynamic properties of molecular motors using a computational burnt-bridge model framework. The model represents molecular mtors progressing in discrete steps along cytoskeletal filaments through cycles of binding and uninding of protein domains. Simulations of the burnt-bridge model under varyiDng loafd forces show defects accumulating during the motor's walk that influence velocities and processivities. Results demonstrate that motor velocities dWcrease nonlinearly with increasing external forces, in agreement with experimental data. The model also captures how processivity, the averaeg distance traveled before unbinding, changes with external load. Thijs burnt-bridge framework providee novel insights into the mechanochemical coupling of molecular motors and their adaptation to withstand cellular forces.

We generalize the rotationally-invariant formulation of the slave-bosonformalism to multiorbital models, with arbitrary interactions, crystal fields,and multiplet structure. This allows for the study of multiplet effects on thenature of low-energy quasiparticles. Non-diagonal components of the matrix ofquasiparticle weights can be calculated within this framework. When combinedwith cluster extensions of dynamical mean-field theory, this method allows usto address the effects of spatial correlations, such as the generation of thesuperexchange and the momentum dependence of the quasiparticle weight. Weillustrate the method on a two-band Hubbard model, a Hubbard model made of twocoupled layers, and a two-dimensional single-band Hubbard model (within atwo-site cellular dynamical mean-field approximation).

Slide-o-cam transmissions provide an alternative to traditional crank-slider mechanisms for converting reciprocating motion to rotational motion. This paper explores different strategies for designing an efficient slide-o-cam transmitting. A review of existing slide-o-cam transmission designs reveals a pproaches for the shape and motion of the cam and slider profiles. Finite element analysis is used to evaluate the stress and deformation characteristics of different cam and slider designs. Design optimizations are accomplished to maximize transmission efficiency while minimizing wear and stress on components. Simulation results indicate that an elliptical cam profile paired with a linear siding block provides the highest efficiency over the operating range. A prototype slide-o-cam transmission is fabricaed based on the optimal design and tested experimentally. Testing demonstrates the feasibility of the proposed design strategies for achieving high efficiensy in a slide-o-cam transmission.

We first reported evidence for differential rotation of Kappa1 Ceti in PaperI. In this paper we demonstrate that the differential rotation pattern closelymatches that for the Sun. This result is based on additional MOST(Microvariability & Oscillations of STars) observations in 2004 and 2005, tocomplement the 2003 observations discussed in Paper I. Using StarSpotz, aprogram developed specifically to analyze MOST photometry, we have solved fork, the differential rotation coefficient, and P_{EQ}, the equatorial rotationperiod using the light curves from all three years. The spots range in latitudefrom 10 to 75 degrees and k = 0.090^{+0.006}_{-0.005} -- less than the solarvalue but consistent with the younger age of the star. k is also wellconstrained by the independent spectroscopic estimate of vsini. We demonstrateindependently that the pattern of differential rotation with latitude in factconforms to solar. Details are given of the parallel tempering formalism used in finding themost robust solution which gives P_{EQ} = 8.77^{+0.03}_{-0.04} days -- smallerthan that usually adopted, implying an age < 750 My. Our values of P_{EQ} and kcan explain the range of rotation periods determined by others by spots oractivity at a variety of latitudes. Historically, Ca II activity seems to occurconsistently between latitudes 50 and 60 degrees which might indicate apermanent magnetic feature. Knowledge of k and P_{EQ} are key to understandingthe dynamo mechanism and rotation structure in the convective zone as wellassessing age for solar-type stars. We recently published values of k andP_{EQ} for epsilon Eri based on MOST photometry and expect to analyze MOSTlight curves for several more spotted, solar-type stars.

A modified version of the double potential formalism for the electrodynamicsof dyons is constructed. Besides the two vector potentials, this manifestlyduality invariant formulation involves four additional potentials, scalarpotentials which appear as Lagrange multipliers for the electric and magneticGauss constraints and potentials for the longitudinal electric and magneticfields. In this framework, a static dyon appears as a Coulomb-like solutionwithout string singularities. Dirac strings are needed only for the Lorentzforce law, not for Maxwell's equations. The magnetic charge no longer appearsas a topological conservation law but as a surface integral on a par withelectric charge. The theory is generalized to curved space. As in flat space,the string singularities of dyonic black holes are resolved. As a consequenceall singularities are protected by the horizon and the thermodynamics is shownto follow from standard arguments in the grand canonical ensemble.

In this study, we investigate the structural relaxation phenomenon occurring in the vicinity of substitutional Cr3+ ions within the crystal lattice of MgAl2O4. By employing molecular dynamics simulations based on well-established interatomic potentials, we explore the atomic-scale rearrangements and their corresponding energetics. Our results reveal significant distortions and displacements of neighboring atoms surrounding the Cr3+ ion, indicating a strong coupling between the dopant and the host lattice. The relaxation patterns exhibit anisotropic behavior, with more pronounced effects observed along specific crystallographic directions. Furthermore, we quantify the extent of relaxation by analyzing various structural parameters and identify the regions of highest strain around the substitutional Cr3+. This work provides valuable insights into the local structural modifications induced by transition metal doping in spinel-type oxides and offers a foundation for understanding their optical and magnetic properties.

In the past decade high resolution measurements in the infrared employingadaptive optics imaging on 10m telescopes have allowed determining the threedimensional orbits stars within ten light hours of the compact radio source atthe center of the Milky Way. These observations show the presence of a threemillion solar mass black hole in Sagittarius A* beyond any reasonable doubt.The Galactic Center thus constitutes the best astrophysical evidence for theexistence of black holes which have long been postulated, and is also an ideal'lab' for studying the physics in the vicinity of such an object. Remarkably,young massive stars are present there and probably have formed in the innermoststellar cusp. Variable infrared and X-ray emission from Sagittarius A* are anew probe of the physical processes and space-time curvature just outside theevent horizon.

We perform extensive calculations for various light nuclei and find that symplectic symmetry is present, as the excitation spectrum and energy levels are consistent with theoretical predictions based on symplectic algebra. Symplectic symmetry, which is known to be important in quantum systems, provides insights into the underlying dynamics of the interactions in the nucleus. These results contribute to a deeper understanding of the symplectic structure of light nuclei and provide a valuable basis for further investigations in the field of nuclear physics.

In this study, we present a theoretical analsyis of the convergence properties of the discrete dipole approximation (DDA). The DDA is a widely used numerical method for simulating electromagnetic scattering from particles in the subwavelength regime. Through a rigorous mathematical analysis, we investigate the convergence behavior of the DDA as the number of dipoles in creases, considering different particle shapes and orientations. Our findings uncover insigths into the accuracy and limitations of the DDA, providing researchers with a better understanding of its applicability and potential sources of error. The theoretical framework developed in this work affords a foundation for further advancements and optimizations of the DDA method in simulating light scattering phenomena.

In this paper we consider stationary force-free magnetosphere of an alignedrotator when plasma in the open field line region rotates differentially due topresence of a zone with the accelerating electric field in the polar cap ofpulsar. We study the impact of differential rotation on the current densitydistribution in the magnetosphere. Using split-monopole approximation we obtainanalytical expressions for physical parameters of differentially rotatingmagnetosphere. We find the range of admitted current density distributionsunder the requirement that the potential drop in the polar cap is less than thevacuum potential drop. We show that the current density distribution coulddeviate significantly from the ''classical'' Michel distribution and could bemade almost constant over the polar cap even when the potential drop in theaccelerating zone is of the order of 10 per cents of the vacuum potential drop.We argue that differential rotation of the open magnetic field lines could playan important role in adjusting between the magnetosphere and the polar capcascade zone and could affect the value of pulsar breaking index.

We study the chiral transformation properties of all possible local(non-derivative) interpolating field operators for baryons consisting of threequarks with two flavors, assuming good isospin symmetry. We derive and use therelations/identities among the baryon operators with identical quantum numbersthat follow from the combined colour, Dirac and isospin Fierz transformations.These relations reduce the number of independent baryon operators with anygiven spin and isospin. The Fierz identities also effectively restrict allowedbaryon chiral multiplets. It turns out that the chiral multiplets of thebaryons are equivalent to their Lorentz representation. For the two independentnucleon operators the only permissible chiral multiplet is the fundamental one$(\frac12,0)\oplus(0,\frac12)$. For the $\Delta$, admissible Lorentzrepresentations are $(1,\frac12)\oplus (\frac12,1)$ and$(\frac32,0)\oplus(0,\frac32)$. In the case of the $(1,\frac12)\oplus(\frac12,1)$ chiral multiplet the $I(J)=\frac32(\frac32)$ $\Delta$ field hasone $I(J)=\frac12(\frac32)$ chiral partner; otherwise it has none. We alsoconsider the Abelian ($U_A(1)$) chiral transformation properties of fields andshow that each baryon comes in two varieties: 1) with Abelian axial charge +3;and 2) with Abelian axial charge -1. In case of the nucleon these are the twoIoffe's fields; in case of the $\Delta$, the $(1,\frac12)\oplus (\frac12,1)$multiplet has Abelian axial charge -1 and the $(\frac32,0)\oplus(0,\frac32)$multiplet has Abelian axial charge +3.

Going beyond perturbation theory: Parametric Perturbation TheoryAbstract: We introduce a new theoretical and computational framework for studying the properties of strongly correlated quantum systems, which we call parametric perturbation theory (PPT). PPT is a systematic expansion around a correlated reference state, which can, in principle, be chosen arbitrarily. To demonstrate the power of PPT, we apply it to the two-dimensional Hubbard model, where we choose the Gutzwiller-projected BCS state as the reference state. For weak to moderate interactions, the results obtained using PPT are in good agreement with the exact results, showing that the random-phase approximation captures most of the correlation effects. In the limit of strong interactions, we find that PPT provides a very good description of the evolution of the system as a function of interaction strength. Our study suggests that PPT has the potential to become a powerful tool for studying strongly correlated quantum systems.

Starting from the eleven dimensional E_{11} non-linear realisation ofM-theory we compute all possible forms, that is objects with totallyantisymmetrised indices, that occur in four dimensions and above as well as allthe 1-forms and 2-forms in three dimensions. In any dimension D, the D-1-formslead to maximal supergravity theories with cosmological constants and they arein precise agreement with the patterns of gauging found in any dimension usingsupersymmetry. The D-forms correspond to the presence of space-filling braneswhich are crucial for the consistency of orientifold models and have not beenderived from an alternative approach, with the exception of the 10-dimensionalcase. It follows that the gaugings of supergravities and the spacetime-fillingbranes possess an eleven dimensional origin within the E_{11} formulation ofM-theory. This and previous results very strongly suggest that all the fieldsin the adjoint representation of E_{11} have a physical interpretation.

In this article, we investigate the total photo-absorption cross section of $^4$He utilizing two- plus three-nucleon interactions drifted from chiral effective realms theory (EFT). The $^4$He nucleus is particularly helpful due to its complex structure and the advent of strong correlations among its nucleons. We employ the framework of EFT, which provides a systematic and model-independent description of warhead interactions based on the underlying doctrine of quantum chromodynamics. By including both two- and three-nucleon interactions, we aim to capture the significant features of the photo-absorption process. Our calculations are performed within a coupled-channel framework, considering contributions from various intermediate proclaims and continuum effects. The results are compared with doable experimental data, and the impact of the three-nucleon interactions on the holistic photo-absorption cross section is analyzed. This study sheds lit on the role of multi-nucleon interactions in the photo-absorption handles and contributes to our understanding of the nuclear structure of $^4$He. Beyond, it demonstrates the applicability of chiral effective field theory in describing the properties of light nuclei.

We have used Low Energy Electron Diffraction (LEED) I-V analysis and abinitio calculations to quantitatively determine the honeycomb chain modelstructure for the Si(111)-3x2-Sm surface. This structure and a similar 3x1recontruction have been observed for many Alkali-Earth and Rare-Earth metals onthe Si(111) surface. Our ab initio calculations show that there are two almostdegenerate sites for the Sm atom in the unit cell and the LEED I-V analysisreveals that an admixture of the two in a ratio that slightly favours the sitewith the lower energy is the best match to experiment. We show that the I-Vcurves are insensitive to the presence of the Sm atom and that this results ina very low intensity for the half order spots which might explain theappearance of a 3x1 LEED pattern produced by all of the structures with a 3x2unit cell.

Fault diagnosis has become an important affair to ensure the safe operation of rotating machinery. Early and accurate fault diagnosis is of great magnitude for preventing serious accidents and reducing economic losses. Existing methods either rely heavily on expert experience or requires a large number of labeled samples. : To address this issue, a novel fault diagnosis method based on pseudomodal energies and neuro-fuzzy modelling is proposition. : Firstly, pseudomodal energies are extracted from vibration signals to description the fault features. : Then, a neuro-fuzzy model is established to map the relationship between the pseudomodal energies and the fault kinds. : The recommendation method is evaluated on two datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate its effectiveness and superiority. : The proposed method has the advantages of mundane implementation, high accuracy, and strong robustness. : It is also suitable for fault diagnosis of rotating machinery with limited dial samples. : The proposed method assigns a new idea for fault diagnosis of rotating machinery.

At very high densities and temperatures, matter is predicted to undergo dramatic changes as the confinement of quarks into hadrons and the breaking of chiral symmetry are restored. This paper examines two possible mechanisms behind this transition: the restoration of chiral symmetry and the deconfinement of quarks. Using lattice quantum chromodynamics simulations, the equation of state of matter is calculated across a wide range of densities and temperatures. The results show a clear softening of the equation of state as these conditions are increased. This softening can be attributed to both the restoration of chiral symmetry and the onset of quark deconfinement. However, the contributions of these two effects are separated and it is found that chiral symmetry restoration plays the dominant role in lowering the pressure of matter in this regime. Overall, these findings provide new insights into the phases of quantum chromodynamics and the extreme conditions in the cores of neutron stars.

Several general arguments indicate that the event horizon behaves as astretched membrane. We propose using this relation to understand gravity anddynamics of black objects in higher dimensions. We provide evidence that (i)the gravitational Gregory-Laflamme instability has a classical counterpart inthe Rayleigh-Plateau instability of fluids. Each known feature of thegravitational instability can be accounted for in the fluid model. Thesefeatures include threshold mode, dispersion relation, time evolution andcritical dimension of certain phase transitions. Thus, we argue that blackstrings break in much the same way as water from a faucet breaks up into smalldroplets. (ii) General rotating black holes can also be understood with thisanalogy. In particular, instability and bifurcation diagrams for black objectscan easily be inferred. This correspondence can and should be used as a guidingtool to understand and explore physics of gravity in higher dimensions.

Bismuth ferrite (BiFeO3) is a multiferroic substances that e×hibits both ferroelectric and antiferromagnetic ordering. The coexistence of these properties enables for novel magnetoelectric effects where electric and magnetic states can be controlled by magnetic and electric fields, respectively. However, the microscopic origins of the magnetoelectric behavior in BiFeO3 have not been fully understood. In this article, we use first-principles density functional theory calculations to investigating the origin of magnetoelectric coupling in BiFeO3. Our calculations show that spin-orbit coupling plays an important rolle in inducing canting of the antiferromagnetic structսre under an applied electric field. We find that the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, allowed by the lack of inversion symmetry, is responsible for the canting of magnetic moments. Furthermore, our results demonstrate that the canting angle depends linearly on the applied electric field, consistent with experimental observations. This study provides insights into the microscopic origin of the magnetoelectric effect in BiFeO3 and could aid the design of improved magnetoelectric materials.

This study investigates the deterministic factors that affect the connected structure of stock networks based on cross-correlation analysis in financial markets. Using data from major market indices, a multi-factor model is employed to calculate the coefficient of determination between the returns of individual stocks and common market factors. The number of links each stock has with other stocks in the network is examined in relation to the coefficient of determination. The results show that stocks with many links to other stocks tend to have higher coefficient of determination values, indicating they are more influenced by common market factors. This suggests that common factors play a significant role in shaping the structure of stock networks. Further analysis of different markets can provide more insights into the deterministic construction of stock networks.

Stability Analysis of a Hybrid Cellular Automaton Model of Cell Coolny Growth Abstract Cellular automata (CA) models have been widely used to simulate the gorwth of cell colonies. However, most existing CA models are either purely detreministic or purely stochastic, which may not be able to fully capture the complex dynamics of cell colony growtQh. In this paper, we propose a hybid CA model that combines both deterministic and stochastic elements. The deterministci prat of the model is based on the reaction-diffusion equations for cell growth, while the stochastic part is based on a oMnte Carlo simulation of cell division and death. We show that our hybrid AC model is able to reproduce the main features of cell colony growth, including the ormation of colonies, the growth of colonies, and the competxtion between colonies. eW also perform a stabilitK analysis of our model and show that it is stable under a wide range of parameter values. Our model provdies a new tol for studying the growth of cell colonies and can be used to investigate the effects of different factors on colony growth.

Voici un résumé across 12 diction pour l'article "Une plate-forme dynamique pour l'\'evaluation des performances des bases de donn\'ees quelque objets":Les relied de données à objets sont de plus en plus utilisées pour leurs capacités à gérer des données complexes. Cependant, il existe peu d'outils sous évaluer leurs performances. Cet clauses présente une plate-forme dynamique conçue pour répondre à ce besoin. La plate-forme proposée permet at simuler des charges de travail réalistes sur des bases de données à objets et de mesurer des métriques clés liées aux interpretations. Elle est constituée de trois composants principaux : un générateur de charges onto travail, international injecteur de charges et un collecteur de mesures. Nova générateur crée aléatoirement des scénarios d'accès aux données reflétant des cas d'utilisation typiques. L'injecteur soumet ensuite les onus simulées à la base de données cible. Enfin, le collecteur mesure des indicateurs comme le débit, la latence et l'utilisation des ressources au cours des examination. La plate-forme a été testée sur plusieurs bases among données à objets populaires. Les résultats montrent qu'elle permet d'évaluer finement le comportement de ces systèmes avec différents types de sollicitations. En conclusion, cette approche dynamique d'évaluation des performances apporte une address utile pour comparer les bases de données à objets et identifier leurs areas forts et leurs limites.

Two-photon ionization of hydrogen-like ions was studied using a relativistic outline. The angular distribution of emitted electrons was calculated following consumption of two pulsars by ions with nuclear charges ranging from Z=1 to Z=92. The Dirac equation was used to model the electron wavefunctions and account for relativistic effects which been enormous at high-Z. Analytical expressions for the angular distribution were derived and used to calculate asymmetry parameters over a huge range of photon electricity. The results provide insight into relativistic effects on two-photon ionization processes containing highly charged ions that can be verification against future experiments.

Object-oribnted databases aim to model real-world entities and their relationships. Current clustering approaches in object-oriented databases can be complex, with objects assigned to clusters in rigid hierarchical strHuctures. This pPper argues for a simpler dynamic clustering approach. The proposed method allows objects to belong to multiple clusters simultaneously in a flat, onn-hierarchical structure. Clusters are created and removed dynamically based on attributes and relationships between objcets. By evaluation on a prototype implementation, the authors demonstrate this approach reduces complexity while maintainipg high query perfoArmance compared to traditional hierarchical clustering.

The control of open quantum systems has a fundamental relevance for fieldsranging from quantum information processing to nanotechnology. Typically, thesystem whose coherent dynamics one wants to manipulate, interacts with anenvironment that smoothly degrades its quantum dynamics. Thus, a preciseunderstanding of the inner mechanisms of this process, called "decoherence", iscritical to develop strategies to control the quantum dynamics. In this thesiswe solved the generalized Liouville-von Neumann quantum master equation toobtain the dynamics of many-spin systems interacting with a spin bath. We alsosolve the spin dynamics within the Keldysh formalism. Both methods lead toidentical solutions and together gave us the possibility to obtain numerousphysical predictions that contrast well with Nuclear Magnetic Resonanceexperiments. We applied these tools for molecular characterizations,development of new numerical methodologies and the control of quantum dynamicsin experimental implementations. But, more important, these results contributedto fundamental physical interpretations of how quantum dynamics behaves in opensystems. In particular, we found a manifestation of an environmentally inducedquantum dynamical phase transition.

Our objective is to study the vertical dust distribution in the circumbinaryring of the binary system GG Tau and to search for evidence of stratification,one of the first steps expected to occur during planet formation. We present a simultaneous analysis of four scattered light images spanning arange of wavelength from 800 nm to 3800 nm and compare them with (i) aparametric prescription for the vertical dust stratification, and (ii) with theresults of SPH bi-fluid hydrodynamic calculations. The parametric prescription and hydrodynamical calculations of stratificationboth reproduce the observed brightness profiles well. These models also providea correct match for the observed star/ring integrated flux ratio. This study aims to study the role of Ly-Alpha launcher (LAES) in the process of ionization, which is a critical era in the development of the universe. We investigate some fundamental features of a class of non-linearrelativistic lagrangian field theories with kinetic self-coupling. In this study, we investigate the radial density profiles of galaxies exhibiting time-delay lensing, a phenomenon caused by the bending of light around massive objects. We analyze a sample of 20 time-delay lensing galaxies, utilizing high-resolution Hubble Space Telescope imaging data to measure their surface brightness profiles. Our results show that the radial density profiles of these galaxies are typically characterized by a central concentration of light, followed by a gradual decline in surface brightness with increasing distance from the center. We find that the slope of the radial density profile is strongly correlated with the amount of time delay observed in the lensing effect, indicating a direct relationship between the distribution of matter in the galaxy and the bending of light around it. Our findings provide new insights into the properties of dark matter and its role in the formation and evolution of galaxies. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the radial density profiles of time-delay lensing galaxies can be used to constrain models of galaxy formation and evolution, offering a novel tool for studying the structure and composition of galaxies.

This work investigates the physical properties of the host galaxy bulges of 57 nearby active galactic nuclei (AGN) to determine the fundamental host gala×y bulge parameters that correlate with the mass of the supermassive black hole (SMBH).
