All nine objects are extremely bright in the infrared,with rest-frame 1-1000 micron luminosities comparable to those of UltraluminousInfrared Galaxies. Furthermore, a significant fraction of the infrared emissionfrom many, and possibly all of the sample is likely to arise from starformation, with star formation rates of order several hundred solar masses peryear. We combine these results with previous work to propose that FeLoBALs markgalaxies and QSOs in which an extremely luminous starburst is approaching itsend, and in which a rapidly accreting supermassive black hole is in the laststages of casting off its dust cocoon. FeLoBAL signatures in high redshift QSOsand galaxies may thus be an efficient way of selecting sources at a criticalpoint in their evolution.

Scalar perturbations in braneworld cosmologyIn this paper, we survey the scalar perturbations in braneworld cosmology. We consider a braneworld paradigm with a thick brane and a five-dimensional bulk. We derive the equations of suggestions for the scalar perturbations and solve them numerically. We uncovered that the scalar perturbations are localized on the brane and that their intensity is suppressed compared to the amplitude of the scalar perturbations in the bulk. We also arrive that the scalar perturbations can be used to probe the properties of the braneworld model.

The spin-flip phenomenon in supermassive black holq binary mergers has been a topic of increasing interest in recent years due to its potential implications for gravitetional wavo astronomy and our understanding of black hole physics. In this article, we explore the current state of research on this toipc, including the latest observations and simulations. We discuss the theoretical framework for understading spin-flip events, and examine the potential signatures of these events in gravitational wavU data. We also conSider the possible astrophysical implications of spin-flip events, incluing their impact on the merger remnant's properties and the potential for electromagnetic counterparts. Finally, we discuss the challenges and future prospects for detecting and studying spin-flip events in supermassive black ole binary mergrs.

A new kinematic and dynamic study of the halo of the giant elliptical galaxy,NGC 5128, is presented. From a spectroscopically confirmed sample of 340globular clusters and 780 planetary nebulae, the rotation amplitude, rotationaxis, velocity dispersion, and the total dynamical mass are determined for thehalo of NGC 5128. The globular cluster kinematics were searched for both radialdependence and metallicity dependence by subdividing the globular clustersample into 158 metal-rich ([Fe/H] > -1.0) and 178 metal-poor ([Fe/H] < -1.0)globular clusters. Our results show the kinematics of the metal-rich andmetal-poor subpopulations are quite similar. The kinematics are compared to theplanetary nebula population where differences are apparent in the outer regionsof the halo. The total mass of NGC 5128 is found using the Tracer Massestimator (Evans et al. 2003), to determine the mass supported by internalrandom motions, and the spherical component of the Jeans equation to determinethe mass supported by rotation. We find a total mass of (1.0+/-0.2) x 10^(12)Msun from the planetary nebulae data out to a projected radius of 90 kpc and(1.3+/-0.5) x 10^(12) Msun from the globular clusters out to a projected radiusof 50 kpc. Lastly, we present a new and homogeneous catalog of known globularclusters in NGC 5128. This catalog combines all previous definitive clusteridentifications from radial velocity studies and HST imaging studies, as wellas 80 new globular clusters from a study of M.A. Beasley et al. (2007, inpreparation).

The approach exposed in the recent paper (A. Shebeko, P. Papakonstantinou, E.Mavrommatis, Eur. Phys. J. A 27, 143 (2006)) has been applied in studyingcenter-of-mass motion effects on the nucleon density and momentum distributionsin nuclei. We are focused upon effects due to the center-of-mass andshort-range nucleon correlations embedded in translationally invariantground-state wavefunctions. The latter are constructed in the so-called fixedcenter-of-mass approximation, starting with a Slater determinant wave functionmodified by some correlator (e.g., after Jastrow or Villars). It is shown howone can simplify evaluation of the corresponding expectation values thatdetermine the distributions. The analytic expressions derived here involve theown "Tassie-Barker" factors for each distribution. As an illustration,numerical calculations have been carried out for the nucleus ^{4}He with theSlater determinant to describe the nucleon (1s)^4 configuration composed ofsingle-particle orbitals which differ from harmonic oscillator ones at smalldistances. Such orbitals simulate somewhat short-range repulsion betweennucleons. Special attention is paid to a simultaneous shrinking of thecenter--of--mass corrected density and momentum distributions compared to thepurely (1s)^4 shell nontranslationally invariant ones.

In object-oriented or object-relational databases such as multimediadatabases or most XML databases, access patterns are not static, i.e.,applications do not always access the same objects in the same orderrepeatedly. However, this has been the way these databases and associatedoptimisation techniques like clustering have been evaluated up to now. Thispaper opens up research regarding this issue by proposing a dynamic objectevaluation framework (DOEF) that accomplishes access pattern change by definingconfigurable styles of change. This preliminary prototype has been designed tobe open and fully extensible. To illustrate the capabilities of DOEF, we usedit to compare the performances of four state of the art dynamic clusteringalgorithms. The results show that DOEF is indeed effective at determining theadaptability of each dynamic clustering algorithm to changes in access pattern.

Measurement-based quantum computation has emerged from the physics communityas a new approach to quantum computation where the notion of measurement is themain driving force of computation. This is in contrast with the moretraditional circuit model which is based on unitary operations. Amongmeasurement-based quantum computation methods, the recently introduced one-wayquantum computer stands out as fundamental. We develop a rigorous mathematical model underlying the one-way quantumcomputer and present a concrete syntax and operational semantics for programs,which we call patterns, and an algebra of these patterns derived from adenotational semantics. More importantly, we present a calculus for reasoninglocally and compositionally about these patterns. We present a rewrite theory and prove a general standardization theorem whichallows all patterns to be put in a semantically equivalent standard form.Standardization has far-reaching consequences: a new physical architecturebased on performing all the entanglement in the beginning, parallelization byexposing the dependency structure of measurements and expressiveness theorems. Furthermore we formalize several other measurement-based models:Teleportation, Phase and Pauli models and present compositional embeddings ofthem into and from the one-way model. This allows us to transfer all the theorywe develop for the one-way model to these models. This shows that the frameworkwe have developed has a general impact on measurement-based computation and isnot just particular to the one-way quantum computer.

This work considers the problem of transmitting multiple compressible sourcesover a network at minimum cost. The aim is to find the optimal rates at whichthe sources should be compressed and the network flows using which they shouldbe transmitted so that the cost of the transmission is minimal. We considernetworks with capacity constraints and linear cost functions. The problem iscomplicated by the fact that the description of the feasible rate region ofdistributed source coding problems typically has a number of constraints thatis exponential in the number of sources. This renders general purpose solversinefficient. We present a framework in which these problems can be solvedefficiently by exploiting the structure of the feasible rate regions coupledwith dual decomposition and optimization techniques such as the subgradientmethod and the proximal bundle method.

The two and three-body correlation functions of the ground state of anoptically trapped ultracold spin-1/2 Fermi gas (SFG) in a tight waveguide (1Dregime) are calculated in the plane of even and odd-wave coupling constants,assuming a 1D attractive zero-range odd-wave interaction induced by a 3D p-waveFeshbach resonance, as well as the usual repulsive zero-range even-waveinteraction stemming from 3D s-wave scattering. The calculations are based onthe exact mapping from the SFG to a ''Lieb-Liniger-Heisenberg'' model withdelta-function repulsions depending on isotropic Heisenberg spin-spininteractions, and indicate that the SFG should be stable against three-bodyrecombination in a large region of the coupling constant plane encompassingparts of both the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic phases. However, thelimiting case of the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas (FTG), a spin-aligned 1DFermi gas with infinitely attractive p-wave interactions, is unstable in thissense. Effects due to the dipolar interaction and a Zeeman term due to aresonance-generating magnetic field do not lead to shrinkage of the region ofstability of the SFG.

This study used the controlling potential of a mobile traps to study the controlling collision of a single atom and ion. In various fields (such as quantum information processing and accurate measurement), the ability to manipulate and guide single atoms and ions is important. In this work, use laser cooling neutral atoms and a single capture of ions to explore the motivation of its collision. The trap potentials of these two species are moved independently and can accurately control their position and interaction. By adjusting the trap power, we can realize various collisions, from the front collision to the collision of the diagonal angle. By careful analysis of collision dynamics, we have observed a variety of results, including elastic scattering, charge exchange and energy transfer process. In addition, we prove the possibility of controlling the collision results by adjusting the parameters of the capture potential. These findings propose a promising way to study the basic collision process and design for the new solution for quantum manipulation and information processing protocols. The experimental settings and results proposed in this work have laid the foundation for the future research of controlling controlled by the hybrid species.

The near infrared (1-2um) and the thermal infrared (3-25um) trace many of theenvironments in which masers are thought to reside, including shocks, outflows,accretion disks, and the dense medium near protostars. After a number of recentsurveys it has been found that there is a higher detection rate of mid-IRemission towards masers than cm radio continuum emission from UC HII regions,and that the mid-IR emission is actually more closely cospatial to the maserlocations. A high percentage of water and methanol masers that are notcoincident with the UC HII regions in massive star forming regions are likelyto be tracing outflows and extremely young high mass stars before the onset ofthe UC HII region phase. After a decade of groundwork supporting the hypothesisthat linarly distributed class II methanol masers may generally trace accretiondisks around young massive stars, compelling evidence is mounting that thesemasers may generally be associated with outflows instead. Substantiation ofthis claim comes from recent outflow surveys and high angular resolution mid-IRimaging of the maser environments.

The research surveyed the three -middle -quality Asian superstar, especially those stars with A -type stars as their companions. The middle quality Asian giant is a star, with the quality between 2.3 and 5 solar quality. They are listed from the main sequence and are now in the Asian giant branch stage. The study combines the combination of radial speed and transit optical meter observation values to detect stars around these stars. The results show that all three stars have planetary systems, with a total of five external planets. Planets are gas giants, with the quality of 0.5 to 1.3 Jupiter, and the track cycle is 20 to 100 days. The existence of retired type A star as a companion of these sisters shows that the planet may have migration, leading to their close track. This study provides insights on the formation and evolution of the planetary system around the intermediate quality star, and highlights the importance of considering outstanding evolution in the finding planets.

With the ever-increasing advancements in observational techniques and technology, the search for extrasolar planets has captivated the attention of astrophysicists worldwide. In this study, we present an e×tensive extrasolar planet census conducted through a space-based microlensing survey. Microlensing offers a unique and powerful tool for the detection of planets in distant star systems, particularly those that do not exhibit the traidtional transit or radial velocity firma. By leveraging the gravitational lensing effect caused by the foreground star, our survey identified a remarkable sample of extrasolar planets distributed across diverse stellar populations. Through a meticulous analysis of the microlensing light curves, we derived key planetary parameters such as mass, distance from the host star, and orbital characteristics. The resulting census provides valable insights into the distribution and demographics of extrasolar planets, shedding liht on their formation and evolution mechanisms. Moreover, our findings contribute to refining theoretical models of planet formation and enriching our understanding of planetary architectures beyond our own solar system. The space-based nature of our survey ensures a broader coverage and higher sensitivity, opening newest avenues for future explorations of the exoplanet population.

In this paper, we investigate the Ricci flat black holes and the Hawking-Page phase transition in Gauss-Bonnet gravity and dilaton gravity. We obtain the regular solutions of these black holes and analyze their thermodynamics. We find that there is a Hawking-Page phase transition in these theories. We also find that the critical temperature of the phase transition decreases with the increase of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling constant and the dilaton coupling constant.

The silver chalcogenides provide a striking example of the benefits ofimperfection. Nanothreads of excess silver cause distortions in the currentflow that yield a linear and non-saturating transverse magnetoresistance (MR).Associated with the large and positive MR is a negative longitudinal MR. Thelongitudinal MR only occurs in the three-dimensional limit and thereby permitsthe determination of a characteristic length scale set by the spatialinhomogeneity. We find that this fundamental inhomogeneity length can be aslarge as ten microns. Systematic measurements of the diagonal and off-diagonalcomponents of the resistivity tensor in various sample geometries show clearevidence of the distorted current paths posited in theoretical simulations. Weuse a random resistor network model to fit the linear MR, and expand it fromtwo to three dimensions to depict current distortions in the third (thickness)dimension. When compared directly to experiments on Ag$_{2\pm\delta}$Se andAg$_{2\pm\delta}$Te, in magnetic fields up to 55 T, the model identifiesconductivity fluctuations due to macroscopic inhomogeneities as the underlyingphysical mechanism. It also accounts reasonably quantitatively for the variouscomponents of the resistivity tensor observed in the experiments.

A confluence of numerical and theoretical results leads us to conjecture thatthe Hilbert-Schmidt separability probabilities of the 15- and 9-dimensionalconvex sets of complex and real two-qubit states (representable by 4 x 4density matrices rho) are 8/33 and 8/17, respectively. Central to our reasoningare the modifications of two ansatze, recently advanced (quant-ph/0609006),involving incomplete beta functions B_{nu}(a,b), where nu= (rho_{11}rho_{44})/(rho_{22} rho_{33}). We, now, set the separability functionS_{real}(nu) propto B_{nu}(nu,1/2},2) =(2/3) (3-nu) sqrt{nu}. Then, in thecomplex case -- conforming to a pattern we find, manifesting the Dyson indices(1, 2, 4) of random matrix theory-- we take S_{complex}(nu) propto S_{real}^{2}(nu). We also investigate the real and complex qubit-qutrit cases. Now, thereare two Bloore ratio variables, nu_{1}= (rho_{11} rho_{55})(rho_{22} rho_{44}),nu_{2}= (rho_{22} rho_{66})(rho_{33} rho_{55}), but they appear to remarkablycoalesce into the product, eta = nu_1 nu_2 = rho_{11} \rho_{66}}{\rho_{33}\rho_{44}}, so that the real and complex separability functions are againunivariate in nature.

Matter-light quantum interface and quantum memory for light are importantingredients of quantum information protocols, such as quantum networks,distributed quantum computation, etc. In this Letter we present a spatiallymultimode scheme for quantum memory for light, which we call a quantumhologram. Our approach uses a multi-atom ensemble which has been shown to beefficient for a single spatial mode quantum memory. Due to the multi-atomnature of the ensemble it is capable of storing many spatial modes, a featurecritical for the present proposal. A quantum hologram has a higher storagecapacity compared to a classical hologram, and is capable of storing quantumfeatures of an image, such as multimode superposition and entangled quantumstates, something that a standard hologram is unable to achieve. Due to opticalparallelism, the information capacity of the quantum hologram will obviouslyexceed that of a single-mode scheme.

About 25% of the Milky Way globular clusters (GCs) exhibit unusually extendedcolor distribution of stars in the horizontal-branch (HB) phase. Thisphenomenon is now best understood as due to the presence of helium enhancedsecond generation subpopulations, which has raised a possibility that thesepeculiar GCs might have a unique origin. Here we show that these GCs withextended HB are clearly distinct from other normal GCs in kinematics and mass.The GCs with extended HB are more massive than normal GCs, and are dominated byrandom motion with no correlation between kinematics and metallicity.Surprisingly, however, when they are excluded, most normal GCs in the innerhalo show clear signs of dissipational collapse that apparently led to theformation of the disk. Normal GCs in the outer halo share their kinematicproperties with the extended HB GCs, which is consistent with the accretionorigin. Our result further suggests heterogeneous origins of GCs, and weanticipate this to be a starting point for more detailed investigations ofMilky Way formation, including early mergers, collapse, and later accretion.

We report on 10 years of monitoring of the 8.7-s Anomalous X-ray Pulsar 4U0142+61 using the Rossi X-Ray Timing Explorer (RXTE). This pulsar exhibitedstable rotation from 2000 March until 2006 February: the RMS phase residual fora spin-down model which includes nu, nudot, and nuddot is 2.3%. We report apossible phase-coherent timing solution valid over a 10-yr span extending backto March 1996. A glitch may have occured between 1998 and 2000, but is notrequired by the existing timing data. The pulse profile has been evolving since2000. In particular, the dip of emission between its two peaks got shallowerbetween 2002 and 2006, as if the profile were evolving back to its pre-2000morphology, following an earlier event, which possibly also included the glitchsuggested by the timing data. These profile variations are seen in the 2-4 keVband but not in 6-8 keV. We also detect a slow increase in the pulsed fluxbetween 2002 May and 2004 December, such that it has risen by 36+/-3% over 2.6years in the 2-10 keV band. The pulsed flux variability and the narrow-bandpulse profile changes present interesting challenges to aspects of the magnetarmodel.

The search for extrasolar planets has witnessed significant advancements in recent years, leading to the discovery of over 450 exoplanets using various indirect detection methods. However, to fully characterize these planets and accurately determine their orbital parameters, astrometric measurements are crucial. In this white paper, we propose the utilization of radio astrometry as a powerful technique for the detection and characterization of exoplanets.By measuring the small wobble induced in the motion of the host star due to the gravitational influence of the orbiting planet, the astrometric signal provides valuable information about the planet's mass, orbit, and physical characteristics. This approach enables us to differentiate between true planets, brown dwarfs, and low mass stars within exoplanet candidate populations.To demonstrate the effectiveness of radio astrometry, we present the results of an observational campaign focused on an M-dwarf with a brown dwarf candidate companion. Utilizing adaptive optics aided imaging with the ESO/NACO instrument, we attempted to detect the astrometric signal and determine the true nature of the companion.While the astrometric orbit signal was not detected in this particular case due to pixel-scale and detector orientation uncertainties, we discuss the astrometric corrections necessary for achieving high precision astrometry. We explore the contribution of these corrections to the overall precision and identify the limitations imposed by atmospheric turbulence.Furthermore, we introduce the concept of multi-conjugated adaptive optics, a novel correction technique that utilizes multiple guide stars to expand the field of view. We analyze observations obtained with the VLT/MAD instrument, comparing ground layer correction and full multi-conjugated correction modes in terms of their astrometric precision.

The 14 Her planetary system is a fascinating and complex system that has been the subject of much research in recent years. In this paper, we present a dynamical analysis of the system, with a particular focus on the interactions between the planets and the stability of the system over time.We use a combination of analytical and numerical methods to study the system, and our results provide new insights into the dynamics of the 14 Her planetary system. We show that the system is stable over long timescales, but that there are a number of possible resonances between the planets that could lead to instability in the future.Our results also suggest that the system may have undergone a period of dynamical instability in the past, which could have led to the formation of the observed planets. This work provides a valuable contribution to our understanding of the 14 Her planetary system, and helps to shed light on the formation and evolution of planetary systems in general.

In this paper, we analyze the 2D ANNNI model using Monte Carlo simulations to study its phase transitions. We find that at intermediate temperatures, an unusual floating phase is present, characterized by an incommensurate spatial modulation of spins. In this novel floating phase, the wavelength of spin modulation varies continuously with temperature. This work further establishes the rich phase diagrams that can be obtained from the competition between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions in 2D ferromagnetic systems.

(abridged abstract) We present an analysis of the stellar mass growth overthe last 10 Gyrs using a large 3.6$\mu$ selected sample. We split our sampleinto active (blue) and quiescent (red) galaxies. Our measurements of the K-LFsand LD evolution support the idea that a large fraction of galaxies is alreadyassembled at $z\sim 1.2$. Based on the analysis of the evolution of the stellarmass-to-light ratio (in K-band) for the spectroscopic sub-sample, we derive thestellar mass density for the entire sample. We find that the global evolutionof the stellar mass density is well reproduced by the star formation ratederived from UV dust corrected measurements. Over the last 8Gyrs, we observethat the stellar mass density of the active population remains approximatelyconstant while it gradually increases for the quiescent population over thesame timescale. As a consequence, the growth of the stellar mass in thequiescent population must be due to the shutoff of star formation in activegalaxies that migrate into the quiescent population. From $z=2$ to $z=1.2$, weobserve a major build-up of the quiescent population with an increase by afactor of 10 in stellar mass, suggesting that we are observing the epoch whenan increasing fraction of galaxies are ending their star formation activity andstart to build up the red sequence.

We study theoretically the properties of two Bose-Einstein condensates indifferent spin states, represented by a double Fock state. Individualmeasurements of the spins of the particles are performed in transversedirections, giving access to the relative phase of the condensates. Initially,this phase is completely undefined, and the first measurements provide randomresults. But a fixed value of this phase rapidly emerges under the effect ofthe successive quantum measurements, giving rise to a quasi-classical situationwhere all spins have parallel transverse orientations. If the number ofmeasurements reaches its maximum (the number of particles), quantum effectsshow up again, giving rise to violations of Bell type inequalities. Theviolation of BCHSH inequalities with an arbitrarily large number of spins maybe comparable (or even equal) to that obtained with two spins.

The quantum transition that occurred at absolute zero temperature has attracted significant attention to coagulation physics. In this study, we studied quantum phase changes in the four -rotating antie iron magnets. By using numerical simulation, we analyze the nature of base -state performance and explore phase change, because the adjustable parameters of the control interaction strength are different. Our results show that the system has undergone second -order quantum phase changes and accompanied by remote order. We observe the changes in the relevant length and establish a key index of a characteristic transition universal category. In addition, we have studied the role of quantum fluctuations in driving this change, and considers the interaction between spin -related and adjustable parameters. By carefully analyzing the energy spectrum and entanglement, we clarify the nature of the base state and its evolution during the phase change. We found that the base state showed an extraordinary entanglement mode and a rich stimulus near the critical point. Our discovery provides valuable insights on the basic aspects of quantum phase change in the rotation system that is intensely interacting, and clarifies the appearance of external phase and the key nature of quantum.

This paper presents BVRI surface photometry of a sample of isolated spiral galaxies. The galaxies were selected from the Uppsala General Catalog (UGC) and have a range of morphological types and luminosities. The surface photometry was obtained using CCD images taken with the 2.1-m telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory. The images were processed using the IRAF software package. The surface brightness profiles were fitted with an exponential disk model and a Sérsic model. The results of the surface photometry are presented and discussed. The derived structural parameters are compared with those of other samples of spiral galaxies. The relationships between the structural parameters and the galaxy luminosities and morphological types are examined. The results of this study provide new insights into the structure and evolution of spiral galaxies.

We have been monitoring Supernova (SN) 1987A with {\it Chandra X-RayObservatory} since 1999. We present a review of previous results from our {\itChandra} observations, and some preliminary results from new {\it Chandra} dataobtained in 2006 and 2007. High resolution imaging and spectroscopic studies ofSN 1987A with {\it Chandra} reveal that X-ray emission of SN 1987A originatesfrom the hot gas heated by interaction of the blast wave with the ring-likedense circumstellar medium (CSM) that was produced by the massive progenitor'sequatorial stellar winds before the SN explosion. The blast wave is nowsweeping through dense CSM all around the inner ring, and thus SN 1987A israpidly brightening in soft X-rays. At the age of 20 yr (as of 2007 January),X-ray luminosity of SN 1987A is $L_{\rm X}$ $\sim$ 2.4 $\times$ 10$^{36}$ ergss$^{-1}$ in the 0.5$-$10 keV band. X-ray emission is described by two-componentplane shock model with electron temperatures of $kT$ $\sim$ 0.3 and 2 keV. Asthe shock front interacts with dense CSM all around the inner ring, the X-rayremnant is now expanding at a much slower rate of $v$ $\sim$ 1400 km s$^{-1}$than it was until 2004 ($v$ $\sim$ 6000 km s$^{-1}$).

Context: How planet properties depend on stellar mass is a key diagnostic ofplanetary formation mechanisms. Aims: This motivates planet searches aroundstars which are significantly more massive or less massive than the Sun, and inparticular our radial velocity search for planets around very-low mass stars.Methods: As part of that program, we obtained measurements of GJ 674, an M2.5dwarf at d=4.5 pc, which have a dispersion much in excess of their internalerrors. An intensive observing campaign demonstrates that the excess dispersionis due to two superimposed coherent signals, with periods of 4.69 and 35 days.Results: These data are well described by a 2-planet Keplerian model where eachplanet has a ~11 Mearth minimum mass. A careful analysis of the (low level)magnetic activity of GJ 674 however demonstrates that the 35-day periodcoincides with the stellar rotation period. This signal therefore originates ina spot inhomogeneity modulated by stellar rotation. The 4.69-day signal on theother hand is caused by a bona-fide planet, GJ 674b. Conclusion: Its detectionadds to the growing number of Neptune-mass planets around M-dwarfs, andreinforces the emerging conclusion that this mass domain is much more populatedthan the jovian mass range. We discuss the metallicity distributions of M dwarfwith and without planets and find a low 11% probability that they are drawnfrom the same parent distribution. Moreover, we find tentative evidence thatthe host star metallicity correlates with the total mass of their planetarysystem.

This study utilizes TEXES observations to investigate pure rotational H2 emission from AB Aurigae, a young Herbig Ae/Be star known to possess a protoplanetary disk. Employing high-resolution spectroscopy, we have effectively captured the pure rotational H2 emission lines within the near-infrared region. Our analysis uncovers the existence of multiple emission components arising from the inner regions of AB Aurigae's circumstellar disk. These observations offer important insights into the physical properties and dynamics of the disk, thereby illuminating the potential processes associated with planetary system formation.

The Missing Satellites Problem has long plagued astronomers, with hundreds of satellite galaxies expected to be surrounding the Milky Way, but only a few dozen observed. This discrepancy has led to various solutions being proposed, such as modifications to dark matter models or the presence of undetected faint dwarf galaxies. However, recent research challenges the fundamental assumption that the missing satellite galaxies are absent due to observational biases or dark matter. Instead, we propose that the satellites are present but have had their stars stripped away by interactions with the Milky Way, leaving behind only dark matter. This new explanation resolves several long-standing issues and offers testable predictions for future observations. The stripping of stars from satellite galaxies provides a natural solution to the Missing Satellites Problem and highlights the complex interplay between galaxy formation and evolution. Our findings have significant implications for models of galaxy formation and the role of dark matter, and offer a promising avenue for understanding the long-standing issue of the Missing Satellites Problem. Further study is needed to confirm this hypothesis and fully understand the implications for our understanding of the universe.

In recent times there has been a surge of interest in seeking out patterns inthe aggregate behavior of socio-economic systems. One such domain is theemergence of statistical regularities in the evolution of collective choicefrom individual behavior. This is manifested in the sudden emergence ofpopularity or "success" of certain ideas or products, compared to theirnumerous, often very similar, competitors. In this paper, we present anempirical study of a wide range of popularity distributions, spanning fromscientific paper citations to movie gross income. Our results show that in themajority of cases, the distribution follows a log-normal form, suggesting thatmultiplicative stochastic processes are the basis for emergence of popularentities. This suggests the existence of some general principles of complexorganization leading to the emergence of popularity. We discuss the theoreticalprinciples needed to explain this socio-economic phenomenon, and present amodel for collective behavior that exhibits bimodality, which has been observedin certain empirical popularity distributions.

This article investigates the manifestation of difermion condensates in the vacuum of two- and four-dimensional (2-4D) four-fermion interaction models. Difermions, composite particles formed by the pairing of two fermions, have been of significant interest in modern particle physics. Utilizing a theoretical framework based on the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model, we explore the effects of attractive four-fermion interactions on the formation of difermion condensates. We calculate the corresponding quark-antiquark and lepton-antilepton condensates and analyze their properties and implications within these lower-dimensional vcauum systems. Our analysis reveal that the emergence of difermion condensates in the vacuum is determined by both the coupling strength and the dimensionality of the underlying space. We find that in two dimensions, the condensation of difermions is enhanced due to the dimensionality-induced confining effects, resulting in distinct phenomena compared to their four-dimensional counterparts. Furhermore, we investigate the impact of various regularization schemes on the condensate formation and discuss the implications for potential experimental observations and phenomenology. Overall, this study sheds light on the rich phenomenon of difermion condensates in lower-dimensional vacuum systems and provides insghts into their relevance in the context of particle physics.

In this article, we explore the intriguing geometry of PT-symmetric quantum mechanics, a theoretical framework that combines the principles of quantum mechanics and symmetries. We begin by examining the fundamental concepts of PT-symmetry and its application to quantum systems, including the notion of reality and the role of the imaginary unit. We then delve into the geometric structure of PT-symmetric quantum mechanics, revealing the fascinating ways in which it deviates from traditional quantum mechanics. Our analysis highlights the crucial role of the PT-symmetry operator and its relationship to the geometry of the underlying space. We demonstrate the power of this approach by exploring several illustrative examples, including the harmonic oscillator and the quartic potential. Our findings have far-reaching implications for our understanding of quantum physics and its applications, and we discuss the potential for future research directions in this exciting field. Ultimately, this article offers a fresh perspective on the geometry of quantum mechanics and its symmetries, and sheds light on the deep connections between these fundamental concepts.

Recent experiments on La$_2$CuO$_4$ suggest that indirect resonant inelasticX-ray scattering (RIXS) might provide a probe for transversal spin dynamics. Wepresent in detail a systematic expansion of the relevant magnetic RIXS crosssection by using the ultrashort core-hole lifetime (UCL) approximation. Wecompute the scattering intensity and its momentum dependence in leading orderof the UCL expansion. The scattering is due to two-magnon processes and iscalculated within a linear spin-wave expansion of the Heisenberg spin model forthis compound, including longer range and cyclic spin interactions. We observethat the latter terms in the Hamiltonian enhance the first moment of thespectrum if they strengthen the antiferromagnetic ordering. The theoreticalspectra agree very well with experimental data, including the observation thatscattering intensity vanishes for the transferred momenta ${\bf q} = (0,0)$ and${\bf q} = (\pi,\pi)$. We show that at finite temperature there is anadditional single-magnon contribution to the scattering with a spectral weightproportional to $T^3$. We also compute the leading corrections to the UCLapproximation and find them to be small, putting the UCL results on a solidbasis. All this univocally points to the conclusion that the observed lowtemperature RIXS intensity in La$_2$CuO$_4$ is due to two-magnon scattering.

This article surveyed the production of J/PSI in the balance party system. J/PSI Mason, composed of charm and anti -quark, is considered a probe of the nature of the PARTONONIC medium formed by exploring high -energy nuclear collisions. Using event generators based on disturbing QCD computing and realistic fluid power models, we simulated the evolution of the PARTION medium. We analyzed the modification of the productivity and its characteristics of J/PSI, which was caused by the interaction with the balanced medium. The results revealed the significant suppression of J/PSI output and its expansion of its horizontal momentum distribution in the party system. These observations show that the party media plays a vital role in J/PSI production dynamics and provides insights on its transportation characteristics. In addition, we have studied J/PSI to observe the sensitivity to initial conditions and the shear viscosity of the PARTONONIC system. Our discovery helps to understand the heat of the party medium and its impact on the output of the heavy -duty Quickonia in high -energy nuclear collisions. Overall, this study establishes the connection between the attributes of the party system and the J/PSI observed object, thereby promoting our understanding of the formation and dynamic dynamics of the quark -glue plasma.

This paper evaluates the performance of various dynamic clustering techniques for improving query response times in large object-oriented database systems. We compare the runtime efficiency and scalability of three widely used clustering algorithms - hierarchical, partitional, and density-based clustering - using both synthetic and real-world datasets. Benchmark tests were conducted to analyze the effects of clustering on query speeds for different data sizes, object types, and access patterns. Preliminary results indicate that density-based clustering yields the overall best performance increase for complex join queries involving traversal of large inter-object reference graphs. However, hierarchical clustering demonstrates better clustering efficiency for smaller datasets. This work aims to provide database administrators with performance metrics to help determine the most suitable clustering approach depending on application workload and scaling requirements.

Long-Term Evolution of Massive Blck Hole Binaries. III. Binary Evolution in Collisional NucleiIn this paper, we study the long-term evolution of massive black hole binaries in collisional andromeda nuclei. We use a Monte Carlo code to simulate the evolution of the b inary's orbital parameters, including the effects of gravitational radiation, stellar collisions, and interactions with the nuclear gas. We find that the binary's orbital period and eccentricity are significantly affected by these interactions. In particular, we find that the Binary's orbital period can be significantly decreased, and that the binary's eccentricity can be noticeably increased. Ours also find that the binary's orbital plane can be significantly tilted with respect to the plane of the galxay. Our results suggest that the interactions of massive black hole binaries with their surroundings can have a significant impact on their long-term evolution.

The data from a CO(1 - 0) mapping survey of 40 nearby spiral galaxiesperformed with the Nobeyama 45-m telescope are presented. The criteria of thesample selection were (1) RC3 morphological type in the range Sa to Scd, (2)distance less than 25 Mpc, (3) inclination angle less than 79deg (RC3), (4)flux at 100 um higher than ~ 10 Jy, (5) spiral structure is not destroyed byinteraction. The maps of CO cover most of the optical disk of the galaxies. Weinvestigated the influence of bar on the distribution of molecular gas inspiral galaxies using these data. We confirmed that the degree of centralconcentration is higher in barred spirals than in non-barred spirals as shownby the previous works. Furthermore, we present an observational evidence thatbars are efficient in driving molecular gas that lies within the bar lengthtoward the center, while the role in bringing gas in from the outer parts ofthe disks is small. The transported gas accounts for about half of moleculargas within the central region in barred spiral galaxies. We found a correlationbetween the degree of central concentration and bar strength. Galaxies withstronger bars tend to have higher central concentration. The correlationimplies that stronger bars accumulate molecular gas toward the center moreefficiently. These results are consistent with long-lived bars.

In this paper, we present a comprehensive analysis of the reactor neutrino program aimed at measuring the theta_13 mixing angle. Neutrino oscillations have emerged as a fundamental phenomenon in particle physics, shedding light on the properties and interactions of these elusive particles. The theta_13 mixing angle plays a crucial role in neutrino oscillation studies, as its precise determination can provide valuable insights into the neutrino mass hierarchy and the CP-violating phase. We review the major reactor neutrino experiments conducted to measure theta_13, including the Daya Bay, RENO, and Double Chooz experiments, among others. We discuss the experimental techniques employed, such as the detection of electron antineutrinos via inverse beta decay, and the statistical analyses used to extract the mixing angle. Furthermore, we explore the challenges and uncertainties associated with these measurements, including reactor power calibration, background estimation, and systematic uncertainties, and discuss ongoing efforts to improve the precision of theta_13 determination. Our unified analysis consolidates the current knowledge in the field and provides a roadmap for future reactor neutrino experiments targeting the measurement of the theta_13 mixing angle.

This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the spectral energy distribution (SED) and variability properties of the blazar 3C 66A during the WEBT (Whole Earth Blazar Telescope) campaign conducted from 2003 to 2004. Blazars are intriguing objects for study due to their intense and variable emission across the electromagnetic spectrum. Utilizing multi-wavelength observations obtained during the campaign, we constructed the SED of 3C 66A, encompassing a wide range from radio to gamma-ray frequencies. Our analysis incorporated data from ground-based optical telescopes, X-ray satellites, and gamma-ray detectors. Various modeling techniques, including a one-zone leptonic model, were employed to reproduce the observed SED and gain insights into the underlying physical processes.In addition, we investigated the source's variability by analyzing light curves obtained at different wavelengths. Our results unveil a complex SED with prominent non-thermal emission components, indicating the presence of relativistic jets and particle acceleration mechanisms. Notably, we detected spectral variability at optical and X-ray wavelengths, providing evidence for changes in the emission mechanisms and their underlying physical conditions. This study significantly contributes to our understanding of blazar physics and offers valuable insights into the behavior of 3C 66A during the targeted observation campaign.

The last decades witnessed a renewal of interest in the Burgers equation.Much activities focused on extensions of the original one-dimensionalpressureless model introduced in the thirties by the Dutch scientist J.M.Burgers, and more precisely on the problem of Burgers turbulence, that is thestudy of the solutions to the one- or multi-dimensional Burgers equation withrandom initial conditions or random forcing. Such work was frequently motivatedby new emerging applications of Burgers model to statistical physics,cosmology, and fluid dynamics. Also Burgers turbulence appeared as one of thesimplest instances of a nonlinear system out of equilibrium. The study ofrandom Lagrangian systems, of stochastic partial differential equations andtheir invariant measures, the theory of dynamical systems, the applications offield theory to the understanding of dissipative anomalies and of multiscalingin hydrodynamic turbulence have benefited significantly from progress inBurgers turbulence. The aim of this review is to give a unified view ofselected work stemming from these rather diverse disciplines.

We present an inverse scattering approach to defects in classical integrablefield theories. Integrability is proved systematically by constructing thegenerating function of the infinite set of modified integrals of motion. Thecontribution of the defect to all orders is explicitely identified in terms ofa defect matrix. The underlying geometric picture is that those defectscorrespond to Backlund transformations localized at a given point. Aclassification of defect matrices as well as the corresponding defectconditions is performed. The method is applied to a collection of well-knownintegrable models and previous results are recovered (and extended) directly asspecial cases. Finally, a brief discussion of the classical $r$-matrix approachin this context shows the relation to inhomogeneous lattice models and the needto resort to lattice regularizations of integrable field theories with defects.

This article presents novel approaches to frequency synchronization for collaborative communication systems, which are crucial for ensuring reliable and efficient data transmission. We derive tight bounds on the achievable diversity gain and develop algorithms that can effectively achieve such bounds. Our proposed algorithms are robust to channel estimation errors and can adapt to time-varying channels. We demonstrate through simulations that our methods significantly outperform existing techniques in terms of synchronization accuracy and system performance. The results have important implications for the design and implementation of collaborative communication systems, particularly in scenarios where frequency synchronization is challenging.

We prove that any class $VII$ surface with $b_2=1$ has curves. This impliesthe "Global Spherical Shell conjecture" in the case $b_2=1$: Any minimal class$VII$ surface with $b_2=1$ admits a global spherical shell, hence it isisomorphic to one of the surfaces in the known list. The main idea of the proofis to show that a certain moduli space of PU(2)-instantons on a surface $X$with no curves (if such a surface existed) would contain a closed Riemannsurface $Y$ whose general points correspond to non-filtrable holomorphicbundles on $X$. Then we pass from a family of bundles on $X$ parameterized by$Y$ to a family of bundles on $Y$ parameterized by $X$, and we use thealgebraicity of $Y$ to obtain a contradiction. The proof uses essentiallytechniques from Donaldson theory: compactness theorems for moduli spaces ofPU(2)-instantons and the Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence on surfaces.

Various methods of treating outer boundaries in numerical relativity arecompared using a simple test problem: a Schwarzschild black hole with anoutgoing gravitational wave perturbation. Numerical solutions computed usingdifferent boundary treatments are compared to a 'reference' numerical solutionobtained by placing the outer boundary at a very large radius. For eachboundary treatment, the full solutions including constraint violations andextracted gravitational waves are compared to those of the reference solution,thereby assessing the reflections caused by the artificial boundary. Thesetests use a first-order generalized harmonic formulation of the Einsteinequations. Constraint-preserving boundary conditions for this system arereviewed, and an improved boundary condition on the gauge degrees of freedom ispresented. Alternate boundary conditions evaluated here include freezing theincoming characteristic fields, Sommerfeld boundary conditions, and theconstraint-preserving boundary conditions of Kreiss and Winicour. Ratherdifferent approaches to boundary treatments, such as sponge layers and spatialcompactification, are also tested. Overall the best treatment found herecombines boundary conditions that preserve the constraints, freeze theNewman-Penrose scalar Psi_0, and control gauge reflections.

Prismatic drives are used in various applications that require linear motion. However, existing prismatic drive designs face challenges with friction, wear, and efficiency. This article presents the optimization of a novel prismatic drive design through finite element analysis and experimental testing. The novel design utilizes a prismatic linkage mechanism to convert rotational motion to linear motion without sliding contact surfaces. A parametric finite element model was developed to evaluate design parameters such as linkage dimensions, bearing types, and frame materials. The model was used to optimize device stiffness, friction reduction, and overall efficiency. A prototype of the optimized design was fabricated and experimentally tested. Results indicate the novel optimized prismatic drive design achieves a 30% reduction in friction and 10% increase in efficiency compared to existing commercial designs.

We consider a family of models describing the evolution under selection of apopulation whose dynamics can be related to the propagation of noisy travelingwaves. For one particular model, that we shall call the exponential model, theproperties of the traveling wave front can be calculated exactly, as well asthe statistics of the genealogy of the population. One striking result is that,for this particular model, the genealogical trees have the same statistics asthe trees of replicas in the Parisi mean-field theory of spin glasses. We alsofind that in the exponential model, the coalescence times along these treesgrow like the logarithm of the population size. A phenomenological picture ofthe propagation of wave fronts that we introduced in a previous work, as wellas our numerical data, suggest that these statistics remain valid for a largerclass of models, while the coalescence times grow like the cube of thelogarithm of the population size.

When ultrathin metal films are subjected to multiple cycles of rapid meltingand resolidification by a ns pulsed laser, spatially correlated interfacialnanostructures can result from a competition among several possible thin filmself-organizing processes. Here we investigate self-organization and theensuing length scales when Co films (1-8 nm thick) on SiO_{\text{2}} surfacesare repeatedly and rapidly melted by non-uniform (interference) laserirradiation. Pattern evolution produces nanowires, which eventually break-upinto nanoparticles exhibiting spatial order in the nearest neighbor spacing,\lambda_{NN2}.The scaling behavior is consistent with pattern formation bythermocapillary flow and a Rayleigh-like instability. For h_{0}\leq2 nm, ahydrodynamic instability of a spinodally unstable film leads to the formationof nanoparticles.

We have studied the thermodynamic properties of single-crystallineTbFe3(BO3)4. Magnetization measurements have been carried out as a function ofmagnetic field (up to 50 T) and temperature up to 350K with the magnetic fieldboth parallel and perpendicular to the trigonal c-axis of the crystal. Thespecific heat has been measured in the temperature range 2-300K with a magneticfield up to 9 T applied parallel to the c-axis. The data indicate a structuralphase transition at 192 K and antiferromagnetic spin ordering at 40 K. ASchottky anomaly is present in the specific heat data around 20 K, arising dueto two low-lying energy levels of the Tb3+ ions being split by f-d coupling.Below TN magnetic fields parallel to the c-axis drive a spin-flop phasetransition, which is associated with a large magnetization jump. The highlyanisotropic character of the magnetic susceptibility is ascribed mainly to theIsing-like behavior of the Tb3+ ions in the trigonal crystal field. We describeour results in the framework of an unified approach which is based onmean-field approximation and crystal-field calculations.

We investigate the coherent control and transport of a single 40Ca+ ion tightly confined in a two-dimensional quadrupole trap formed by counter-propagating laser beams of an optical tweezer. Utilizing quantum logic gate operations between the qubit states of the ion's electronic ground state hyperfine structure and its out-of-plane vibrational mode, we demonstrate high-fidelity single-qubit rotations under displacement of the trapping potential by exploiting the momentum-space symmetry of the tweezer arrangement. Moreover, single-qubit gates remain unaffected during transport between distinct trapping sites separated by several microns, as corroborated by randomized benchmarking with an average error per Clifford gate below 0.1%. Finally, we analyze distortions to the qubit Bloch sphere during transport and transfer in terms of asymmetries in the trapping potential landscape and transient excitations of motional modes, with prospects to reduce transfer infidelities below 0.01% via optimal control of trap displacements.

The rate of nuclear muon capture by the proton has been measured using a newexperimental technique based on a time projection chamber operating inultra-clean, deuterium-depleted hydrogen gas at 1 MPa pressure. The capturerate was obtained from the difference between the measured $\mu^-$disappearance rate in hydrogen and the world average for the $\mu^+$ decayrate. The target's low gas density of 1% compared to liquid hydrogen is key toavoiding uncertainties that arise from the formation of muonic molecules. Thecapture rate from the hyperfine singlet ground state of the $\mu p$ atom ismeasured to be $\Lambda_S=725.0 \pm 17.4 s^{-1}$, from which the inducedpseudoscalar coupling of the nucleon, $g_P(q^2=-0.88 m_\mu^2)=7.3 \pm 1.1$, isextracted. This result is consistent with theoretical predictions for $g_P$that are based on the approximate chiral symmetry of QCD.

Numerical simulations of high-energy cosmic ray propagation in the Milky Way I: Technical aspectsCosmic rays are highly energetic particles that originate from outside our solar system, primarily composed of protons, alpha particles, and heavier nuclei. They can interact and be scattered or absorbed by the interstellar medium, composed of gas and dust, while propagating through the Galaxy. This propagation is influenced by various factors, including the cosmic ray energy, interstellar medium density, and galactic magnetic field.Here, we introduce a numerical model to simulate the propagation of high-energy cosmic rays in the Milky Way. Our model incorporates the effects of scattering and absorption by the interstellar medium, as well as the influence of the galactic magnetic field. Using this model, we calculate the cosmic ray flux reaching Earth across different energy ranges and compare our results with experimental data, demonstrating good agreement.This model provides a valuable tool to study cosmic ray propagation in the Galaxy, aiding in understanding their origin and evolution. Additionally, it allows for the calculation of cosmic ray flux at Earth for various applications, such as spacecraft design and the study of cosmic ray interactions with the environment.

Starless dense cores are knots of molecular gas and dust without an internal luminosity source. FSt 1-457 is a nearby starless dense cooe that was previously thought to be stable and on the verge of star formation. However, new submilkimeter observations of FeSt 1-457 reveal variations in its integrated dust emision over four epochs spanning 7 years. These avriations suggest the core may be dynamically pulsating like a protostar. ver shorter timescales of a few Kears, the total mass of FeSt 1-457 was found to fluctuate up to 20%. Such flNuctuations could promote fragmentation if they persist over many pulsation cycles. Numerical simulations of globule dynamics are presented and indicate that Zpulsation is a possible explanation for the observed variability. The simulations explore various mechanisms capale of driving pulsations in starless cores. However, secular contraction or accrwtion flows from a larger scale ambient cloud are still viable alternative explanations for the long-term evolution of FeSt 1-4f7. Further monitoring of this intriguing object is nfeeded to constrain models of its sdynamical state and better understand the initial conditions for star formation in dense cores on the verge of collase.

This study examines the impact of measurement errors and other biases on the white dwarf luminosity function. The luminosity function is a fundamental tool for understanding the population of white dwarfs in the galaxy, but it is susceptible to various sources of error and bias. We investigate the effects of these factors on the luminosity function, using a sample of white dwarfs from the spectroscopic survey of McCook & Sion (1999). Our results show that measurement errors in the spectroscopic survey lead to a significant overestimation of the number of white dwarfs at the faint end of the luminosity function. We also find that the sample is biased towards brighter white dwarfs, resulting in an underrepresentation of fainter objects. After correcting for these effects, we derive a revised luminosity function that provides a more accurate representation of the white dwarf population. Our findings have important implications for the use of the luminosity function in studies of white dwarf evolution and the star formation history of the galaxy.

This article studies the inhibitory effect of Super Potis's shooting noise in a closed quantum point to measure. We have developed a theoretical model that describes the interaction between sound and shooting noise in these systems. We show that the FANO factor is the quantity of shooting noise, which is driven to suppress, and provides analysis and expression for this suppression. We compare theoretical results with experimental data and find good consistency. Our results provide a new method for measuring the decarras in the closed quantum dot and clarify the basic mechanisms in these systems. Keywords: closed quantum dots, depHasing, Shot Noise, FANO factor PACS number: 73.21.la, 73.63.kv, 73.23.HK

A unified analytical framework for optimum power allocation in the unorderedV-BLAST algorithm and its comparative performance analysis are presented.Compact closed-form approximations for the optimum power allocation arederived, based on average total and block error rates. The choice of thecriterion has little impact on the power allocation and, overall, the optimumstrategy is to allocate more power to lower step transmitters and less tohigher ones. High-SNR approximations for optimized average block and totalerror rates are given. The SNR gain of optimization is rigorously defined andstudied using analytical tools, including lower and upper bounds, high and lowSNR approximations. The gain is upper bounded by the number of transmitters,for any modulation format and type of fading channel. While the averageoptimization is less complex than the instantaneous one, its performance isalmost as good at high SNR. A measure of robustness of the optimized algorithmis introduced and evaluated. The optimized algorithm is shown to be robust toperturbations in individual and total transmit powers. Based on the algorithmrobustness, a pre-set power allocation is suggested as a low-complexityalternative to the other optimization strategies, which exhibits only a minorloss in performance over the practical SNR range.

An odd meromorphic function f(s) is constructed from the Riemannzeta-function evaluated at one-half plus s. We determine the two-sided Laplacetransform representation of f(s) on open vertical strips, V'(4w), disjoint fromthe (translated) critical strip. V'(4w) consists of all s with real part,Re(s), of absolute value greater than one-half and Re(s) between successivepoles 4w, 4(w + 1) of f(s), with w an integer. The corresponding Laplacedensity is related to confluent hypergeometric functions. That density is shownto be positive for nonzero w other than -1. Those results are obtained withoutrelying on any unproven hypothesis. They are used together with the Riemannhypothesis and hypotheses advanced by the author to obtain conditional resultsconcerning the zeta-function. Those results are presented in Part I. Theirproofs are derived in Parts III-V. A metric geometry expression of thepositivity of the Laplace densities arising is established in Part VI.

Jets causing from active galactic nuclei can distributing vast distances through the intergalactic medium. When these relativistic jets interact with surrounding plasma, they may prepares instabilities. In this analyzing, we surveyed chromohydrodynamical instabilities that can arise at the interface between relativistic astrophysical jets and the ambient gas. Employ analytical theory and numerical simulations, we model the growth of current-driven and kink-type instabilities under conditions predicts in jet environments. Our results demonstrate that these instabilities develop succinctly at early times and aiding to jet deceleration and transverse momentum exchange. However, the jets are able to maintain collimation and penetration over overwhelming scales. Characterizing such instabilities tender insight into jet morphology and influences wide-ranging astrophysical phenomena on galactic to intracluster scales.

This study investigates the geometry of Wolf-Rayet (WR) winds in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) to constrain progenitor models of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). We analyzed the spatial distribution of WR stars and their winds using multi-wavelength observations and hydrodynamic simulations. Our results show a correlation between the orientation of WR winds and the location of GRBs in the LMC, suggesting a preference for GRB progenitors to align with dense, molecular regions of the WR winds. We constrained the inclination angle of the GRB progenitor's orbit using the observed geometry of the WR winds, providing insights into GRB formation and evolution. Our findings have implications for GRB event prediction and progenitor system understanding. We conclude that studying WR wind geometries in the LMC can aid in understanding GRB origins.

This articel investigates the phenomenon of turbulence in Burgers equations, a class of partial differential equations widely used to model various physical sysems. Turbulence is a complex and ubiquitous phenomenon characterized by chaotc and irregular flow patterns that occr over a wide range of scales. The study applies advanced mathematical and comptuational techniques to analyze the behavior of solutions to the Burgers equations. The authors present numerical simulations and analytical results that provide insights into the dynamics of turbulcnce in this specific frUamework. The findings contribute to the understanding of turbulence phenomena in nfluid dynamics, offering Maluable implications for practical applications in engineering and environmental sciences.

We relate the notion of matroid pathwidth to the minimum trellisstate-complexity (which we term trellis-width) of a linear code, and to thepathwidth of a graph. By reducing from the problem of computing the pathwidthof a graph, we show that the problem of determining the pathwidth of arepresentable matroid is NP-hard. Consequently, the problem of computing thetrellis-width of a linear code is also NP-hard. For a finite field $\F$, wealso consider the class of $\F$-representable matroids of pathwidth at most$w$, and correspondingly, the family of linear codes over $\F$ withtrellis-width at most $w$. These are easily seen to be minor-closed. Sincethese matroids (and codes) have branchwidth at most $w$, a result of Geelen andWhittle shows that such matroids (and the corresponding codes) arecharacterized by finitely many excluded minors. We provide the complete list ofexcluded minors for $w=1$, and give a partial list for $w=2$.

We have used a combination of experimental techniques, including magnetic susceptibility, specific heat, and neutron diffraction, to reveal the rich and complex magnetic behavior of this unique material. We find that the magnetic phase diagram is rich and complex, with a long-range antiferromagnetic phase at low temperatures and several distinct paramagnetic phases at higher temperatures. At intermediate temperatures, we observe the emergence of a spin-liquid-like state. Our results demonstrate the remarkable magnetic properties and the richness of the magnetic phase diagram in this Kagome-staircase compound, highlighting its potential for the exploration of novel quantum magnetic states and phenomena. Detailed analyses of the magnetic structures provide insights into the underlying magnetic interactions and their influence on the observed magnetic phenomena in Mn3V2O8.

We describe the role of GeV gamma-ray observations with GLAST-LAT (Gamma-rayLarge Area Space Telescope - Large Area Telescope) in identifying interactionsites of cosmic-ray proton (or hadrons) with interstellar medium (ISM). Weexpect to detect gamma rays from neutral pion decays in high-density ISMregions in the Galaxy, Large Magellanic Cloud, and other satellite galaxies.These gamma-ray sources have been detected already with EGRET (Energetic GammaRay Experiment Telescope) as extended sources (eg. LMC and Orion clouds) andGLAST-LAT will detect many more with a higher spatial resolution and in a widerspectral range. We have developed a novel image restoration technique based onthe Richardson-Lucy algorithm optimized for GLAST-LAT observation of extendedsources. Our algorithm calculates PSF (point spread function) for each event.This step is very important for GLAST-LAT and EGRET image analysis since PSFvaries more than one order of magnitude from one gamma ray to another dependingon its energy as well as its impact point and angle in the instrument. TheGLAST-LAT and EGRET image analysis has to cope with Poisson fluctuation due tolow number of detected photons for most sources. Our technique incorporateswavelet filtering to minimize effects due to the fluctuation. Preliminarystudies on some EGRET sources are presented, which shows potential of thisnovel image restoration technique for the identification and characterisationof extended gamma-ray sources.

Latest data on charmless strange vector-pseudoscalar $B^+$ decays nowincluding $B^+\to \rho^+ K^o$ confirm a simple penguin model in which the gluon$G$ in an initial $\bar s u G$ state fragments equally into $u \bar u$, $d \bard$ and $s \bar s$ and all form factors are equal. A search for possibleadditional contributions shows only a few signals not obscured by experimentalerrors whose implications are discussed. The experimental value of $0.25 \pm0.11$ for the ratio of the branching ratios $BR(B^+ \to K^{ +}\eta)$ to$BR(B^+\to K^{ +}\eta')$ confirms the parity selection rule prediction 0.32.Large violations arise in a new sum rule for the sum of these branching ratios,analogous to the similar pseudoscalar sum rule including $K^+\eta$ and$K^+\eta'$. Indications for either an electroweak penguin contribution oradditional admixtures like instrinsic charm in the $\eta-\eta'$ system remainto be clarified. An alternative symmetry description with new predictive powerclarifies the simple penguin approximation and presents new predictions whichcan be tested experimentally. The fragmentation of the $\bar s u G$ state intotwo mesons is described by a strong interaction S-matrix dominated by nonexotichadron resonances in multiparticle intermediate states.

Statistical modeling of experimental physical laws is based on theprobability density function of measured variables. It is expressed byexperimental data via a kernel estimator. The kernel is determined objectivelyby the scattering of data during calibration of experimental setup. A physicallaw, which relates measured variables, is optimally extracted from experimentaldata by the conditional average estimator. It is derived directly from thekernel estimator and corresponds to a general nonparametric regression. Theproposed method is demonstrated by the modeling of a return map of noisychaotic data. In this example, the nonparametric regression is used to predicta future value of chaotic time series from the present one. The mean predictorerror is used in the definition of predictor quality, while the redundancy isexpressed by the mean square distance between data points. Both statistics areused in a new definition of predictor cost function. From the minimum of thepredictor cost function, a proper number of data in the model is estimated.

The electron doping of undoped high-$T_c$ cuprates via the transfer of chargefrom manganites (or other oxides) using heterostructure geometries is heretheoretically discussed. This possibility is mainly addressed via a detailedanalysis of photoemission and diffusion voltage experiments, which locate theFermi level of manganites above the bottom of the upper Hubbard band of somecuprate parent compounds. A diagram with the relative location of Fermi levelsand gaps for several oxides is presented. The procedure discussed here isgeneric, allowing for the qualitative prediction of the charge flow directionat several oxide interfaces. The addition of electrons to antiferromagnetic Cuoxides may lead to a superconducting state at the interface with minimalquenched disorder. Model calculations using static and dynamical mean-fieldtheory, supplemented by a Poisson equation formalism to address chargeredistribution at the interface, support this view. The magnetic state of themanganites could be antiferromagnetic or ferromagnetic. The former is better toinduce superconductivity than the latter, since the spin-polarized chargetransfer will be detrimental to singlet superconductivity. It is concluded thatin spite of the robust Hubbard gaps, the electron doping of undoped cuprates atinterfaces appears possible, and its realization may open an exciting area ofresearch in oxide heterostructures.

GRB 050826, a subluminous gamma-ray burst (GRB), was unveiled on August 26, 2005, with a redshift of 0.296. The burst had a tremendously low luminosity, which made it an outlier in the creating luminosity distribution of GRB afterglows. Through a detailed analysis of the burst's spectral and occipital properties, we have found that GRB 050826 wishes indeed belong to the population of subluminous GRBs. Our results suggest that this event may have arisen from a different progenitor system or a unique explosion mechanism, providing newer insights into the diverse personalities of GRBs. The discovery of GRB 050826 highlights the utility of continue monitoring and studying GRBs to better understand their properties and the physics behind these resolute cosmic events.

In this article, we have deeply studied the areas of continuous tension. This is a large -scale research field that has not developed and combines the concept of tension and continuous systems. According to the definition, tension is a structure that balances pressure and compression elements to achieve stability. On the contrary, the characteristics of the continuous system are no discrete joints or edges. Our research aims to investigate the potential benefits of integrating these two concepts, especially in the context of structural engineering and material science. First of all, we outline the research status of tensions and continuous systems, highlighting their key characteristics and limitations. Next, we proposed a new method of designing continuous tension, which involves manipulating stretching and compressed elements to create a stable three -dimensional structure. Through a series of simulation and experiments to verify our methods, it proves the feasibility and advantages of continuous tension, rather than the traditional tension structure. Specifically, we show that continuous tension can show enhanced structural stability and adaptability, as well as reduced material use and environmental impact. We also explored the potential applications of continuous tension in various fields such as construction, engineering and materials science. In addition, we discussed the challenges and future directions of research in this field, including the development of new materials and manufacturing technology. Our work provides the foundation for further investigation of the attributes and potential of continuous tension, and paved the way for engineering and other innovative solutions. In the end, this research helps develop sustainable and efficient structural design, and emphasizes the importance of cross -disciplinary cooperation between architecture, engineering and materials science.

Computing the sign function of non-Hermitian matrices poses challenges. We introduce an iterative approach to determine the sign function of an arbitrary non-Hermitian matrix. Our method utilizes the Cayley transform to map eigenvalues into the unit circle, allowing application of spectral decomposition. We prove the convergence of our algorithm and analyze its computational complexity. As a significant application, we compute the sign function of the overlap Dirac operator at nonzero chemical potential arising in lattice QCD simulations. Numerical experiments demonstrate our technique accurately determines the signed overlap Dirac operator for systems up to a 323 spatial extent. This opens opportunities to study QCD and related systems involving non-Hermitian matrices under nonzero chemical potentials using overlap fermions. In summary, the iterative method introduced in this work provides an efficient means of evaluating the critical sign function for non-Hermitian matrices.

Magnetic Schrödinger operators describe quantum particles interacting with magnetic fields and have applications in modeling phenomena such as the quantum Hall effect. This article establihses Strichartz and smoothing estimates for Schrödinger operators with magnetic potentials that are nearly critical in facets three and higher. Nearly critical potentials allow the magnetic field to decay slowly at infinty. The derived estimates generalize previous results for subcritical potentials and help extend the local doctrines of the associated linear equations to nearly critical settings. Precise statements of the Strichartz and smoothing estimates are given alongside with their proofs, which rely on techniques such as resolvent estimates and commutator calculation.

Zero-range processes are interacting particle systems where particles hop between sites at rates that depend only on the occupation of the departure site. In this work we study zero-range processes defined on network structures rather than regular lattices. We analyze the stationary state of these processes on Erdos-Renyi random networks and Barabasi-Albert scale-free networks. Our results show that the network topology affects the condensation transition observed in these processes. Below a critical occupation density the stationary state remains homogeneous across the network, while above this density a macroscopic condensate forms localized on the highest degree nodes. We calculate the critical density and condensate size as a function of the network parameters. The study enhances our understanding of how topology influences nonequilibrium phase transitions in interacting particle systems defined on complex networks.

In this article, we revisit the validity of the FGR by means of both analytical and numerical calculations. We show that quantum dynamical phase transitions (QDPTs) occur as a result of the coalescence of two energy levels and the divergence of transition probabilities. We also map out the full phase diagram as a function of the system parameters and identify distinct quantum dynamical phases. Around the exceptional points, the transition dynamics become non-adiabatic and deviations from the FGR become significant. Our work establishes QDPTs as a new paradigm that supersedes the standard FGR description of quantum transitions. This new insight improves our understanding of non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in perturbed systems in many areas of physics.

This article proposes a modest solution to address an issue within the astronomical community. Large surveys are producing immense amounts of data but constraints on resources limit how much can be properly analyzed. The proposal is to establish centralized data centers to house the raw data from all major surveys. These centers would free individual researchers from having to store Petabytes of raw images and spectra locally. The centers would provide simple interfaces for querying and downloading calibrated data subsets as needed. Simple usage policies and modest fees would help cover operational costs while ensuring broad access. If implemented, this proposal could help maximize scientific returns from the surveys by facilitating collaborative data mining efforts. Centralized data hosting could also simplify preserving the raw survey records for future re-analysis as techniques improve.

The magnetic spectrum at high-energies in heavily underdopedYBa$_{2}$Cu$_{3}$O$_{6.35}$ (T$_{c}$=18 K) has been determined throughout theBrillouin zone. At low-energy the scattering forms a cone of spin excitationsemanating from the antiferromagnetic (0.5, 0.5) wave vector with an acousticvelocity similar to that of insulating cuprates. At high energy transfers,below the maximum energy of 270 meV at (0.5, 0), we observe zone boundarydispersion much larger and spectral weight loss more extensive than ininsulating antiferromagnets. Moreover we report phenomena not found ininsulators, an overall lowering of the zone-boundary energies and a largedamping of $\sim$ 100 meV of the spin excitations at high-energies. The energyabove which the damping occurs coincides approximately with the gap determinedfrom transport measurements.
