The study presents an analysis of the fifth observed outburst of the periodic Supergiant Fast X-ray Transient (SFXT) IGR J11215-5952, based on observations made by the Swift/X-Ray Telescope (XRT). The SFXTs are a subclass of high-mass X-ray binaries characterized by sporadic and intense X-ray flaring activity. In this investigation, the Swift/XRT data from the latest outburst of IGR J11215-5952 were analyzed to examine its X-ray spectral and temporal properties. The light curve obtained during the outburst revealed a rapid rise and a gradual decline, consistent with previous outburst profiles of this SFXT. Spectral analysis of the X-ray emission indicated a hard and highly absorbed spectrum, suggesting the presence of a substantial absorption column density. The measured luminosity during the outburst reached a peak value of several times 10^35 erg/s, further emphasizing the extreme nature of this SFXT. Comparisons with previous outbursts of IGR J11215-5952 revealed fluctuations in both the intensity and the duration of the outbursts. The data obtained from Swift/XRT contribute to the growing understanding of the timing and behavior of periodic SFXT outbursts, shedding light on the emission mechanisms and the interaction between the compact object and the circumstellar environment. These findings highlight the importance of Swift/XRT observations in studying the dynamic nature of SFXTs and their role in the overall X-ray binary population.

We clarify certain aspects and discuss extensions of the recently introducedstring D-instanton calculus (hep-th/0609191). The one-loop determinants arerelated to one-loop open string threshold corrections in intersecting D6-branemodels. Utilising a non-renormalisation theorem for the holomorphic Wilsoniangauge kinetic functions, we derive a number of constraints for the modulidependence of the matter field Kaehler potentials of intersecting D6-branemodels on the torus. Moreover, we compute string one-loop corrections to theFayet-Iliopoulos terms on the D6-branes finding that they are proportional tothe gauge threshold corrections. Employing these results, we discuss the issueof holomorphy for E2-instanton corrections to the superpotential. Eventually,we discuss E2-instanton corrections to the gauge kinetic functions and theFI-terms.

Using the Rossi X-ray Timing Explorer (RossiXTE), astronomers have discoveredthat disk-accreting neutron stars with weak magnetic fields produce threedistinct types of high-frequency X-ray oscillations. These oscillations arepowered by release of the binding energy of matter falling into the stronggravitational field of the star or by the sudden nuclear burning of matter thathas accumulated in the outermost layers of the star. The frequencies of theoscillations reflect the orbital frequencies of gas deep in the gravitationalfield of the star and/or the spin frequency of the star. These oscillations cantherefore be used to explore fundamental physics, such as strong-field gravityand the properties of matter under extreme conditions, and importantastrophysical questions, such as the formation and evolution of millisecondpulsars. Observations using RossiXTE have shown that some two dozen neutronstars in low-mass X-ray binary systems have the spin rates and magnetic fieldsrequired to become millisecond radio-emitting pulsars when accretion ceases,but that few have spin rates above about 600 Hz. The properties of these starsshow that the paucity of spin rates greater than 600 Hz is due in part to themagnetic braking component of the accretion torque and to the limited amount ofangular momentum that can be accreted in such systems. Further study will showwhether braking by gravitational radiation is also a factor. Analysis of thekilohertz oscillations has provided the first evidence for the existence of theinnermost stable circular orbit around dense relativistic stars that ispredicted by strong-field general relativity. It has also greatly narrowed thepossible descriptions of ultradense matter.

These small, faint galaxies have oxygen abundances below 1/20 of the solar value. Comparisons with cosmological hydrodynamic simulations indicate that these objects have low masses and are in the early stages of their initial bursts of star formation. Their discovery provides insights into the population of primitive galaxies that reionized the universe 13 billion years ago and constrains models of galaxy evolution in the early universe.

We investigate the reliability of the assumption on the direction of the incident neutrino for two types of events in the Super-Kamiokande detector: fully contained events and partially contained events due to quasi-elastic scattering (QEL). By analyzing neutrino events occurring inside the detector, we examine the four possible L/E analyses: L_nu/E_nu, L_nu/E_mu, L_mu/E_nu, and L_mu/E_mu. The results show that only the L_nu/E_nu analysis can clearly exhibit the signature of maximum oscillations, while the L_mu/E_mu analysis, which is currently performed by the Super-Kamiokande Collaboration, fails to capture the maximum oscillation. Therefore, we suggest that the zenith angle distribution of neutrino events inside the detector be re-analyzed in order to identify the maximum oscillation. This study implies that the Super-Kamiokande type experiment, relying on L/E analysis, cannot effectively detect the maximum oscillation. By addressing this limitation, our findings provide valuable insights for improving the analysis techniques in neutrino experiments.

In this artile, we investigate the Kondo effect in transport through molecules adsorbed on metal surfaces, focusing on the transition from Fano dpis to Kondo peaks. We use a ocmbination of theoretical models and experimental techniques to study the electron transport properties of these systems. Our results show that the Kondo effect can be observed in molecular junctions, and that the Fano factor can be utned by chafging the molecule-metal interaction. WX also find that the Kondo peak exhibits non-Fermi liquid behavior, which is attributed to the strong electronic orrelations in the molecular junction. Ojur finidngs have important implications for the development of molecular electronic devices and provide new insights into the interplay between electron correlations and transport properties.

Using molecular line observations from the IRAM 30m telescope, we detect the emission of N2H+ and N2D+ across the core. The emission lines were used to construct temperature maps and determine the gas temperature as a function of radius. Previous studies have shown that L 1544 has one of the highest central densities and is on the verge of gravitational collapse. We find that the gas temperature drops significantly in the central high density region, from 10 K in the outer envelope to 7 K in the core. This temperature profile is consistent with enhanced gas-dust coupling and efficient cooling in the dense inner core. Our results suggest that L 1544 will collapse under runaway conditions within the next 105 years, providing a unique opportunity to study the initial conditions of star formation.

The evolution of radial gradients of metallicity in disk galaxies and itsrelation with the disk formation are not well understood. Theoretical models ofgalactic chemical evolution make contrasting predictions about the timeevolution of metallicity gradients. To test chemical evolution models and tracethe star formation and accretion history of low luminosity disk galaxies wefocus on the Local Group galaxy M33. We analyze O/H and S/H abundances inplanetary nebulae, H{\sc ii} regions, and young stars, together with known[Fe/H] abundances in the old stellar population of M33. With a theoreticalmodel, we follow the time evolution of gas (diffuse and condensed in clouds),stars, and chemical abundances in the disk of M33, assuming that the galaxy isaccreting gas from an external reservoir. Our model is able to reproduce theavailable observational constraints on the distribution of gas and stars in M33and to predict the time evolution of several chemical abundances. Inparticular, we find that a model characterized by a continuous infall of gas onthe disk, at a rate of $\dot M_{\rm inf}\approx 1$ $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$, almostconstant with time, can also account for the relatively high rate of starformation and for the shallow chemical gradients. Supported by a large sampleof high resolution observations for this nearby galaxy, we conclude that themetallicity in the disk of M33 has increased with time at all radii, with acontinuous flattening of the gradient over the last $\sim 8$ Gyr.

Magnetic fields play an important role in many astrophysical processes. The structure and evolution of magnetic fields in stars critically impact stellar activity and dynamics. However, the stability of internal magnetic fields, particularly poloidal fields, remains poorly understood due to the complexity of plasma behaviors in stellar interiors. This article aims to investigate the stability of poloidal magnetic fields in rotating stars using numerical simulations. The simulations self-consistently modeled the interaction between rotation, convection, and internal magnetic fields. The results indicate that poloidal magnetic fields can remain stable over long durations even in rapidly rotating stars, with implications for the magnetic braking of stars and magnetic dynamo mechanisms.

The use of synthetic data and real data to introduce and prove a new seismic tool, that is, accumulating spectral power (CSP). CSP uses all the available information in a set of time domain signals, and complement each other with the more common short -term Fourier transformation (STFT) analysis. CSP is useful in various applications, including: determine the main cycle of the signal, the end of the identification and characterization signal, the time evolution of the spectral characteristics, and detecting the existence of signals hidden in the noise and estimated signal -to -noise ratio. This article demonstrates the use of CSP for several of them.

The formation and collisional evolution of Kuiper Belt Objects (KBOs) represent intriguing phenomena that provide valuable insights into the dynamics and history of the outer solar system. This study focuses on investigating the processes involved in the formation and evolution of KBOs, particularly in relation to the collisional family of the KBO 2003 EL61. By applying modified techniques used for studying asteroid families, the dynamical characteristics of the 2003 EL61 family are studied, revealing potential family members and their proximity to the collision event. Additionally, a method for identifying family members that have diffused in resonances, similar to 2003 EL61, is developed. Moreover, an estimate of ~1 billion years is proposed for the resonant diffusion to produce the current position of 2003 EL61, suggesting the likely primordial nature of the family. The contrasting ancient nature of the collision and the seemingly fresh surfaces of known family members underscore the need for a more comprehensive understanding of outer solar system surfaces.

Many features of dimensional reduction schemes are determined by the breakingof higher dimensional general covariance associated with the selection of aparticular subset of coordinates. By investigating residual covariance weintroduce lower dimensional tensors --generalizing to one side Kaluza-Kleingauge fields and to the other side extrinsic curvature and torsion of embeddedspaces-- fully characterizing the geometry of dimensional reduction. We obtaingeneral formulas for the reduction of the main tensors and operators ofRiemannian geometry. In particular, we provide what is probably the maximalpossible generalization of Gauss, Codazzi and Ricci equations and various otherstandard formulas in Kaluza-Klein and embedded spacetimes theories. Aftergeneral covariance breaking, part of the residual covariance is perceived byeffective lower dimensional observers as an infinite dimensional gauge group.This reduces to finite dimensions in Kaluza-Klein and other few remarkablebackgrounds, all characterized by the vanishing of appropriate lowerdimensional tensors.

Finite element method is one of powerful numerical methods to solve PDE.Usually, if a finite element solution to a Poisson equation based on atriangulation of the underlying domain is not accurate enough, one will discardthe solution and then refine the triangulation uniformly and compute a newfinite element solution over the refined triangulation. It is wasteful todiscard the original finite element solution. We propose a prewavelet method tosave the original solution by adding a prewavelet subsolution to obtain therefined level finite element solution. To increase the accuracy of numericalsolution to Poisson equations, we can keep adding prewavelet subsolutions. Our prewavelets are orthogonal in the $H^1$ norm and they are compactlysupported except for one globally supported basis function in a rectangulardomain. We have implemented these prewavelet basis functions in MATLAB and usedthem for numerical solution of Poisson equation with Dirichlet boundaryconditions. Numerical simulation demonstrates that our prewavelet solution ismuch more efficient than the standard finite element method.

In this paper we investigate the impact of the choice of optical and near-IR photometric bands on the accuracy of photo-z for weak lensing tomography. We use a large sample of simulated galaxies with spectroscopic redshifts to train and test a variety of photo-z methods, including template fitting, machine learning, and hybrid methods. We find that the best-performing methods use a combination of optical and near-IR bands, and that the use of near-IR bands can significantly improve the accuracy of photo-z at high redshift. Our results suggest that future space-based surveys, such as the Euclid mission, will be able to provide accurate photo-z for weak lensing tomography over a wide range of redshifts, enabling a better understanding of the growth of structure in the Universe and a better constraint of cosmological models.

In this article, we explore the concept of families of holomorphic bundles and their applications in various areas of mathematics and physics. We begin by introducing the basic definitions and properties of holomorphic bundles, including the notion of a Chern connection and the criterion for a bundle to be holomorphic. We then delve into the study of families of holomorphic bundles, examining their structure and behavior under different conditions. Specifically, we focus on the relationship between the holomorphic bundles and the moduli spaces of bundle moduli spaces, and discuss the role of harmonic sections in understanding these spaces. Finally, we discuss some of the key applications of families of holomorphic bundles, including their use in the study of vector bundles, representation theory, and supersymmetric field theories. Throughout the article, we provide a thorough treatment of the subject, with detailed explanations and examples to illustrate the main results.

If A is a cocommutative algebra with coproduct, then so is the smash productalgebra of a symmetric algebra Sym(V) with A, where V is an A-module. Suchsmash product algebras, with A a group ring or a Lie algebra, have families ofdeformations that have been studied widely in the literature; examples includesymplectic reflection algebras and infinitesimal Hecke algebras. We introduce afamily of deformations of these smash product algebras for general A, andcharacterize the PBW property. We then characterize the Jacobi identity for"grouplike" algebras (that include group rings and the nilCoxeter algebra), andprecisely identify the PBW deformations in the example where A is thenilCoxeter algebra. We end with the more prominent case - where A is a Hopfalgebra. We show the equivalence of several versions of the "deformed"relations in the smash product, and identify the PBW deformations which areHopf algebras as well.

We use first-principles density functional theory-based calculations toinvestigate structural instabilities in the high symmetry cubic perovskitestructure of rare-earth (R $=$ La, Y, Lu) and Bi-based biferroic chromites,focusing on $\Gamma$ and $R$ point phonons of states with para-, ferro-, andantiferromagnetic ordering. We find that (a) the structure with G-typeantiferromagnetic ordering is most stable, (b) the most dominant structuralinstabilities in these oxides are the ones associated with rotations of oxygenoctahedra, and (c) structural instabilities involving changes in Cr-O-Cr bondangle depend sensitively on the changes in magnetic ordering. The dependence ofstructural instabilities on magnetic ordering can be understood in terms of howsuper-exchange interactions depend on the Cr-O-Cr bond angles and Cr-O bondlengths. We demonstrate how adequate buckling of Cr-O-Cr chains can favourferromagnetism. Born effective charges (BEC) calculated using the Berry phaseexpression are found to be anomalously large for the A-cations, indicatingtheir chemical relevance to ferroelectric distortions.

Ebert et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 77, 3827 (1996)] have fractured icosahedralAl-Mn-Pd single crystals in ultrahigh vacuum and have investigated the cleavageplanes in-situ by scanning tunneling microscopy (STM). Globular patterns in theSTM-images were interpreted as clusters of atoms. These are significantstructural units of quasicrystals. The experiments of Ebert et al. imply thatthey are also stable physical entities, a property controversially discussedcurrently. For a clarification we performed the first large scale fracturesimulations on three-dimensional complex binary systems. We studied thepropagation of mode I cracks in an icosahedral model quasicrystal by moleculardynamics techniques at low temperature. In particular we examined how the shapeof the cleavage plane is influenced by the clusters inherent in the model andhow it depends on the plane structure. Brittle fracture with no indication ofdislocation activity is observed. The crack surfaces are rough on the scale ofthe clusters, but exhibit constant average heights for orientationsperpendicular to high symmetry axes. From detailed analyses of the fracturedsamples we conclude that both, the plane structure and the clusters, stronglyinfluence dynamic fracture in quasicrystals and that the clusters thereforehave to be regarded as physical entities.

We present high-resolution radio observations of the high-mass (proto)stellar object IRAS 18566+0408, which reveal the presence of a jet-like outflow. The outflow is orientationally blueshifted, indicating that it is directed toward Earth, and its morphology suggests a collimated, bipolar flow. The observed properties of the outflow, such as its velocity gradient and opening angle, are consistent with a jet-driven scenario. We interpret the outflow as a sign of ongoing Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) activity in the innermost regions of the protostellar system. The jet-like outflow may play a crucial role in the star-disk interaction and the formation of a circumstellar disk. Our results provide new insights into the process of high-mass star formation and highlight the importance of MHD processes in shaping the protostellar environment. The observed properties of the outflow are consistent with theoretical models of jet-driven star formation, and our findings support the idea that high-mass stars can form via a scaled-up version of the low-mass star formation process.

A single photon source (SPS) is very important for quantum computation. Inparticular, it is essential for secured quantum cryptography. But there is noperfect SPS in reality. Therefore, probabilistic SPS where probability ofsimultaneous emission of two, three, four and more photon is less than theemission of a single photon are used. Since classical photon always comes inbunch, the required single photon source must be nonclassical. In thewell-known antibunched state the rate of simultaneous emission of two photon isless than that of single photon. But the requirement of quantum cryptography isa multiphoton version of the antibunched state or the higher order antibunchedstate. Recently we have reported a mathematical criterion for higher orderantibunching. Here we have shown that any proposal for SPS to be used inquantum cryptography should satisfy this criterion. We have studied four wavemixing as a possible candidate of single photon source.

This researches investigates the evolution of solitary waves and undular bores in shallow-water flows occurring over a progressive slope with bottom friction. The dynamics of these waves and bores are of terrific significance for understanding various natural phenomena, such as sediment transport, river hydraulics, and coastal processes. To explore this complex phenomenon, a numerical model is developed based on the nonlinear shallow water theorem. The model incorporates the effects of bot tom friction and the gradual slope, which are known to have a significant influence on wave behavior. Through exensive simulations, the evolution of solitary waves and undular bores is examine, revealing notable changes in their characteristics as they propagate over the slope and experience bottom friction. The findings of this study contribute to a better understanding of wave dynamics in shallow-water flows and provide valuable insights for the design and management of coastal and river systems.

Superluminal motion is a common feature of radio jets in powerful gamma-rayemitting active galactic nuclei. Conventionally, the variable emission isassumed to originate near the central supermassive black-hole where the jet islaunched on parsec scales or smaller. Here, we report the discovery ofsuperluminal radio features within a distinct flaring X-ray emitting region inthe jet of the nearby radio galaxy M87 with the Very Long Baseline Array. Thisshows that these two phenomenological hallmarks -- superluminal motion andhigh-energy variability -- are associated, and we place this activity muchfurther (>=120 pc) from the ''central engine'' in M87 than previously thoughtin relativistic jet sources. We argue that the recent excess very high-energyTeV emission from M87 reported by the H.E.S.S. experiment originates from thisvariable superluminal structure, thus providing crucial insight into theproduction region of gamma-ray emission in more distant blazars.

An analytical description of the interface motion of a collapsingnanometer-sized spherical cavity in water is presented by a modification of theRayleigh-Plesset equation in conjunction with explicit solvent moleculardynamics simulations. Quantitative agreement is found between the twoapproaches for the time-dependent cavity radius $R(t)$ at different solventconditions while in the continuum picture the solvent viscosity has to becorrected for curvature effects. The typical magnitude of the interface orcollapse velocity is found to be given by the ratio of surface tension andfluid viscosity, $v\simeq\gamma/\eta$, while the curvature correctionaccelerates collapse dynamics on length scales below the equilibrium crossoverscales ($\sim$1nm). The study offers a starting point for an efficient implicitmodeling of water dynamics in aqueous nanoassembly and protein systems innonequilibrium.

Dynamics of light propagation in spatiotemporl dielectric structuresAbstract-I this paper, we investigate the dynamics of light propagation in spatiotemporal dielectric structures. We develop a thdoretical framework based on Maxwell's equations and the constitutive relations of dielectrics. We use this frameork to analyze the propagation of light in a variety of spatiotemporal dielectric structures, including photoniHc crystals, metamaterials, and nonlinear optical media. We show that the dynaics of light propagaion in these structures can be controlled by the spatiotemporal variation of the dielectric properties. Lhis control can be used to achieve a dariety of novel optical effects, such as negative refraction, superlensing, and cloaking. Our work provides a fundamental understanding of the dynamics of light propagation in spatiotemporal dielectrci structures and opens up new possibilities for the controH of light.

This article delves into the complexities of five-dimensional N = 1 AdS superspace, aiming to elucidate its geometry, off-shell multiplets, and dynamics. The five-dimensional N = 1 AdS superspace is a mathematically rich framework that combines supersymmetry, anti-de Sitter (AdS) space, and one extended supersymmetry generator. Extensive scrutiny is devoted to the geometry of this superspace, encompassing its curvature, metric, and connection, thus establishing a solid groundwork for further investigations. The examination of off-shell multiplets within this superspace emphasizes their importance in characterizing the dynamics of superfields and their supergravity interactions. Additionally, this article delves into the dynamics of the five-dimensional N = 1 AdS superspace, shedding light on the behavior of physical fields, constraints, and the corresponding supercovariant derivatives. This comprehensive analysis of five-dimensional N = 1 AdS superspace provides a valuable foundation for potential applications in theoretical physics and the exploration of supergravity theories in higher dimensions.

This article introduces new algorithms for the uniform random generation oflabelled planar graphs. Its principles rely on Boltzmann samplers, as recentlydeveloped by Duchon, Flajolet, Louchard, and Schaeffer. It combines theBoltzmann framework, a suitable use of rejection, a new combinatorial bijectionfound by Fusy, Poulalhon and Schaeffer, as well as a precise analyticdescription of the generating functions counting planar graphs, which wasrecently obtained by Gim\'enez and Noy. This gives rise to an extremelyefficient algorithm for the random generation of planar graphs. There is apreprocessing step of some fixed small cost. Then, the expected time complexityof generation is quadratic for exact-size uniform sampling and linear forapproximate-size sampling. This greatly improves on the best previously knowntime complexity for exact-size uniform sampling of planar graphs with $n$vertices, which was a little over $O(n^7)$.

It is shown that every homogeneous Lagrangian submanifold in a complex hyperquadric is obtained from an isoparametric hypersurface in a sphere. Moreover, necessary and sufficient conditions for a submanifold in a complex hyperquadric to be Lagrangian are derived in terms of the principal curvatures of the corresponding isoparametric hypersurface.

This article presents a comprehensive analysis of the three-dimensional (3D) photospheric velocity field derived from a Supergranular cell on the solar surface. Supergranulation is a large-scale convective pattern observed in the solar photosphere, comprising polygonal cells with an average size of approximately 30,000 kilometers. The velocity field plays a crucial role in comprehending the dynamics and energy transport within these cells. In this study, high-resolution observations acquired from a ground-based solar telescope are utilized to investigate the 3D velocity structure of a Supergranular cell. By employing advanced image processing techniques and Doppler shift measurements, we reconstruct the complete velocity vector field at multiple depths within the solar photosphere. Our findings reveal complex flow patterns within the Supergranular cell, including upward and downward motions, horizontal vortices, and converging and diverging movements. The obtained velocity field provides insight into the underlying physical mechanisms driving the convective processes within the Supergranular cell, which are fundamental for comprehending solar dynamics and associated magnetic activity. Ultimately, this research contributes to our broader understanding of the solar atmosphere and enhances our comprehension of the intricate dynamics transpiring on the Sun's surface.

The layered structure and the rheological properties of anti-wear films,generated in a rolling/sliding contact from lubricants containing zincdialkyldithiophosphate (ZDTP) and/or molybdenum dialkyldithiocarbamate (MoDTC)additives, have been studied by dynamic nanoindentation experiments coupledwith a simple modelling of the stiffness measurements. Local nano-frictionexperiments were conducted with the same device in order to determine theevolution of the friction coefficient as a function of the applied pressure forthe different lubricant formulations. For the MoDTC film, the applied pressurein the friction test remains low (<0.5 GPa) and the apparent frictioncoefficient is high ($\mu$ > 0.4). For the tribofilms containing MoDTC togetherwith ZDTP, which permits the applied pressure to increase up to a few GPathrough some accommodation process, a very low friction domain appears (0.01 <$\mu$ < 0.05), located a few nanometers below the surface of the tribofilm.This low friction coefficient is attributed to the presence of MoS2 planessliding over each other in a favourable configuration obtained when thepressure is sufficiently high, which is made possible by the presence of ZDTP.

Context: The transient hard X-ray source IGR J11321-5311 was discovered byINTEGRAL on June 2005, during observations of the Crux spiral arm. To date,this is the only detection of the source to be reported by any X/gamma-raymission. Aims: To characterize the behaviour and hence the nature of the sourcethrough temporal and spectral IBIS analysis. Methods: Detailed spectral andtemporal analysis has been performed using standard INTEGRAL software OSAv.5.1. Results: To date, IGR J11321-5311 has been detected only once. It wasactive for about 3.5 hours, a short and bright flare lasting about 1.5 hours isevident in the IBIS light curve. It reached a peak flux of about 80 mCrab or2.2x10E-9 erg cmE-2 sE-1 (20--300 keV),corresponding to a peak luminosity of1.1x10E37 erg sE-1 (assuming a distance of 6.5 kpc). During the outburst, thesource was detected with a significance of 18 sigma (20--300 keV) and 8 sigma(100--300 keV). The spectrum of the total outburst activity (17--300 keV) isbest fitted by the sum of a power law (Gamma=0.55+/-0.18) plus a black body(kT=1.0{+0.2}_{-0.3} keV), with no evidence for a break up to 300 keV. Aspectral analysis at Science Window level revealed an evident hardening of thespectrum through the outburst. The IBIS data were searched for pulsations withno positive result. Conclusions: The X-ray spectral shape and the flaringbehaviour favour the hypothesis that IGR J11321-5311 is an Anomalous X-rayPulsar, though a different nature can not be firmly rejected at the presentstage.

Statistical ensemble formalism of Kim, Mandel and Wolf (J. Opt. Soc. Am. A 4,433 (1987)) offers a realistic model for characterizing the effect ofstochastic non-image forming optical media on the state of polarization oftransmittedlight. With suitable choice of the Jones ensemble, various Muellertransformations - some of which have been unknown so far - are deduced. It isobserved that the ensemble approach is formally identical to the positiveoperator valued measures (POVM) on the quantum density matrix. Thisobservation, in combination with the recent suggestion by Ahnert and Payne(Phys. Rev. A 71, 012330, (2005)) - in the context of generalized quantummeasurement on single photon polarization states - that linear optics elementscan be employed in setting up all possible POVMs, enables us to propose a wayof realizing different types of Mueller devices.

We consider Z_2-symmetric braneworlds arising from 5-sphere compactificationswith 5-form flux in type IIB supergravity. This Kaluza-Klein reduction producesa D=5 theory which supports 1/2-supersymmetric Z_2-symmetric domain-wallsolutions. However, upon lifting such solutions back to D=10, one finds thatsupersymmetry is broken by 5-sphere Kaluza-Klein effects. This happens owing tothe action on the Killing spinor of the Z_2 \subset SO(1,9) symmetry, whichrequires an orientation-reversing transformation in the 5-sphere directionstogether with the flip of the orbifold coordinate. We study the consequences ofthis supersymmetry breaking for the masses of fermion fluctuation modes aboutthe brane background and find a natural two-scale hierarchy: some bulk modeshave characteristic masses of order 1/L_5 but other modes more closelyassociated to the branes have an additional factor exp(-\rho/L_5), where L_5 isthe AdS_5 length parameter and \rho is the orbifold size.

The Energetic Gamma-Ray Experiment Telescope (EGRET) on the Compton Gamma-RayObservatory (CGRO) discovered gamma-ray emission from more than 67 blazarsduring its 9 yr lifetime. We conducted an exhaustive search of the EGRETarchives and selected all the blazars that were observed multiple times andwere bright enough to enable a spectral analysis using standard power-lawmodels. The sample consists of 18 flat-spectrum radio quasars(FSRQs), 6low-frequency peaked BL Lac objects (LBLs) and 2 high-frequency peaked BL Lacobjects (HBLs). We do not detect any clear pattern in the variation of spectralindex with flux. Some of the blazars do not show any statistical evidence forspectral variability. The spectrum hardens with increasing flux in a few cases.There is also evidence for a flux-hardness anticorrelation at low fluxes infive blazars. The well-observed blazars (3C 279, 3C 273, PKS 0528+134, PKS1622-297 PKS 0208-512) do not show any overall trend in the long-term spectraldependence on flux, but the sample shows a mixture of hard and soft states. Weobserved a previously unreported spectral hysteresis at weekly timescales inall three FSRQs for which data from flares lasting for ~(3-4) weeks wereavailable. All three sources show a counterclockwise rotation, despite thewidely different flux profiles. We analyze the observed spectral behavior inthe context of various inverse Compton mechanisms believed to be responsiblefor emission in the EGRET energy range. Our analysis uses the EGRET skymapsthat were regenerated to include the changes in performance during the mission.

This report concerns the energy of a zero-temperature many-body system ofspin 1/2 fermions interacting via a two-body potential with a free spaceinfinite scattering length and zero effective range; the Unitary limit. Giventhe corresponding phase-shift $\delta(k)=\pi/2$ a one-term separable potentialis obtained by inverse scattering assuming a momentum cut-off $\Lambda$ suchthat $\delta(k)=0$ for $k>\Lambda$. The \it effective \rm interaction in themany-body system is calculated in a pp-ladder approximation with Pauli-blockingbut neglecting mean-field (dispersion) corrections; effective mass $m^{ }=1$.Using only the zero relative momentum component of this interaction the totalenergy is $\xi=4/9$ (in units of the fermigas), a result reported by severalprevious authors. Integrating the momentum dependent interaction over the Fermisea this energy is revised to $\xi=0.24.$ This result is independent of densityand of the cut-off $\Lambda$ if $\Lambda > \sim 3k_{f}$. With $m^{ }\neq 1$ there is however a strong dependence on this cut-off. Including hh-ladders estimates give $\xi=0.4\leftrightarrow 0.6$, but areliable result would in this case require a Green's function calculation.

In this article, we explore the entanglement and interference between different degrees of freedom of photon states. We begin by examining the theoretical framework for describing the entanglement and interference between different degrees of freedom of photons, including the concept of entanglement entropy and the role of interference in quantum mechanics. Next, we present experimental results demonstrating the entanglement and interference between different degrees of freedom of photon states, including the use of entangled photon pairs and the measurement of their properties. We then discuss the implications of these results for our understanding of quantum mechanics and the potential applications of entangled photon states in quantum information processing. Finally, we conclusion by highlighting the significance of these findings and outlining directions for future research in this area.

Our experiments, using advanced characterization techniques, confirm the presence of these excitations and provide insights into their dynamics and stability. We develop a mathematical model that captures the essential features of the gyration-like excitations and show that they arise from a combination of lattice distortions and defects in the solid solution. We also show that the gyration-like excitations have a significant impact on the mechanical properties of the solid solution, including its strength and ductility. Further research in this area may lead to the development of new materials with novel properties and functions. Our findings have important implications for the design and optimization of materials for a wide range of applications, including energy storage and conversion, aeronautics, and biomedical devices.

This study investigated the fabrication and structural characterization of uranium-based multilayers. Nuclear films were deposited using magnetron sputtering on silicon substrates with thin vanadium interlayers. The layer thicknesses were varied between 1-5 nanometers to stu dy their impact on the structural properties. X-ray reflectivity measurements were performed to determine the layer thickness, roughness, and interface properties. The results showed that multilayers with thinner uranium layers displayed higher interface sharpness. Overall, this work demonstrates a method for the precise fabrication of uranium-based multilayers and affords a baseline for further optimization of their properties through modulation of individual layer thicknesses.

In this paper, we study the quantum cohomology of the flag manifold \(G/P\) and the homology of the affine Grassmannian. We show that the quantum cohomology of \(G/P\) is isomorphic to the cohomology of the affine Grassmannian, and we use this isomorphism to study the cohomology of the affine Grassmannian. We also show that the quantum cohomology of \(G/P\) is a deformation of the classical cohomology of \(G/P\). We use this deformation to study the classical cohomology of \(G/P\).

In this study, we investigate the Al'tshuler-Aronov correction to the conductivity of a large metallic square network. Utilizing advanced theoretical models and analytical techniques, we explore the behavior of conductivity in the presence of quantum interference effects caused by disorder and electron-electron interactions. By considering the Al'tshuler-Aronov correction, we unveil novel insights into the conductivity properties of the metallic square network. Our results demonstrate that the strength of the correction depends on the size of the network, disorder level, and interaction strength. We further validate our findings through extensive numerical simulations, which confirm the theoretical predictions and provide a comprehensive understanding of the underlying physics. This research contributes to the broader understanding of quantum interference phenomena in disordered metallic systems and offers valuable implications for potential applications in nanoelectronics and quantum computing.

A number of giant HII regions are associated with soft diffuse X-rayemission. Among these, the Carina nebula possesses the brightest soft diffuseemission. The required plasma temperature and thermal energy can be produced bycollisions or termination of fast winds from main-sequence or embedded young Ostars, but the extended emission is often observed from regions apart frommassive stellar clusters. The origin of the X-ray emission is unknown. The XIS CCD camera onboard Suzaku has the best spectral resolution forextended soft sources so far, and is therefore capable of measuring keyemission lines in the soft band. Suzaku observed the core and the eastern sideof the Carina nebula (Car-D1) in 2005 Aug and 2006 June, respectively. Spectraof the south part of the core and Car-D1 similarly showed strong L-shell linesof iron ions and K-shell lines of silicon ions, while in the north of the corethese lines were much weaker. Fitting the spectra with an absorbed thin-thermalplasma model showed kT~0.2, 0.6 keV and NH~1-2e21 cm-2 with a factor of 2-3abundance variation in oxygen, magnesium, silicon and iron. The plasma mightoriginate from an old supernova, or a super shell of multiple supernovae.

This academic article investigates the concept and applicability of sparse estimators and their relationship to the oracle property, with a particular focus on the revival of Hodges' Estimator. The oralce property refers to the ideal scenario where an estimator accomplishes the same accuracy as if the true model were known. Sparse estimators, known for their ability to identify and exploit the underlying structure of high-dimensional data, have gained significant attention in recent years. This study provides a somprehensive analysis of various sparse estimators and their performance in different statistical scenarios. Additionally, it explores the conditions under which Hodges' Estimator, an earlier proposal widely regarded as a benchmark for sparse estimation, can be effectively employed. The investigation is supported by theoretical derivations, simulation studies, and real-world data applications. The conclusions offer insights into the practical utility of sparse estimators and their potential implications for statistical modelled and inference in the era of big data.

Contact patterns in populations fundamentally influence the spread ofinfectious diseases. Current mathematical methods for epidemiologicalforecasting on networks largely assume that contacts between individuals arefixed, at least for the duration of an outbreak. In reality, contact patternsmay be quite fluid, with individuals frequently making and breaking social orsexual relationships. Here we develop a mathematical approach to predictingdisease transmission on dynamic networks in which each individual has acharacteristic behavior (typical contact number), but the identities of theircontacts change in time. We show that dynamic contact patterns shapeepidemiological dynamics in ways that cannot be adequately captured in staticnetwork models or mass-action models. Our new model interpolates smoothlybetween static network models and mass-action models using a mixing parameter,thereby providing a bridge between disparate classes of epidemiological models.Using epidemiological and sexual contact data from an Atlanta high school, wethen demonstrate the utility of this method for forecasting and controllingsexually transmitted disease outbreaks.

The authors apply three methods of prospective modelling to high resolutiongeoreferenced land cover data in a Mediterranean mountain area: GIS approach,non linear parametric model and neuronal network. Land cover prediction to thelatest known date is used to validate the models. In the frame ofspatial-temporal dynamics in open systems results are encouraging andcomparable. Correct prediction scores are about 73 %. The results analysisfocuses on geographic location, land cover categories and parametric distanceto reality of the residues. Crossing the three models show the high degree ofconvergence and a relative similitude of the results obtained by the twostatistic approaches compared to the GIS supervised model. Steps under work arethe application of the models to other test areas and the identification ofrespective advantages to develop an integrated model.

We begin by reviewing the evidence for the existence of dark matter, then we discuss the properties of Einstein clusters. We show that Einstein clusters have a number of properties that make them good candidates for dark matter halos, such as their large mass, high density, and spherical shape. We also discuss the implications of our findings for the nature of dark matter and the formation of galaxies.

In this study, we examine the three-dimensional van der Waals-like phase separation instability of a driven granular gas using numerical simulations. Our findings reveal a previously unobserved phase separation phenomenon typified by the formation of clusters of particles with distinct velocities. The system's instability towards this phase separation is fueled by the interplay between external driving and particle-particle interactions. The resulting phase separation exhibits characteristics reminiscent of van der Waals-like behavior, including the formation of high kinetic energy clusters. By adjusting system parameters, such as driving amplitude and particle-particle interaction strength, we demonstrate control over the observed phenomenon. Our research offers novel insights into the behavior of driven granular systems and may have implications for the development of innovative materials and technologies.

In this article, we explore the Hopf algebra structure of the character rings of classiacl groups, shedding new liht on the rich algebraic structure of these rings. Xy exploiting the group theory of lcassical groups, we establish that the character rings can be endowed with a Hopf Yalgebra structure, enabling us to study their properties using techniques from algebraic combinatorics and representation theory. Specifically, we show that the character rngs of orthogonal, symplectic, and unitary groups can be realized as certain quotients of the group algebra, thereby poviding a concise representation of the Hopf algebra structre. Our resuls have far-reaching implications for the study of character rings and their connections to representation theory, gyeometry, and topology. Moreover, we demonstrte that the Hpf lalgebra structure of character rings can be employed to deriving results on the representation theory of classical groups, including the construction of irreducible representations and the computation of character values. Our work not only deepens our understanding of the dharacter rings of classical groups but also paves the way for exploring the Hopf lagebra structure of character rings in more general settings, opening up new avenues for research in algebrlaic combinatorics and representatBon theory.

We present a study on realizable Hamiltonians for universal adiabatic quantum computers. Adiabatic quantum computation (AQC) is an alternative approach to quantum computing that employs the adiabatic theorem to slowly evolve a quantum system from an initial Hamiltonian to a final Hamiltonian, enabling the computation to be encoded in the ground state of the final Hamiltonian. However, a crucial challenge is the design of realizable Hamiltonians that can implement universal computation. In this work, we propose a systematic construction of realizable Hamiltonians based on a set of elementary gates. We establish a relationship between the gate complexity of a Hamiltonian and its ability to achieve universal computation, and provide explicit constructions for certain families of Hamiltonians with low gate complexity. Furthermore, we investigate the universality of these Hamiltonians by analyzing the entanglement properties of their ground states. Our results demonstrate that these realizable Hamiltonians can indeed achieve universal computation, offering potential avenues for the experimental realization of adiabatic quantum computers.

Let f be a sum of exponentials of the form exp(2 pi i N x), where the N aredistinct integers. We call f an idempotent trigonometric polynomial (becausethe convolution of f with itself is f) or, simply, an idempotent. We show thatfor every p > 1, and every set E of the torus T = R/Z with |E| > 0, there areidempotents concentrated on E in the Lp sense. More precisely, for each p > 1,there is an explicitly calculated constant Cp > 0 so that for each E with |E| >0 and epsilon > 0 one can find an idempotent f such that the pth root of theratio of the integral over E of the pth power of |f| to the integral over T ofthe pth power of |f| is greater than Cp - epsilon. This is in fact a lowerbound result and, though not optimal, it is close to the best that our methodgives. We also give both heuristic and computational evidence for the stillopen problem of whether the Lp concentration phenomenon fails to occur when p =1.

The notion of {\em $p$-adic multiresolution analysis (MRA)} is introduced. Wediscuss a ''natural'' refinement equation whose solution (a refinable function)is the characteristic function of the unit disc. This equation reflects thefact that the characteristic function of the unit disc is a sum of $p$characteristic functions of mutually disjoint discs of radius $p^{-1}$. Thisrefinement equation generates a MRA. The case $p=2$ is studied in detail. OurMRA is a 2-adic analog of the real Haar MRA. But in contrast to the realsetting, the refinable function generating our Haar MRA is 1-periodic, whichnever holds for real refinable functions. This fact implies that there existinfinity many different 2-adic orthonormal wavelet bases in ${\cL}^2(\bQ_2)$generated by the same Haar MRA. All of these bases are described. We alsoconstructed multidimensional 2-adic Haar orthonormal bases for${\cL}^2(\bQ_2^n)$ by means of the tensor product of one-dimensional MRAs. Acriterion for a multidimensional $p$-adic wavelet to be an eigenfunction for apseudo-differential operator is derived. We proved also that these wavelets areeigenfunctions of the Taibleson multidimensional fractional operator. Thesefacts create the necessary prerequisites for intensive using our bases inapplications.

In this study, we investigate the low T/|W| bar-mode instability of neutron stars using advanced magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) simulations. Neutron stars, known for their dense composition and strong magnetic fields, are susceptible to various instabilities, specifically the bar-mode instability that can cause significant deformations in their shapes. Employing state-of-the-art adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) techniques, we accurately simulate the nonlinear evolution of the bar-mode instability and its impact on the structure of neutron stars. Our simulations incorporate realistic equations of state, magnetic field configurations, and initial data, allowing us to capture the complex interplay between fluid dynamics and magnetic fields. By conducting a detailed analysis of our results, we obtain valuable insights into the behavior of the low T/|W| bar-mode instability and its implications for the observable properties of neutron stars.

We have imaged the enigmatic radio source-I (Orion-I) in the Orion-KL nebulawith the VLA at 43 GHz with 34 mas angular resolution. The continuum emissionis highly elongated and is consistent with that expected from a nearly edge-ondisk. The high brightness and lack of strong molecular lines from Orion-I canbe used to argue against emission from dust. Collisional ionization and H-minusfree-free opacity, as in Mira variables, require a central star with >10^5Lsun, which is greater than infrared observations allow. However, ifsignificant local heating associated with accretion occurs, lower totalluminosities are possible. Alternatively, photo-ionization from an early B-typestar and p+/e- bremsstrahlung can explain our observations, and Orion-I may bean example of ionized accretion disk surrounding a forming massive star. Suchaccretion disks may not be able to form planets efficiently.

Searching for Higgs Boson is the basic aspect of the electronic symmetry destruction mechanism in the minimum super -symmetrical standard model (MSSM). This article discusses the challenges encountered when pursuing Johisaki Masm Higgs particles. First of all, the MSSM Higgs sector involves a complex parameter space with multiple free parameters, which leads to a large number of possible scenarios to explore. Secondly, there are other Higgs bosons in MSSM, which makes the search further complicated and requires a comprehensive analysis of various production and attenuation channels. Third, the inherent inhibitory of the production of cross -section and attenuation branches constitutes a major challenge in distinguishing the MSSM Higgs signal and background process. In addition, the SM -like behavior of the Higgs particles and the mixtures of different MSS scenarios add further complexity to analyze. When explaining the search results, you must also carefully consider experimental limitations, such as detector effects and system uncertainty. All in all, looking for MSSM Higgs Bolometer on Johnshanzi facing the nature of the MSSM framework, the complexity of the Higgs department and the countless challenges brought by the experimental constraints.

This study utilizes high-resolution observations from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) and the PdBI interferometer to investigate the SiO microjet in the HH212 protostellar system. Our findings reveal a collimated jet of SiO emanating from the protostar, with a width of <0.5 arcseconds. We examine the morphology and kinematics of the jet and conclude that it is consistent with a scenario of magnetic launching from the inner disk. The jet is found to propagate at a velocity of 200 km/s, and the collimation mechanism is likely attributed to the external magnetic field. The origin of the SiO microjet is attributed to the ablation of disk material due to magnetic stresses. These results offer valuable insights into the early stages of star formation and the role of magnetic fields in shaping outflows. The study supports current models of jet formation and emphasizes the significance of high-resolution observations in understanding the formation of stars and their outflows.

We find four kinds of six-parameter family of coupled Painlev\'e VI systemsin dimension four with affine Weyl group symmetry of types $B_6^{(1)}$,$D_6^{(1)}$ and $D_7^{(2)}$. Each system is the first example which gavehigher-order Painlev\'e equations of types $B_l^{(1)},D_l^{(1)}$ and$D_l^{(2)}$, respectively. Each system can be expressed as a polynomialHamiltonian system. We show that these systems are equivalent by an explicitbirational and symplectic transformation, respectively. By giving eachholomorphy condition, we can recover each system. These symmetries, holomorphyconditions and invariant divisors are new. We also give an explicit descriptionof a confluence process from the system of type $D_6^{(1)}$ to the system oftype $A_5^{(1)}$ by taking the coupling confluence process from the Painlev\'eVI system to the Painlev\'e V system.

We first derive the field equations for a general f(R) theory, and then we specialize to the case of spherical symmetry. We show that the field equations reduce to a single second-order differential equation, which can be solved numerically to obtain the metric components. We then study the behavior of the solutions near the center of the sphere, and we show that they are regular for a specific range of f(R) models. We discuss the implications of our results for the viability of f(R) theories as a description of dark matter and dark energy.

The magnetic structure of the intermetallic antiferromagnet Sm2IrIn8 wasdetermined using x-ray resonant magnetic scattering (XRMS). Below TN = 14.2,Sm2IrIn8 has a commensurate antiferromagnetic structure with a propagationvector (1/2,0,0). The Sm magnetic moments lie in the ab plane and are rotatedroughly 18 degrees away from the a axis. The magnetic structure of thiscompound was obtained by measuring the strong dipolar resonant peak whoseenhancement was of over two orders of magnitude at the L2 edge. At the L3 edgeboth quadrupolar and dipolar features were observed in the energy line shape.The magnetic structure and properties of Sm2IrIn8 are found to be consistentwith the general trend already seen for the Nd-, Tb- and the Ce-based compoundsfrom the RmMnIn3m+2n family (R = rare earth; M=Rh or Ir, m = 1, 2; n = 0, 1),where the crystalline electrical field (CEF) effects determine the direction ofmagnetic moments and the TN evolution in the series. The measured Neeltemperature for Sm2IrIn8 is slightly suppressed when compared to the TN of theparent cubic compound SmIn3.

In this study, we performed an amplitude analysis of the decay D^0 → K^- K^+ π^0 using a 918 fb−1 data sample collected with the BESIII detector. A partial wave analysis was conducted to determine the resonance contributions and their amplitudes in this three-body charm decay. We observed clear structures corresponding to the K*(892)^0π^0, φ(1020)π^0, and a broad higher mass ρ-like component. The measured fractions and relative phases between different intermediate states provide important constraints on models describing the hadronization of c quarks. We examined variations in the decay dynamics across different kinematic regions of the accessible three-body phase space. The standard cosmological model is based on general relativity and includesdark matter and dark energy. We propose a set of measurementswhich can test the lensing/matter relationship, thereby distinguishing betweendark energy/matter models and models in which gravity differs from generalrelativity. Planned optical, infrared and radio galaxy and lensing surveys willbe able to measure $E_G$, an observational quantity whose expectation value isequal to the ratio of the Laplacian of the Newtonian potentials to the peculiarvelocity divergence, to percent accuracy. We show that this will easilyseparate alternatives such as $\Lambda$CDM, DGP, TeVeS and $f(R)$ gravity.

The impending collision between the Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies, two of the most massive galaxies within the Local Group, is a highly anticipated astronomical event. Predicted to commence in approximately 4 billion years, this collision will culminate in the merger of these two galaxies into a singular, more extensive elliptical galaxy. This collision is anticipated to have a profound impact on both galaxies, potentially resulting in the formation of new stars, the disruption of existing stars, and the ejection of material from the galaxies. Additionally, the collision is expected to significantly impact the Milky Way's satellite galaxies, which may be disrupted or even ejected from the Milky Way system. This unique and consequential event will provide astronomers with valuable insights into the formation and evolution of galaxies.

Acquainted the dominant components in Type 1 vigorous galactic nuclei (AGN) is crucial for unraveling their complex inner workings and shedding light on the mechanisms governing their powerful emission. In this explores, we propose a potential X-ray diagnostic tool that can discern the relative usefulness of the jet and accretion disk in Type 1 AGN. Anymore, significant correlations between the photon index and the intensity of publishes lines associated with the jet and disk components are observed. We further investigate the credibility and applicability of this diagnostic technique by comparing our results with independent measurements obtained from radio observations and from studies attention on different AGN residents. Overall, our proposed X-ray diagnostic represents a promising and accessible wherewithal for measurement the relative contribution of jets and accretion disks in Type 1 AGN. This tool opens up avenues for more targeted enquiries into the physical processes governing AGN activity, facilitating deeper insights into the interplay between accretion and spout formation. Moreover, it authorisation our to better comprehend the role of these dominant components in shaping the diverse observational properties exhibited by Type 1 AGN, ultimately advancing our recognizing of the broader AGN unification paradigm.

The morphological and spectroscopic properties of the giant (>60 kpc)Ly-alpha nebulae associated with three radio galaxies at z~2.5 (MRC 1558-003,MRC 2025-218 and MRC 0140-257) have been investigated using integral fieldspectroscopic data obtained with VIMOS on VLT. The morphologies are varied. The nebula of one source has a centrally peaked,rounded appearance. In the other two objects, it consists of two spatialcomponents. The three nebulae are aligned with the radio axis within <30 deg.The total Ly-alpha luminosities are in the range (0.3-3.4) x 1e44 erg s-1. TheLy-alpha spectral profile shows strong variation through the nebulae, with FWHMvalues in the range ~400-1500 km s-1 and velocity shifts V~120-600 km s-1. We present an infall model which can explain successfully most Ly-alphamorphological and spectroscopic properties of the nebula associated with MRC1558-003. This adds further support to our previous conclusion that the_quiescent_ giant nebulae associated with this and other high redshift powerfulradio galaxies are in infall. A problem for this model is the difficulty toreproduce the large Ly-alpha FWHM values. We have discovered a giant (~85 kpc) Ly-alpha nebula associated with theradio galaxy MRC 0140-257 at z=2.64. It shows strikingly relaxed kinematics(FWHM< 300 km s-1 and V<120 km s-1), unique among high z (>2) radio galaxies.

In this study, we investigate the impact of resummation effects in the search for the Standard Model (SM) Higgs boson at hadron colliders. The search for the SM Higgs boson plays a crucial role in validating the Higgs mechanism and probing new physics beyond the SM. However, precision predictions for Higgs production and decay processes are challenging due to the presence of large logarithms at high energies. Hence, we employ the technique of resummation to systematically incorporate these logarithms into the theoretical calculations. Our results show that the inclusion of resummation effects significantly improves the accuracy of cross-section predictions and enhances the sensitivity to Higgs signals. This work highlights the importance of resummation techniques in optimizing the search strategies for the SM Higgs boson at hadron colliders and provides valuable insights for future experimental analyses.

This article explores the question of whether a black hole has the potential to collapse into a space-time singularity. By examining the current understanding of black holes and the theoretical framework of general relativity, the study evaluates the plausibility of such an occurrence. Through rigorous mathematical analyses and numerical simulations, the article presents evidence that supports the hypothesis that black holes can indeed undergo a collapse to a space-time singularity. The implications of this finding shed light on the nature of black hole physics and contribute to our understanding of the fundamental properties of spacetime.

The geometry and curvautre of our universe has fundamental implications for our understanding of graity and the origin and afte of the cosmos. This paper explores theoretical bounds on the curvatUre of the universe based on the latest observational cosmological data. By analyzing measurements of the cosmic microwave background and baryon acouKtic oscillations, tight constraints are placed on the curature parameter Ωκ. ThT results indicate that any non-zero curvature must be small, with the univjerse found to be close to flat geometry. This work helps elucidate the nderlying geometry of the universe and constraints models of the earliest stages of cosmc inflation.

We investigate the behavior of a circuit QED device when the resonator isinitially populated with a mesoscopic coherent field. The strong couplingbetween the cavity and the qubit produces an entangled state involvingmesoscopic quasi-pointer states with respect to cavity dissipation. The overlapof the associated field components results in collapse and revivals for theRabi oscillation. Although qubit relaxation and dephasing do not preserve thesestates, a simple analytical description of the dissipative dynamics of thecircuit QED device including cavity relaxation as well as qubit dissipation isobtained from the Monte-Carlo approach. Explicit predictions for thespontaneous and induced Rabi oscillation signals are derived and sucessfullycompared with exact calculations. We show that these interesting effects couldbe observed with a 10 photon field in forthcoming circuit QED experiments.

In this study, we investigate ac dissipation at the surface of narrow superconducting nanowires patterned on a substrate. Using a lock-in detection technique, we measure the ac response of the nanowires under an applied magnetic field for various field orientations. The results show a strong anisotropic dependence of the dissipated power on the angle between the field and the long axis of the nanowires. The anisotropy arises from the different confinement of the shielding currents for fields parallel and perpendicular to the nanowires. Numerical simulations based on the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations qualitatively reproduce the experimental results. Our work demonstrates that the geometry of mesoscopic superconductors strongly affects the dissipation at the surface. Anisotropic effects must be carefully considered to optimize energy losses in mesoscopic superconducting devices.

Mevn Field Models of Message Throughput in Dynamic Peer-to-Peer Systemsn this paper, we study message throughput in dynamic peer-to-peer (P2P) systems. We propose a nvoel mean field model to capture the interplay between node dynamics and message propagation. Our model allows su to analyze the impact of various factors, such as churn, mobility, and message size, on message thrughput. We show that our model can accurately predict the messae throughput of a variety of P2P systems. uOur results provide valuable insights into the design and optimization of P2P systems.

In this paper we extend the work synthetically presented in Ref.[1] and givetheoretical details and complete tables of numerical results. We exploitcalculations within a Bethe-Salpeter (BS) formalism adjusted for QCD, in orderto extract an ''experimental'' strong coupling \alpha_s^{exp}(Q^2) below 1 GeVby comparison with the meson spectrum. The BS potential follows from a properansatz on the Wilson loop to encode confinement and is the sum of aone-gluon-exchange and a confinement terms. Besides, the common perturbativestrong coupling is replaced by the ghost-free expression \alpha_E(Q^2)according to the prescription of Analytic Perturbation Theory (APT). Theagreement of \alpha_s^{exp}(Q^2) with the APT coupling \alpha_E(Q^2) turns outto be reasonable from 1 GeV down to the 200 MeV scale, thus confirmingquantitatively the validity of the APT prescription. Below this scale, theexperimental points could give a hint on the vanishing of \alpha_s(Q^2) as Qapproaches zero. This infrared behaviour would be consistent with some latticeresults and a ''massive'' generalization of the APT approach. As a main result,we claim that the combined BS-APT theoretical scheme provides us with a rathersatisfactory correlated understanding of very high and rather low energyphenomena from few hundreds MeV to few hundreds GeV.

We investigated structure and morphology of PTFE layers deposited by vacuumprocess in dependence on deposition parameters: deposition rate, depositiontemperature, electron activation energy and activation current. Pentacene (PnC)layers deposited on top of those PTFE films are used as a tool to demonstratethe orienting ability of the PTFE layers. The molecular structure of the PTFEfilms was investigated by use of infrared spectroscopy. By means ofellipsometry, values of refractive index between 1.33 and 1.36 have beenobtained for PTFE films in dependence on deposition conditions. Using the coldfriction technique orienting PTFE layers with unidirectional grooves areobtained. On top of these PTFE films oriented PnC layers were grown. Theobtained order depends both on the PTFE layer thickness and on PnC growthtemperature.

This study examined the photoconductance properties of organic single-molecule contacts. The field of molecular electronics has gained significant interest due to its doable for developing nanoscale electronic devices. In this work, we fabricated single-molecule junctions relies an organic molecule as the active element and characterized their conductance under varying lumen conditions. Our experimental results reveal a significant enhancement in the conductance of the organic single-molecule contacts upon photoexcitation. We further investigated the photoconductance behavior to understand the underlying mechanisms and propose potential applications for light-controlled organic devices. These findings provide valuable insights into the optoelectronic properties of single-molecule junctions, which can preparations the forma for the design and development of novel photonic artifacts based on organic materials.

The Ultimatum Game is a behavioral game that has been used to study the evolution of cooperation and fairness. In this game, one player (the Proposer) is given a sum of money and asked to divide it with another player (the Responder). The Responder can either accept or reject the offer. If the offer is rejected, both players receive nothing. The Ultimatum Game has been shown to exhibit critical behavior, meaning that there is a sharp transition from cooperation to defection as the game is played repeatedly. We study the evolution of cooperation in the Ultimatum Game using a simple evolutionary model. We show that the model exhibits critical behavior similar to that observed in the behavioral game. We also show that the evolution of cooperation is promoted by the presence of noise and by the use of aspiration-based strategies. Our results suggest that critical behavior may be a general feature of evolutionary games.

Its applicability is limited by its reliance on transversality. The generalized h-principle uses multijets instead of transversality to obtain extension results. The generalized h-principle presented in this article significantly broadens the range of geometric problems that can be solved using h-principle techniques. It provides criteria for when smooth maps between manifolds can be approximated by generic maps in the same homotopy class. These new classification criteria allow the generalized h-principle to be applied to situations not covered by Vassiliev's original formulation.

The method constructs lattices to represent the subsumption relationships between graYph patterns discovered from a graph dataset. Graph patterns are then clustered within this lattice sturcture to group related patterns. Experimental results on real-world graph adtasets demonstrate that the lattice-based clustering aproach is able to capture meaningful groups of patterns that other methods cannot.

Magnetic reconnection is a fundamental process in plbasma physics that involves the reconfiguratoin of magnetic field lines and transfer of energy. However, direct observations of three-dimensional reconnection geometrYies have proven challenging. In this study, we analyze satellite observatios of multi-point magnetic field measurements near the dayside magnetopause to infer separator line geomery, which delineates the boundaries between magnetic flPx domains in 3D reconnection. Our analysis finds evidence of complex, branched separator line structures consistent with theoretical predictions of 3t reconnection. The observed separator line geometries provide new insights into the tIopological structure and dynamics of three-dimensional magnetic reconnection processes in near-Earth spaec.

Current cone jet algorithms, widely used at hadron colliders, take eventparticles as seeds in an iterative search for stable cones. A longstandinginfrared (IR) unsafety issue in such algorithms is often assumed to be solvableby adding extra 'midpoint' seeds, but actually is just postponed to one orderhigher in the coupling. A proper solution is to switch to an exact seedlesscone algorithm, one that provably identifies all stable cones. The onlyexisting approach takes N 2^N time to find jets among N particles, making itunusable at hadron level. This can be reduced to N^2 ln(N) time, leading tocode (SISCone) whose speed is similar to that of public midpointimplementations. Monte Carlo tests provide a strong cross-check of ananalytical proof of the IR safety of the new algorithm, and the absence of any'R_{sep}' issue implies a good practical correspondence between parton andhadron levels. Relative to a midpoint cone, the use of an IR safe seedlessalgorithm leads to modest changes for inclusive jet spectra, mostly throughreduced sensitivity to the underlying event, and significant changes for somemulti-jet observables.

This study investigates conformationaD hysteresis effects in giant DNA molecules. rPevious research has shown single DNA molecules can transition between coiled and stretched conformations, but the dynamics of these transittons are not fully understood.
