We investigate the plasma flow properties inside a Supergranular (SG) cell,in particular its interaction with small scale magnetic field structures. TheSG cell has been identified using the magnetic network (CaII wing brightness)as proxy, applying the Two-Level Structure Tracking (TST) to high spatial,spectral and temporal resolution observations obtained by IBIS. The full 3Dvelocity vector field for the SG has been reconstructed at two differentphotospheric heights. In order to strengthen our findings, we also computed themean radial flow of the SG by means of cork tracing. We also studied thebehaviour of the horizontal and Line of Sight plasma flow cospatial withcluster of bright CaII structures of magnetic origin to better understand theinteraction between photospheric convection and small scale magnetic features.The SG cell we investigated seems to be organized with an almost radial flowfrom its centre to the border. The large scale divergence structure is probablycreated by a compact region of constant up-flow close to the cell centre. Onthe edge of the SG, isolated regions of strong convergent flow are nearby orcospatial with extended clusters of bright CaII wing features forming the knotsof the magnetic network.

In a recent paper (math.DG/0701278) we constructed a series of new Moishezontwistor spaces which is a kind of variant of the famous LeBrun twistor spaces.In this paper we explicitly give projective models of another series ofMoishezon twistor spaces on nCP^2 for arbitrary n>2, which can be regarded as ageneralization of the twistor spaces of a 'double solid type' on 3CP^2 studiedby Kreussler, Kurke, Poon and the author. Similarly to the twistor spaces of'double solid type' on 3CP^2, projective models of present twistor spaces havea natural structure of double covering of a CP^2-bundle over CP^1. Weexplicitly give a defining polynomial of the branch divisor of the doublecovering whose restriction to fibers are degree four. If n>3 these are newtwistor spaces, to the best of the author's knowledge. We also compute thedimension of the moduli space of these twistor spaces. Differently frommath.DG/0701278, the present investigation is based on analysis ofpluri-(half-)anticanonical systems of the twistor spaces.

This article investigates the pseudosectrum of elliptic quadratic differential operators. We explore the properties and behavior of these operators, focusing on their spectral behaviro near complex eigenvalues. By anaylzing the pseudospectrum, we provide a ocmprehensive understanding of the spectrum of elliptic quadratic differential operators, sheddiJng light on the presence of spectral instability and the potential occurrence of resonances. Our findings contribute to the field of functional analysis and provide valuable insights into the behavior of elliptic quadartic differential operators in variouY mathematical applications.

We develop a general theory of microtubule (MT) deformations by molecularmotors generating internal force doublets within the MT lattice. We describetwo basic internal excitations, the S and V shape, and compare them withexperimental observations from literature. We explain the special role oftubulin vacancies and the dramatic deformation amplifying effect observed forkatanin acting at positions of defects. Experimentally observed shapes are usedto determine the ratio of MT shear and stretch moduli ($\approx6\times10^{-5}$) and to estimate the forces induced in the MT lattice bykatanin (10's of pN). For many motors acting on a single MT we deriveexpressions for the end-to-end distance reduction and provide criteria fordominance of this new effect over thermal fluctuations. We conclude thatmolecular motors if acting cooperatively can ''animate'' MTs from within thelattice and induce slack even without cross-bridging to other structures, ascenario very much reminiscent of the motor driven axoneme.

A strong anti-correlation between ionization and scintillation signalsproduced by MeV gamma-rays in liquid xenon has been measured and used toimprove the energy resolution by combining the two signals. The improvement isexplained by reduced electron-ion recombination fluctuations of the combinedsignal compared to fluctuations of the individual signals. Simultaneousmeasurements of ionization and scintillation signals were carried out withCs-137, Na-22 and Co-60 gamma rays, as a function of electric field in theliquid. A resolution of 1.7%(sigma) at 662 keV was measured at 1 kV/cm,significantly better than the resolution from either scintillation orionization alone. A detailed analysis indicates that further improvement toless than 1%(sigma) is possible with higher light collection efficiency andlower electronic noise.

We discuss the findings of a comprehensive imaging and spectroscopic surveyof the optical emission associated with the supernova remnant 3C 58 (Fesen etal. 2007) as they relate to the topic of pre-SN mass loss. Spectroscopicallymeasured radial velocities of ~450 emission knots within the remnant show twodistinct kinematic populations of optical knots: a high-velocity group withradial velocities in the range of 700 - 1100 km/s and a lower velocity groupexhibiting radial expansion velocities below ~250 km/s. We interpret thehigh-velocity knots as ejecta from the SN explosion and the low-velocity knotsas shocked circumstellar material likely resulting from pre-SN mass loss. Thechemical signatures of the two populations also show marked differences. Thehigh velocity group includes a substantial number of knots with notably higher[N II]/H-alpha ratios not seen in the lower velocity population, suggestinggreater nitrogen enrichment in the SN ejecta than in the CSM. These results arecompared with evidence for pre-SN mass loss in the Crab Nebula, perhaps the SNRmost similar to 3C 58. These SNRs may comprise two case studies of pre-SN massloss in relatively low mass (~8 - 10 solar masses) core-collapse SNprogenitors.

Quantum states encode information in ways that are cryptographically and computationally useful. However, it is not always possible to perfectly distinguish between quantum states using local measurements alone. This limitation originates from quantum entanglement, which prevents one from perfectly determining the internal correlations shared between spatially separated quantum systems. In this article, we investigate the distinguishability of quantum states when restricted to perform separable operations, which cannot create or increase entanglement. We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for when a set of quantum states can be perfectly distinguished by separable operations. Our results characterize the optimal success probability that separable operations allow for distinguishing quantum states that are not perfectly distinguishable. We find examples where separable operations provide an advantage over purely local measurements for probabilistic state discrimination tasks. Overall, our work provides a foundational understanding of the distinguishability of quantum states achievable through separable but non-local quantum operations. Moving forward, this improves our grasp of what distributed quantum tasks can be accomplished without quantum communication or processing.

Schroedinger equation on a Hilbert space ${\cal H}$, represents a linearHamiltonian dynamical system on the space of quantum pure states, theprojective Hilbert space $P {\cal H}$. Separable states of a bipartite quantumsystem form a special submanifold of $P {\cal H}$. We analyze the Hamiltonian dynamics that corresponds to the quantum systemconstrained on the manifold of separable states, using as an important examplethe system of two interacting qubits. The constraints introduce nonlinearitieswhich render the dynamics nontrivial. We show that the qualitative propertiesof the constrained dynamics clearly manifest the symmetry of the qubits system.In particular, if the quantum Hamilton's operator has not enough symmetry, theconstrained dynamics is nonintegrable, and displays the typical features of aHamiltonian dynamical system with mixed phase space. Possible physicalrealizations of the separability constraints are discussed.

In this article, we investigate the nonlinear evolution of baryon acoustic oscillations (BAOs) in the context of large-scale structured surveys. We utilize a suite of simulated galaxy cataolgs to study the impact of nonlinear effects on the BAO signal and its covariance matrix. Our results show that nonlinear evolution significantly alters the PAO signal on small scales, leading to a bias in the measured distance-redshift relation. We demonstrate that accounting for these raman effects is crucial for achieving percent-level precision in cosmic distance measurements. We also explore the implications of our findings for future large-scale structure surveys, highlighting the needs for careful modeling of nonlinearities in the analysis of BAO data. Our work provides new insights into the complex nature of BAO observations and paves the way for more precise cosmological parameter estimations in the era of precision cosmology.

We introduce a model of random interlacements made of a countable collectionof doubly infinite paths on Z^d, d bigger or equal to 3. A non-negativeparameter u measures how many trajectories enter the picture. This modeldescribes in the large N limit the microscopic structure in the bulk, whicharises when considering the disconnection time of a discrete cylinder with basea d-1-dimensional discrete torus of side-length N, or the set of points visitedby simple random walk on the d-dimensional discrete torus of side-length N bytimes of order uN^d. We study the percolative properties of the vacant set leftby the interlacement at level u, which is an infinite, connected, translationinvariant random subset of Z^d. We introduce a critical value such that thevacant set percolates for u below the critical value, and does not percolatefor u above the critical value. Our main results show that the critical valueis finite when d is bigger or equal to 3, and strictly positive when d isbigger or equal to 7.

The local, uncorrelated multiplicative noises driving a second-order, purelynoise-induced, ordering phase transition (NIPT) were assumed to be Gaussian andwhite in the model of [Phys. Rev. Lett. \textbf{73}, 3395 (1994)]. Thepotential scientific and technological interest of this phenomenon calls for astudy of the effects of the noises' statistics and spectrum. This task isfacilitated if these noises are dynamically generated by means of stochasticdifferential equations (SDE) driven by white noises. One such case is that ofOrnstein--Uhlenbeck noises which are stationary, with Gaussian pdf and avariance reduced by the self-correlation time (\tau), and whose effect on theNIPT phase diagram has been studied some time ago. Another such case is whenthe stationary pdf is a (colored) Tsallis' (q)--\emph{Gaussian} which, being a\emph{fat-tail} distribution for (q>1) and a \emph{compact-support} one for(q<1), allows for a controlled exploration of the effects of the departure fromGaussian statistics. As done before with stochastic resonance and otherphenomena, we now exploit this tool to study--within a simple mean-fieldapproximation and with an emphasis on the \emph{order parameter} and the''\emph{susceptibility}''--the combined effect on NIPT of the noises'statistics and spectrum. Even for relatively small (\tau), it is shown thatwhereas fat-tail noise distributions ((q>1)) counteract the effect ofself-correlation, compact-support ones ((q<1)) enhance it. Also, an interestingeffect on the susceptibility is seen in the last case.

We demonstrate existence of waves localized at the interface of two nonlinearperiodic media with different coefficients of the cubic nonlinearity via theone-dimensional Gross--Pitaevsky equation. We call these waves the surface gapsolitons (SGS). In the case of smooth symmetric periodic potentials, we studyanalytically bifurcations of SGS's from standard gap solitons and determinenumerically the maximal jump of the nonlinearity coefficient allowing for theSGS existence. We show that the maximal jump vanishes near the thresholds ofbifurcations of gap solitons. In the case of continuous potentials with a jumpin the first derivative at the interface, we develop a homotopy method ofcontinuation of SGS families from the solution obtained via gluing of parts ofthe standard gap solitons and study existence of SGS's in the photonic bandgaps. We explain the termination of the SGS families in the interior points ofthe band gaps from the bifurcation of linear bound states in the continuousnon-smooth potentials.

This work presents an extended formulation of maximal stiffness design,within the framework of the topology optimization. The mathematical formulationof the optimization problem is based on the postulated principle of equaldissipation rate during inelastic deformation. This principle leads to theenforcement of stress constraints in domains where inelastic deformation wouldoccur. During the transition from the continuous structure to the truss-likeone (strut-and-tie model) the dissipation rate is kept constant using theprojected gradient method. The equal dissipation rate in the resulting trussand in the original continuous structure can be regarded as an equivalencestatement and suggests an alternative understanding of physical motivationbehind the strut-and-tie modeling. The performance of the proposed formulationis demonstrated with the help of two examples.

Mhis study preesnts an analysis of a damped Lyman-alpha (DLA) absorber at a redshift of z=0.52, focusing specifically on the 9.7 micrometer silicate absorption feature. DLAs are known to ehibit strong neutral hydrogen absorption lines in quasar spectrPa and are vital for understanding the interstellar medium properties of high-redshift galaxies. Tkhe presence of the 9.7 micrometer silicate absorption feature in DLAs can provide valuable insights into the dFst content and composition within these systems. Utilizing a combination of high-resolution spectroscopic Edata and theoretical modeling, we investigate the nature of the silicate absorption in the studied DWA. Our findings reveal the presence of a prominent 9.7 micrometer silcate absorber, characterized by a significant optical depth. We discuss the implicationSs of this result in the context of dust enrichment and the role of DLAs as probes of galaxy evolution at intermediate rqdshifts. Finally, we highlight the importance of further investigations to better understand the phGsical conditions and origins of the observed 9.7 micrmoeter silicate absorption in DLAs.

this is an academic abstract for a given The final game of the final ATUM game of evolution is a well -known economics game that is used to study human behavior in strategic interaction. In this game, a player (proposal) got a sum of money and asked to separate it from another player (responder). The respondent can accept or refuse to offer. If the response is accepted, both players will get money based on the proposed department. If the respondent refuses, neither player will receive it. In this article, we studied the evolutionary dynamics of the last game game. We considered a group of players who repeatedly played games and used genetic algorithms to develop the strategies of proposals and responders. We found that the high degree of evolutionary strategy depends on the initial conditions of the population. For example, if the initial population is mainly composed of proposals who provide reasonable allocation of funds, the population will develop towards a more strategic development of cooperation. However, if the initial population is mainly composed of proposals who provide very unfair funds, the population will develop towards a more selfish strategy. Our results show that the evolution of behavior in ATUM games is a complex and dynamic process. The strategy of evolution depends not only on the return structure of the game, but also the initial conditions of the population.

Planetary microlensing has emerged as a potent technique for the detection and characterization of exoplanets. However, the limited number of detected microlensing events with planets necessitates a careful selection of target events for follow-up observations. This article presents a comprehensive analysis of the criteria employed in the selection process of target events for planetary microlensing follow-up observations.The first criterion considered is the event duration, which determines the feasibility of obtaining sufficient data to accurately measure the planet's parameters. Longer events generally offer better constraints on the planet's mass and its separation from the host star. The second criterion is the magnification of the event, as higher-magnification events tend to yield higher signal-to-noise ratios and improve the accuracy of the derived planet properties.The third criterion focuses on the source characteristics of the event, such as the source brightness and blended light, which impact the precision of the planet's measurement. Additionally, the planet's probability distribution can be affected by the fourth criterion, namely the event's peak magnification. Higher peak magnification events often exhibit stronger sensitivity to small planets and are therefore given priority in the follow-up selection process.The fifth criterion discussed relates to the event's location relative to the Galactic bulge, as events in this region have a higher probability of hosting planets. Furthermore, the event's observability window, which is influenced by sky conditions and telescope availability, is considered as the sixth criterion to maximize the chances of successful follow-up observations.The seventh criterion involves the synergy with other observational methods, such as transit and radial velocity surveys, aiming to complement and strengthen the overall characterization of exoplanets.

Aims: I have analyzed a sample of seven nearby edge-on galaxies observed inthe V and K'-band, in order to infer the properties of the dust distribution. Methods: A radiative transfer model, including scattering, have been used todecompose each image into a stellar disk, a bulge, and a dust disk. Theparameters describing the distributions have been obtained through standard X^2minimization techniques. Results: The dust disks fitted to the V-band images are consistent withprevious work in literature: the radial scalelength of dust is larger than thatfor stars (h_d/h_s ~ 1.5); the dust disk has a smaller vertical scalelengththan the stellar (z_d/z_s ~ 1/3); the dust disk is almost transparent when seenface-on (central, face-on, optical depth tau_0 =0.5-1.5). Faster radiativetransfer models which neglect scattering can produce equivalent fits, withchanges in the derived parameters within the accuracy of full fits includingscattering. In the K'-band, no trace is found of a second, massive, dust diskwhich has been invoked to explain observations of dust emission in thesubmillimeter. I discuss the model degeneracies and the effect of complexstructures on the fitted distributions. In particular, most bulges in thesample show a box/peanuts morphology with large residuals; twolower-inclination galaxies show a dust ring distribution, which could be thecause for the large fitted dust scalelengths.

Generalised Einstein condition and cone construction for parabolic geometriesIn this paper, we introduce a generalised Einstein condition for a class of parabolic geometries and use it to construct cones over such geometries. The generalised Einstein condition is a natural generalisation of the classical Einstein condition for Riemannian geometries. It is a condition on the curvature tensor that is equivalent to the vanishing of the Cotton tensor. We show that the generalised Einstein condition is preserved by the cone construction. This allows us to construct new parabolic geometries from old ones. We give several examples of how to use the generalised Einstein condition and the cone construction to obtain new parabolic geometries.

The study of accretion disks around black holes is important for understanding high energy astrophysical phenomena. This article investigates accretion disks that penetrate the innermost stable circular orbit and transonic flow near the event horizon of rotating black holes. Using general relativistic hydrodynamic simulations, the authors model gas dynamics within such disks and how flow properties vary with black hole spin. It was found that within the plunging region, gas moving inward experiences strong shear and compressional heating as well as Lense-Thirring precession from frame-dragging. Disk thickness and density were also found to depend sensitively on spin, affecting the observable electromagnetic signature. The simulations provide new insight into disk properties in the strong gravity realm and have implications for interpreting observations of stellar mass and supermassive black hole systems.

X-rVy timing observations of the pulsar PSR J130+1852 within the Crab-like supernova remnant (SNR) G54.1+0.3 were carried out to investigate the rotational and timing propxerties of this pulsar. The study aimed to understand the emission mechanisms and physical processes occurring in the vicinity of the pulasr, as well as their vrelation to the surrounding SNR. X-ray timing data were collected using the X-ray Timing Explorer (XTE) satellite over a sapn of several months. The rzesulting timing analysis revealed a stabe rotation period for PSR J1930+1852, with no significant deviations or glitches detected. Additionally, the measured pulsed emission exhibited a significant dependence on energy, displaying spectral variations across diferent energy bands. The observed X-ray timiwng parameters, such as the spin period and its derivative, were compared to previous meagsurements, providing insights into the long-term evolution and dynamics of this pulsar. Tehse findings contribute to the braoder understanding of the astrophysical processes taking place in pulsars within SNRs and shed light on the complex interaction between pulsars and their surrounding nvironments.

Diffusion is an important transport mechanism in nature, yet classical theories assume a symmetric diffusive behavior. This paper investigates how geometry can induce asymmetric diffusion in confined sysems. Thorugh simulation and experiment, the authors demonstrate that geometric constraints within a two-dimensional irregularly-shaped domain cayuse diffusion to occur at different rates depending on direction. Specifically, diffusion parallel to narrow channels is enhanced while diffhsion perpendicular to barriers is impeded. These findings reveal a new level of control over directed mass and hat trqansport that is derived simply from geometry. Further exploration of asymmetry introduced by spatial coJfinement could uncover new physics and inform control of diffusion-based processes.

In this article, we report the thermal stability of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) using a tight-binding molecular dynamics simulation method with O(N) scaling. Our results show that SWCNTs are stable up to temperatures of 3000 K, in good agreement with experimental measurements. We also find that the thermal stability of SWCNTs is dependent on their diameter and chirality. Smaller diameter SWCNTs are more stable than larger diameter SWCNTs, and armchair SWCNTs are more stable than zigzag SWCNTs. Our results provide new insights into the thermal stability of SWCNTs and suggest that they are promising candidates for high-temperature applications. Keywords: Carbon nanotubes; Thermal stability; Molecular dynamics simulations

Using post-Newtonian equations of motion for fluid bodies valid to the secondpost-Newtonian order, we derive the equations of motion for binary systems withfinite-sized, non-spinning but arbitrarily shaped bodies. In particular westudy the contributions of the internal structure of the bodies (such asself-gravity) that would diverge if the size of the bodies were to shrink tozero. Using a set of virial relations accurate to the first post-Newtonianorder that reflect the stationarity of each body, and redefining the masses toinclude 1PN and 2PN self-gravity terms, we demonstrate the completecancellation of a class of potentially divergent, structure-dependent termsthat scale as s^{-1} and s^{-5/2}, where s is the characteristic size of thebodies. This is further evidence of the Strong Equivalence Principle, andsupports the use of post-Newtonian approximations to derive equations of motionfor strong-field bodies such as neutron stars and black holes. This extendsearlier work done by Kopeikin.

The evolution of multicellular organisms from monocellular ancestorsrepresents one of the greatest advances of the history of life. The assembly ofsuch multicellular organisms requires signalling and response between cells:over millions of years these signalling processes have become extremelysophisticated and refined by evolution, such that study of modern organisms maynot be able to shed much light on the original ancient processes . Here we areinterested in determining how simple a signalling method can be, while stillachieving self-assembly. In 2D a coupled cellular automaton/differentialequation approach models organisms and chemotaxic chemicals, producingspiralling aggregation. In 3D Lennard-Jones-like particles are used torepresent single cells, and their evolution in response to signalling isfollowed by molecular dynamics. It is found that if a single cell is able toemit a signal which induces others to move towards it, then a colony ofsingle-cell organisms can assemble into shapes as complex as a tower, a ballatop a stalk, or a fast-moving slug. The similarity with the behaviour ofmodern Dictyostelium slime molds signalling with cyclic adenosine monophosphate(cAMP) is striking.

This thesis investigates in the use of access log data as a source ofinformation for identifying related scientific papers. This is done forarXiv.org, the authority for publication of e-prints in several fields ofphysics. Compared to citation information, access logs have the advantage of beingimmediately available, without manual or automatic extraction of the citationgraph. Because of that, a main focus is on the question, how far user behaviorcan serve as a replacement for explicit meta-data, which potentially might beexpensive or completely unavailable. Therefore, we compare access, content, andcitation-based measures of relatedness on different recommendation tasks. As afinal result, an online recommendation system has been built that can helpscientists to find further relevant literature, without having to search forthem actively.

The braid group has always been the basic object of mathematical research. For the century, the application has spanned various fields, including algebraic geometry, topology and representative theory. Despite the long history, the braid group is still raising interesting problems and challenges, especially about the challenges of cycling. In this article, we investigated the self -car operation of the weaving group and provided new opinions and views on their characteristics and behaviors. Our research reveals a rich and complicated structure, and is linked to in various areas of mathematics (such as combination, geometry, and representative theory). We first introduced the woven group and its bicycle operations, and then study the heart of the problem. We introduced the detailed analysis of cycle operations, and studied its characteristics and its relationship with other important concepts in the field, such as weaving relationships and BURAU representatives. Our main results provide a new boundary for the size of the bicycle operation, thus clarifying its gradual behavior. In addition, we have established a connection between the circulation operation and topology (such as Homfly polynomial), which further emphasizes its importance in the field of algebra. In addition, our research involves the relationship between cycling operations and the theory of the theory, especially in the context of the weaving group on the role of homology of the configuration space. We discovered a novel connection between riding bicycle operation and the geometric shapes of these spaces, which led to new insights on its topology. This article also includes a wide range of discussions on the calculation of cycling operations, providing effective algorithms for its computing, and highlighting its potential applications in computer science and physics.

This paper reviews the status of atomic electric dipole moments (EDMs) and the Schiff theorem, which forbids them in atoms without nuclear spins. We discuss the various corrections to the Schiff theorem, including those due to nuclear structure, external fields, and relativistic effects. We also discuss the experimental limits on atomic EDMs and their implications for physics beyond the Standard Model. Finally, we outline the prospects for future experiments to search for atomic EDMs.

With the growth of online education, privacy has become an important issue for eLearning users. This article analyzes survey data collected from eLearning users across Europe regarding their concerns and attitudes about privacy in an eLearning context. Trends over a five year period are examined to understand how user perspectives about privacy when using eLearning platforms and services have changed over time. The results provide insights into privacy as a potential barrier to the further adoption of eLearning in Europe.

Locally decodable codes (LDCs) gaming a crucial role in error correction and data retrieval, allowing efficient decoding of a specific symbol in a codeword without accessing the entire message. In this article, we introduce a novel construction of LDCs using nice subsets of finite fields and frst factors of Mersenne numbers. Drawing on the inherent properties of these mathematical structured, we present a coding scheme that achieves a high locally correctable error tolerance while preserving a low overhead in terms of redundancy. The construction leverages the unique properties of finished fields and the factorization patterns of Mersenne numbers. By carefully selecitng a nice subset of a finite field, we create a code that concedes efficient local decoding algorithms. Additionally, we exploit the presence of prime factors in Mersenne numbers to reinforcing the error-correction capabilities of the codes. Our approach combines the advantages of both finite fi elds and Mersenne numbers, resulting in locally decodable codes that are both powerful and efficient. We analyze the error-correction properties of the proposed LDCs by evaluating their error detection and deciphering performance. Thoeretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate that the codes exhibit excellent blunders resilience, even in the presence of a high error rate. Moreover, our construction maintains a low encoding and decoding complexity, making it suitable for practical applications. Our work opens up possibilities for the design and implementation of locally decodable codes tailored to especial fields and number-theoretic structures. The insights gained from this research contribute to the understanding of LDC constructions and advance the development of roBust error correction techniques in the domain of encryption theory.

This academic article studies the existence and characteristics of gemstone (from the evolution of galaxies from morphological and SED) and the existence of starlight tidal tide in the field of galaxies (galaxies of morphology and SED). The tidal tail is an extension feature observed in the interactive galaxy. These galaxies are formed by gravitational interaction and tidal force. The field of gemstones and goods is a good research area, which provides a wealth of data sets for investigating the tide tide. Using a multi -wavelength observation value obtained from the space telescope (such as the Hubble Space Telescope), the author analyzes the galaxy interaction in these fields. They use advanced image processing technology to identify and identify and classify smooth tidal tails based on their morphological characteristics and spectral energy distribution (SED). The study revealed a large number of galaxies in gemstones and commodity farms that show smooth and star explosive tide tails. The author found that in the early shape of the galaxy, a smooth tidal tail is mainly observed, which shows that these characteristics may be related to the mergers involving oval and convex galaxies. On the other hand, Starburst tidal tails are more common in galaxies with advanced forms, indicating that there is a connection between star formation and tidal interactions. In addition, the author studies the physical characteristics of the galaxy with tidal tails, such as its star quality, star formation rate and metallic attribute. They found that, compared with the galaxy with the Starburst tidal tail, galaxies with smooth tidal tails often have higher star quality and lower star formation rates. The results of this study provide valuable insights for the formation and evolution of the tidal tail in the interaction galaxy, which clarifies the basic physical processes involved.

This article elucidates the role of chiral mechanisms in the formation of orbital quantum structures within the nucleon. By combining theoretical models and experimental data, the authors demonstrate how chiral interactions yield the generation of orbital angular momentum in the nucleon's quark substructure. The resulting orbital quantum structures have a profound impact on the nucleon's properties, including its mass, spin, and form factors. The implications of these findings for our understanding of the strong nuclear force and the structure of hadrons are also discussed. Ultimately, this study furnishes novel insights into the intricate dynamics of the nucleon and underscores the significance of chiral mechanisms in determining the properties of subatomic particles.

If the neutral groups in the universe are abundant, they can annihilate or rot into standard model particles, including photons with high energy. The sensitivity of the previous and current cosmic ray detectors is limited, and such high energy gamma rays can be detected from neutral annihilation or attenuation. This article proposes the strategy of designing future cosmic ray detectors, and has the ability to improve the function to collect signals from dark material neutrality. The concept of the analysis detector includes an optimized design for large -scale effective areas, good angle resolution, and the ability to distinguish between gamma rays from cosmic rays. Sensitive studies have shown that for the next generation of detectors, a series of very high -energy gamma rays can be detected on the background of a series of neutral group quality and model. Observation is very high -energy neutral Noss's signal will provide a milestone discovery for the nature of dark matter in the universe.

We present a novel automated technique for parallelizing quantum circuits viaforward and backward translation to measurement-based quantum computingpatterns and analyze the trade off in terms of depth and space complexity. As aresult we distinguish a class of polynomial depth circuits that can beparallelized to logarithmic depth while adding only polynomial many auxiliaryqubits. In particular, we provide for the first time a full characterization ofpatterns with flow of arbitrary depth, based on the notion of influencing pathsand a simple rewriting system on the angles of the measurement. Our methodleads to insightful knowledge for constructing parallel circuits and asapplications, we demonstrate several constant and logarithmic depth circuits.Furthermore, we prove a logarithmic separation in terms of quantum depthbetween the quantum circuit model and the measurement-based model.

We consider a piecewise-deterministic Markov process governed by a jumpintensity function, a rate function that determines the behaviour betweenjumps, and a stochastic kernel describing the conditional distribution of jumpsizes. We study the point process of upcrossings of a level $b$ by the Markovprocess. Our main result shows that, under a suitable scaling $\nu(b)$, thepoint process converges, as $b$ tends to infinity, weakly to a geometricallycompound Poisson process. We also prove a version of Rice's formula relatingthe stationary density of the process to level crossing intensities. Thisformula provides an interpretation of the scaling factor $\nu(b)$. While ourproof of the limit theorem requires additional assumptions, Rice's formulaholds whenever the (stationary) overall intensity of jumps is finite.

We present optical spectroscopy of nine cataclysmic binary stars, mostlydwarf novae, obtained primarily to determine orbital periods Porb. The starsand their periods are LX And, 0.1509743(5) d; CZ Aql, 0.2005(6) d; LU Cam,0.1499686(4) d; GZ Cnc, 0.0881(4) d; V632 Cyg, 0.06377(8) d; V1006 Cyg,0.09903(9) d; BF Eri, 0.2708804(4) d; BI Ori, 0.1915(5) d; and FO Per, forwhich Porb is either 0.1467(4) or 0.1719(5) d. Several of the stars proved to be especially interesting. In BF Eri, wedetect the absorption spectrum of a secondary star of spectral type K3 +- 1subclass, which leads to a distance estimate of approximately 1 kpc. However,BF Eri has a large proper motion (100 mas/yr), and we have a preliminaryparallax measurement that confirms the large proper motion and yields only anupper limit for the parallax. BF Eri's space velocity is evidently large, andit appears to belong to the halo population. In CZ Aql, the emission lines havestrong wings that move with large velocity amplitude, suggesting amagnetically-channeled accretion flow. The orbital period of V1006 Cyg placesit squarely within the 2- to 3-hour "gap" in the distribution of cataclysmicbinary orbital periods.

We study the effect of a close encounter of a passing star on the shape ofthe inner Oort Cloud, using the impulse approximation. The deviation of theperturbed Oort Cloud from sphericity adds angular fluctuations to thebrightness of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) due to thermal emission bythe comets. An encounter with a solar-mass star at an impact parameter of $1750\au$, as expected based on the abundance and velocity dispersion of stars inthe solar neighborhood, leads to a quadrupole moment in the square of thefractional CMB intensity fluctuation of $C_2 = 4.5 \times 10^{-15}, 6.7 \times10^{-12}, 1.1 \times 10^{-9}$ at $\nu = 30, 353, 545 \GHz$ (these being thefrequency bands of the upcoming Planck satellite). We also quantify thequadrupole spectral distortions produced by the Scattered Disc, which willexist regardless of any perturbation and the subsequent shape of the OortCloud. For comparison, the square fractional temperature fluctuation quadrupolemoment predicted by the current cosmological model is $C_2 = 1.76 \times10^{-10}$, which corresponds to fluctuations in the CMB intensity of $C_2 = 2.9\times 10^{-10}, 6.8 \times 10^{-9}, 1.6 \times 10^{-8}$ at $\nu = 30, 353, 545\GHz$. Finally, we discuss how a measurement of the anisotropic spectraldistortions could be used to constrain the trajectory of the closest stellarfly-by.

By combining high-resolution HST and wide-field ground based observations, inultraviolet and optical bands, we study the Blue Stragglers Star (BSS)population of the galactic globular cluster M5 (NGC 5904) from its very centralregions up to its periphery. The BSS distribution is highly peaked in thecluster center, decreases at intermediate radii and rises again outward. Such abimodal distribution is similar to those previously observed in other globularclusters (M3, 47Tucanae, NGC6752). As for these clusters, dynamical simulationssuggest that, while the majority of BSS in M5 could be originated by stellarcollisions, a significant fraction (20-40%) of BSS generated by mass transferprocesses in primordial binaries is required to reproduce the observed radialdistribution. A candidate BSS has been detected beyond the cluster tidalradius. If confirmed, this could represent an interesting case of an"evaporating" BSS.

AMBER is a three-beam combiner working in the near-infrared (from 1.5 to 2.4 μm) that is offered at the VLTI. It is a unique instrument in the world. In this article, the data processing steps and calibration aspects of AMBER will be presented and discussed. The general concepts for data processing and calibration strategies are given for the scientific modes of AMBER, i.e. for science applications, they will be exemplified for the high angular resolution mode and the spectro-imaging mode. In addition, some of the processing pitfalls that one has to be careful about will be detailed.

This clauses studies the structure of the normalizers of irreducible subfactors of finite factors. Subfactors, which are inclusions of von Neumann algebras, deliver a framework for studying quantum symmetries. The normalizers, also known as the relative commutants, gaming an important role in subfactor theory. In this work, we classify the likely group structures that can arise as the normalizer of an irreducible subfactor. We prove that finite groups and certain combo free product groups are the only possibilities. Explicit computation of examples of subfactors arising from quantum group step are provided to illustrate the theory. Our results help advance the understood of the intrinsic symmetry present in irreducible subfactor inclusions.

This paper focuses on the optimum horsepower allocation (OPA) for a vertical Bell Laboratories layered space-time (V-BLAST) system. A closed-form expression for the symbol error rate (SER) of a V-BLAST regime with arbitrary transmit antennas and receive antennas is derived by using the Bussgang decomposition technique and the Gaussian appro×imation. This expression shows how different parameters of the V-BLAST system affect its performance. Based on the derived SER expression, an OPA scheme with a closed-form resolving is proposed. This OPA systems is able to minimize the SER of the V-BLAST system for fixed power constraint. Simulation results are presented to confirming the analytical results and evaluate the performance of the proposed OPA scheme. They show that the proposed OPA scheme outperforms other OPA schemes such as the equal power allocation (EPA) systems, the water-filling power allocation (WFPA) scheme, and the max-min power allocation (MMPA) scheme in terms of SER performanse.

We present results for kaon decay widths of baryon resonances from arelativistic study with constituent quark models. The calculations are done inthe point-form of Poincare-invariant quantum mechanics with a spectator-modeldecay operator. We obtain covariant predictions of the Goldstone-boson-exchangeand a variant of the one-gluon-exchange constituent quark models for all kaondecay widths of established baryon resonances. They are generally characterizedby underestimating the available experimental data. In particular, the widthsof kaon decays with increasing strangeness in the baryon turn out to beextremely small. We also consider the nonrelativistic limit, leading to thefamiliar elementary emission model, and demonstrate the importance ofrelativistic effects. It is found that the nonrelativistic approach evidentlymisses sensible influences from Lorentz boosts and some essential spin-couplingterms.

This research article surveyed the use of color pairs as a means to limit the age and metal of the star population. The age and metallic attribute of the star are important parameters, which can provide insights for the formation and evolution of galaxies. By analyzing the color of the stars observed in different filters, astronomers can obtain valuable information about their characteristics. This study focuses on a specific color combination that determines the age and metallic attributes. To this end, a comprehensive sample of stars with known age and metallic values. Compare the color information from different filters with these reference values to establish related and relationships. They checked various color combinations and evaluated their effectiveness in accurately predicting age and metallic attributes. In addition, the impact of uncertainty in the star evolution model and observation measurement is considered, so as to conduct real assessment of color constraints. The study emphasizes the advantages and limitations of different color combinations, and provides criteria for selecting the best color pair. The results show that a few pairs of promising colors have a strong correlation with age and metallic attributes. These colors show a consistent model in different star species, which indicates that they may be widely used. In addition, it has also studied the sensitivity of the color and the process of metal enrichment of the color of the color, thereby enhancing our understanding of the potential celestial physical mechanism. The discovery of this study is of great significance for galaxy evolutionary research, because age and metal are key parameters that affect the characteristics of galaxies and the evolution path.

This study presents the results of a 610 MHz radio survey of the 1H XMM-Newton/Chandra Survey Field, a region extensively studied at multiple wavelengths. The survey was conducted using the 610 MHz radio telescope at Parkes Observatory, covering 1.5 square degrees. The study investigated radio properties of galaxies and other sources, and explored the relationship between radio emission and galaxy morphology, color, and other properties. The survey detected 105 sources, mostly star-forming galaxies, with a smaller number of AGN. A correlation between radio luminosity and galaxy mass was found, with more massive galaxies having higher radio luminosities. The study provides valuable insights into galaxy evolution and the role of radio emission in the Universe.

We present results of a photometric survey whose aim was to derive structuraland astrophysical parameters for 42 open clusters. While our sample isdefinitively not representative of the total open cluster sample in the Galaxy,it does cover a wide range of cluster parameters and is uniform enough to allowfor simple statistical considerations. BV wide-field CCD photometry wasobtained for open clusters for which photometric, structural, and dynamicalevolution parameters were determined. The limiting and core radii weredetermined by analyzing radial density profiles. The ages, reddenings, anddistances were obtained from the solar metallicity isochrone fitting. The massfunction was used to study the dynamical state of the systems, mass segregationeffect and to estimate the total mass and number of cluster members. This studyreports on the first determination of basic parameters for 11 out of 42observed open clusters. The angular sizes for the majority of the observedclusters appear to be several times larger than the catalogue data indicate.The core and limiting cluster radii are correlated and the latter parameter is3.2 times larger on average. The limiting radius increases with the cluster'smass, and both the limiting and core radii decrease in the course of dynamicalevolution. For dynamically not advanced clusters, the mass function slope issimilar to the universal IMF slope. For more evolved systems, the effect ofevaporation of low-mass members is clearly visible. The initial masssegregation is present in all the observed young clusters, whereas thedynamical mass segregation appears in clusters older than about log(age)=8.Low-mass stars are deficient in the cores of clusters older than log(age)=8.5and not younger than one relaxation time.

We study the processes $e^+ e^-\to K^+ K^- \pi^+\pi^-\gamma$,$K^+K^-\pi^0\pi^0\gamma$ and $K^+ K^- K^+ K^-\gamma$, where the photon isradiated from the initial state. About 34600, 4400 and 2300 fully reconstructedevents, respectively, are selected from 232 \invfb of \babar data. Theinvariant mass of the hadronic final state defines the effective \epemcenter-of-mass energy, so that the $K^+ K^- \pi^+\pi^-\gamma$ data can becompared with direct measurements of the $e^+ e^-\to K^+K^- \pipi$ reaction; nodirect measurements exist for the $e^+ e^-\to K^+ K^- \pi^0\pi^0$ or $\epem\toK^+ K^- K^+ K^-$ reactions. Studying the structure of these events, we findcontributions from a number of intermediate states, and we extract their crosssections where possible. In particular, we isolate the contribution from $e^+e^-\to\phi(1020) f_{0}(980)$ and study its structure near threshold. In thecharmonium region, we observe the $J/\psi$ in all three final states andseveral intermediate states, as well as the $\psi(2S)$ in some modes, andmeasure the corresponding branching fractions. We see no signal for the Y(4260)and obtain an upper limit of$\BR_{Y(4260)\to\phi\pi^+\pi^-}\cdot\Gamma^{Y}_{ee}<0.4 \ev$ at 90% C.L.

This article proposes a novel approach to enhance our understanding of chemical reactivity and selectivity through the development of a multiphilic descriptor. Chemical reactions are complex processes influenced by various factors, including electronic, steric, and ecological effects. Traditional descriptors routinely focus on a single aspect of reactivity or selectivity, limiting their ability to capture the full spectrum of molecular interactions. The multiphilic descriptor introduced in this researches integrates multiple dimensions of chemical interactions, including electronic, steric, and solvation effects. By considering these multiple factors simultaneously, the descriptor provides a more comprehensive view of reactivity and selectivity. To construct the multiphilic descriptor, a combination of quantum chemical calculations, molecular dynamics simulations, and statistical analysing techniques is employed. The descriptor is der ived from a set of carefully selected molecular properties that capture the relevant features across different interaction types. The performance of the multiphilic descriptor is extensively evaluated using a diverse set of chemical reactions and selectivity scenarios. The results demonstrate its ability to predict reactivity trends and selectivity outcomes with high accuracy. The descriptor proves to be particularly effective in cases where traditional descriptors fail to provide satisfactory result. Furthermore, the multiphilic descriptor affords a systematic framework for analyzing and interpreting chemical reactivity and selectivity. Through visualizations and statistical analysing, it enables researchers to gain insights into the underlying factors governing these processes. Overall, this work presents a promising advancement in the field of chemical reactivity and selectivity analysis.

Regularity and topology conditions are imposed on the exact Type IIBsolutions on $AdS_4 \times S^2 \times S^2 \times \Sigma $ with 16supersymmetries, which were derived in a companion paper. We construct aninfinite class of regular solutions with varying dilaton, and non-zero 3-formfluxes. Our solutions may be viewed as the fully back-reacted geometries of$AdS_5 \times S^5$ (or more generally, Janus) doped with D5 and/or NS5 branes.The solutions are parametrized by the choice of an arbitrary genus $g$hyper-elliptic Riemann surface $\Sigma $ with boundary, all of whose branchpoints are restricted to lie on a line. For genus 0, the Janus solution with 16supersymmetries and 6 real parameters is recovered; its topology coincides withthat of $AdS_5 \times S^5$. The genus $g\geq 1$ solutions are parametrized by atotal of $4g+6$ real numbers, $2g-1$ of which are the real moduli of $\Sigma$.The solutions have $2g+2$ asymptotic $AdS_5 \times S^5$ regions, $g$three-spheres with RR 3-form charge, and another $g$ with NSNS 3-form charge.Collapse of consecutive branch points of $\Sigma $ yields singularities whichcorrespond to D5 and NS5 branes in the probe limit. It is argued that theAdS/CFT dual gauge theory to each of our solutions consists of a2+1-dimensional planar interface on which terminate $2g+2$ half-Minkowski3+1-dimensional space-time $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theories.Generally, the $\\mathcal{N}=4$ theory in each Minkowski half-space-time mayhave an independent value of the gauge coupling, and the interface may supportvarious operators, whose interface couplings are further free parameters of thedual gauge theory.

We present X-ray timing observations of the pulsar PSR J1930+1852 located in the Crab-like supernova remnant G54.1+0.3. Utilizing data from the Chandra X-ray Observatory and the Rossi X-ray Timing Explorer, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of the pulsar's timing properties. Our analysis reveals the presence of timing noise characterized by fluctuations in the pulse arrival times, indicating inherent irregularities in the pulsar's rotational behavior. Furthermore, we discovered the occurrence of a spin-up glitch, with a fractional frequency increase of approximately 2.5E-6, suggesting sudden changes in the stellar interior. The X-ray timing analysis is supplemented by an investigation of the pulse profile, demonstrating the detection of the pulsar up to energies exceeding 30 keV. Additionally, we determined the phase offset between the X-ray and radio pulses to be phi=0.07 +/- 0.02, indicating a slight lead of the radio emission with respect to the X-rays. By comparing our findings with existing measurements of phase offsets in other X-ray and gamma-ray pulsars, we further support the lack of a discernible relationship between pulse period and phase offset. These X-ray timing observations contribute to our understanding of the pulsar PSR J1930+1852 and shed light on the complex dynamics within the Crab-like supernova remnant G54.1+0.3.

In this research, we explore the concept of nature-inspired interconnects for self-assembled large-scale network-on-chip (NoC) designs. We draw inspiration from the natural world, specifically the branching patterns of trees and the flow of rivers, to develop a novel approach to interconnect design. Our proposed method uses self-assembling components to create efficient and scalable interconnects, allowing for the creation of large-scale NoC designs that are both powerful and energy-efficient. We evaluate the performance of our nature-inspired interconnects using a range of benchmarks and compare them to traditional interconnect designs, demonstrating their superiority in terms of speed, power consumption, and area usage. Our findings have significant implications for the development of future NoC designs, and highlight the potential of biomimicry in the field of computer architecture.

Multiple Antenna Safer Broadcast over Wireless NetworksIn this paper, we investigate the issues of secure broadcast over wireless networks with multiple antennas at both the transmitter and receivers. We propose a novel transmission mechanisms that exploits the spatial diversity offered by multiple antennas to enhance the security of broadcast propeller. The proposed programs utilizes a combination of beamforming and space-time coding to provide multiple layers of security. Accurately, beamforming is used to focus the communicable signal towards the intended receivers, while space-time coding is employed to randomize the signal constellation, making it difficult for eavesdroppers to intercept and decode the transmitted specifics. We analyses the guaranteeing performance of the proposed scheme and show that it can achieve perfect secrecy against eavesdropping under certain conditions. Furthermore, we evaluate the performance of the proposed scheme in terms of secrecy prices and compare it with existing secure broadcast blueprint. The results reveals that the proposed scheme outperforms existing schemes in clauses of both secrecy rate and robustness to eavesdropping.

XMMU J174716.1-281048 is a strange source of X-ray, which recently discovered in Galaxy NGC 6744. Its luminescence is about 10^37 ERG/s, which is one of the weakest X -ray transients known to date. The source shows a special "quasi -durable" behavior, which is enhanced by X -ray activity, and then a relatively static period. The XMMU J174716.1-281048's X-ray spectrum is characterized by high absorption column density, which indicates that the source is covered with a large amount of intervention substances. The observed X-ray variant and spectral features indicate that the XMMU J174716.1-281048 may be a dual system composed of compact objects and low-quality accompanying stars. However, the nature of compact objects is still uncertain, and the possibility is from black holes to neutron stars. It is necessary to further observe and study to confirm the nature of this mysterious source and clarify its behavior and origin.

Gamma-ray burst (GRB) 980425 exhibited an unusually low redshift and was associated with supernova SN1998bw, indicating a potential link between some GRBs and supernovae. Using the Atacama Submillimeter Telescope Experiment (ASTE), we conducted observations of the host galaxy for GRB 980425 to search for carbon monoxide (CO) J=3-2 emission. ASTE is highly sensitive in the frequency range needed to detect CO J=3-2 emission from GRB 980425's host galaxy given its redshift. No CO J=3-2 emission was detected above 3-sigma from our observations. We discuss the implications of this non-detection and calculate gas mass limits that can be placed on the host galaxy. Elucidating the relationship between GRBs and their environments may provide insight into proposed GRB progenitor models. Future deeper observations are required to better constrain the molecular gas content of this low-redshift GRB host galaxy.

This paper examines cosmological perturbations, cosmic microwave background (CMB) radiation, and large-scale structure (LSS) formation within a primordial neutrino interacting dark-energy (DE) model with an exponential potential. The neutrino viscosity coefficient significantly affects the growth rate of matter perturbations and leaves discernible signatures on CMB and matter power spectra. Using the Markov Chain Monte Carlo method, we constrain the neutrino viscosity coefficient using the latest CMB and LSS observations. Current observations provide only a loose constraint on the neutrino viscosity coefficient.

Statistics of the Number of Zero Crossings: From Random Polynomials to Diffusion Equation This paper investigates the statistical properties of zero crossings for a class of random polynomials and diffusion processes. We demonstrate that the limiting distribution of zero crossings for a random polynomial is Gaussian, while for a diffusion process, it is Gaussian with a distinct variance.Furthermore, we derive an explicit formula for the limiting variance of zero crossings in diffusion processes. Our findings are applicable to studying various physical phenomena, such as particle diffusion in fluids and wave propagation through random media.

The power spectral density (PSD) function is commonly used to specifyseismometer performance. It is derived from the FFT of acceleration andcorrection is made for the transfer function of the instrument that generatedthe data. As with any such spectrum of density ('per Hz') type, the noiseinherent to a PSD is large. This article illustrates the value of a functionthat is derived from the PSD and for which the influence of noise issignificantly reduced. Called the cumulative spectral power (CSP), it isobtained from the PSD through the noise-reducing process of integration. Themaximum of the CSP (corresponding to the longest graphed value of the period)provides a means for estimating the total vibrational power of the earth. Thepresent author has significantly simplified the process of PSD generation. Thusroutine graphing is straightforwared-of first the FFT, followed by thegeneration of both a PSD and its associated CSP. The unique properties of theCSP make it valuable for the study of a variety of earth dynamics. For example,the strking simplicity of a CSP graph generated from a record containing astrong teleseismic earthquake is undoubtedly important to the development andrefinement of any viable theory of earthquake dynamics.

It has been observed that particular rate-1/2 partially systematic parallelconcatenated convolutional codes (PCCCs) can achieve a lower error floor thanthat of their rate-1/3 parent codes. Nevertheless, good puncturing patterns canonly be identified by means of an exhaustive search, whilst convergence towardslow bit error probabilities can be problematic when the systematic output of arate-1/2 partially systematic PCCC is heavily punctured. In this paper, wepresent and study a family of rate-1/2 partially systematic PCCCs, which wecall pseudo-randomly punctured codes. We evaluate their bit error rateperformance and we show that they always yield a lower error floor than that oftheir rate-1/3 parent codes. Furthermore, we compare analytic results tosimulations and we demonstrate that their performance converges towards theerror floor region, owning to the moderate puncturing of their systematicoutput. Consequently, we propose pseudo-random puncturing as a means ofimproving the bandwidth efficiency of a PCCC and simultaneously lowering itserror floor.

Unsustained matter distributions unescapely collapse unless fragmentation andcentrifugal or pressure support take place. Starting from the above evidence,supermassive compact objects at the centre of large-mass galaxies are conceivedas the end-product of the gravitational collapse of local density maxima aroundwhich overdensities are located. At the beginning of evolution, local densitymaxima are idealized as homogeneous peaks, while the surrounding envelopes aredescribed by a power-law density profile. The dependence of the density profileon a second parameter, chosen to be the ratio between peak and total mass, isanalysed. Overdensity evolution is discussed in the context of quintessencecosmological models and further investigation is devoted to a special case withthe aim to describe the central collapse. An empirical relation between holeand dark halo mass is translated into a dependence of the fractional hole masson the overdensity mass. Computations are performed up to the end of centralcollapse, and density profiles of related configurations are determinedtogether with additional parameters. The central collapse is completed in earlytimes, no longer than a few hundredths of Gyr, which implies hole formationwhen proto-haloes, proto-bulges, and proto-disks are still expanding orcontracting. No appreciable change in evolution is found with regard todifferent mean peak heights related to equal masses. On the other hand, it isrecognized that homogeneous peaks collapse ''faster'' with respect tosurroundings envelopes, in low-mass than in large-mass overdensities. Inconclusion, it is inferred that gravitational collapse of homogeneous peakswithin overdensities may be a viable mechanism for hole generation.

This article investigates the relationship between entropic caliber and Wasserstein diffusion in the context of stochastic processes. The concept of entropic measure delivers a quantification of uncertainty or randomness in a probability distribution, while Wasserstein diffusion characterizes the evolution of jeopardy distributions over time. The main purposes of this study is to creations a formal connection between these two concepts and explore their implications in various applications. Through a ferocious mathematical analysis, our implication demonstrate that the entropic measure of a probability distribution is directly related to the speed of dispersion described by the Wasserstein diffusion. Specifically, higher values of the entropic evaluated correspond to faster diffusion rates, indicating a greater echelons of randomness or unpredictability in the system. Furthermore, we built a generalized framework that authorise for the computation of the entropic measure for a given probability distribution and determine its influence on the behavior of the associated Wasserstein diffusion treating. The practical significance of our findings is noted through numerical simulations in different scenarios, varied from financial markets to biological systems. By understanding the interplay between entropic measure and Wasserstein diffusion, we provide a valuable tool for quantifying and characterizing the uncertainty dynamics in a largest range of stochastic handled. This contributes to the develops of more accurate models, improved risk analysis, and enhanced decision-making strategies in various fields where probabilistic analysis is crucial.

We present the mid-infrared spectrum, obtained with the Spitzer InfraredSpectrograph (IRS), of HD 98800, a quadruple star system located in the10-Myr-old TW Hydrae association. It has a known mid-infrared excess thatarises from a circumbinary disk around the B components of the system. The IRSspectrum confirms that the disk around HD 98800 B displays no excess emissionbelow about 5.5 micron, implying an optically thick disk wall at 5.9 AU and aninner, cleared-out region; however, some optically thin dust, consisting mainlyof 3-micron-sized silicate dust grains, orbits the binary in a ring between 1.5and 2 AU. The peculiar structure and apparent lack of gas in the HD 98800 Bdisk suggests that this system is likely already at the debris disks stage,with a tidally truncated circumbinary disk of larger dust particles and aninner, second-generation dust ring, possibly held up by the resonances of aplanet. The unusually large infrared excess can be explained by gravitationalperturbations of the Aa+Ab pair puffing up the outer dust ring and causingfrequent collisions among the larger particles.

Black holes have long been a subject of fascination and curiosity for physicists and astronomers alike. The semi-classical description of black hole evaporation, which is based on the theory of quantum mechanics and general relativity, has been widely accepted for decades. However, recent studies have revealed that this description is incomplete and fails to account for certain phenomena. In this article, we explore the limitations of the semi-classical description and discuss alternative approaches that go beyond it. We examine the role of quantum gravity and the importance of considering the full quantum nature of black holes. We also discuss the potential implications of these findings for our understanding of black hole evaporation and the behavior of black holes in various environments. Finally, we highlight the challenges and future directions for research in this area, including the need for a complete theory of quantum gravity.

Ordinary Boltzmann-Gibbs entropy is inadequate to be used in systemsdepending on a control parameter that yield different mean energy values. Suchsystems fail to give the correct comparison between the off-equilibrium andequilibrium entropy values. Klimontovich's S theorem solves this problem byrenormalizing energy and making use of escort distributions. Since nonextensivethermostatistics is a generalization of Boltzmann-Gibbs entropy, it tooexhibits this same deficiency. In order to remedy this, we present thenonextensive generalization of Klimontovich's S theorem. We show that thisgeneralization requires the use of ordinary probability and the associatedrelative entropy in addition to the renormalization of energy. Lastly, weillustrate the generalized S theorem for the Van der Pol oscillator.

This study investigates clustering features exhibited by the nuclei of beryllium-9 ($^9$Be), nitrogen-14 ($^{14}$N), beryllium-7 ($^7$Be), and boron-8 ($^8$B) within the framework of relativistic fragmentation. Employing high-energy collision experiments and advanced computational models, we analyze the formation and decay processes of these nuclei under extreme conditions. Our findings unveil significant clustering phenomena in the investigated isotopes. Specifically, we observe the emergence of alpha-like clusters in $^9$Be and $^{14}$N, accompanied by distinctive patterns in their fragmentation channels. Furthermore, a striking halo-like structure is identified in $^7$Be, characterized by loosely bound nucleons surrounding a compact core. The properties of the $^8$B nucleus exhibit characteristics of both alpha-like clustering and proton-halo structures. Through comprehensive investigations, we gain insights into the underlying mechanisms responsible for the observed clustering effects, which involve strong nuclear forces and the interplay of nuclear shells. Overall, our results contribute to a deeper understanding of the behavior and structure of light nuclei under relativistic fragmentation conditions, thereby shedding light on the fundamental properties of nuclear matter.

Stochastic resonance (SR) is a phenomenon that can enhance the responsse of nonlinear systems to weak signals through the presencge of noise. In this article, we investigate aspects of stochastic resonance in reaction-diffusion systems usng the nonequilibrium-potential approach. We introduce a mathematical framework that accounts for the combined effect of noisze, nonlinearity, and diffusion in these systems. By analyzing the nonequilibrium potentials, we uncover the conditions under which stochastic resonance ocucrs and characterize its properties. Our results demonstrate that the interplay between onise intensity, system parameters, and diffusion coefficients plays a crucial role in the manifestation of stochastic resonace. Moreover, we establish a connection between the nonequilibrium potentials and the underlying dynamAics of the reaction-diffusion sytsems, shedding light on the mechanisms behind stochastic resonance. Overall, our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the complex behavior exhibited by reaction-diffusion systems and provide insights into the potential applications of stochastic resonance in idverse fields ranging from bioMogy to phyics.

It is shown that the the interference of above-threshold electron de Brogliewaves, generated by an intense laser pulse at a metal surface yields attosecondelectron pulses. This inerference is an analogon of the superposition of highharmonics generated from rare gas atoms, resulting in trains of attosecondlight pulses.Owing to the inherent kinematic dispersion, the propagation ofattosecond de Broglie waves in vacuum is very different from that of attosecondlight pulses, which propagate without changing shape. Above the metal surfacethere are "collaps bands" and "revival layers" of the electron current even atmacroscopic distances. In the range of parameters considered, the maximum valueof the current densities of such ultrashort electron pulses has been estimatedto be of order of couple of tenths of milliamps per square centimeters.

We present a numerical study of the $\Delta H(M,\Delta M)$ method and itsability to accurately determine intrinsic switching field distributions ininteracting granular magnetic materials such as perpendicular recording media.In particular, we study how this methodology fails for large ferromagneticinter-granular interactions, at which point the associated strongly correlatedmagnetization reversal cannot be properly represented by the mean-fieldapproximation, upon which the $\Delta H(M,\Delta M)$ method is based. In thisstudy, we use a 2-dimensional array of symmetric hysterons that have anintrinsic switching field distribution of standard deviation $\sigma$ andferromagnetic nearest-neighbor interactions $J$. We find the $\Delta H(M,\DeltaM)$ method to be very accurate for small $J/\sigma$ values, while substantialerrors develop once the effective exchange field becomes comparable with$\sigma$, corroborating earlier results from micromagnetic simulations. Wefurthermore demonstrate that this failure is correlated with deviations fromdata set redundancy, which is a key property of the mean-field approximation.Thus, the $\Delta H(M,\Delta M)$ method fails in a well defined andquantifiable manner that can be easily assessed from the data sets alone.

We report new detailed surface U, B, V, R, and I photometry of 81 stellarstructures in the disk of the barred galaxy NGC 3367. The images show manydifferent structures indicating that star formation is going on in the mostpart of the disk. NGC 3367 is known to have a very high concentration ofmolecular gas distribution in the central regions of the galaxy and bipolarsynchrotron emission from the nucleus with two lobes (at 6 kpc) forming atriple structure similar to a radio galaxy. We have determined the U, B, V, R,and I magnitudes and U - B, B - V, U - V, and V - I colors for the centralregion (nucleus), a region which includes supernovae 2003 AA, and 79 starassociations throughout NGC 3367. Estimation of ages of star associations isvery difficult due to several factors, among them: filling factor, metallicity,spatial distribution of each structure and the fact that we estimated themagnitudes with a circular aperture of 16 pixels in diameter, equivalent to$6''.8\sim1.4$ kpc. However, if the colors derived for NGC 3367 were similar tothe colors expected of star clusters with theoretical evolutionary star tracksdeveloped for the LMC and had a similar metallicity, NGC 3367 show 51 percentof the observed structures with age type SWB I (few tens of Myrs), with sevensources outside the bright surface brightness visible disk of NGC 3367.

We present the results of a deep optical-near-infrared multi-epoch surveycovering 2.5 square degrees of the Pleiades open star cluster to search for newvery-low-mass brown dwarf members. A significant (~ 5 year) epoch differenceexists between the optical (CFH12k I-, Z-band) and near infrared (UKIRT WFCAMJ-band) observations. We construct I,I-Z and Z,Z-J colour magnitude diagrams toselect candidate cluster members. Proper motions are computed for all candidatemembers and compared to the background field objects to further refine thesample. We recover all known cluster members within the area of our survey. Inaddition, we have discovered 9 new candidate brown dwarf cluster members. The 7faintest candidates have red Z-J colours and show blue near-infrared colours.These are consistent with being L and T-type Pleiads.
