This article applies the model to calculate the mass spectra of light quark-antiquark mesons and glueballs. The model includes the Lorentz contraction and the effects of the kinematics of the flux tube. Recent lattice QCD studies have shown that the flux tube picture can be used to describe the formation of hadronic bound states. The results show that the relativistic flux tube model can reproduce the observed spectra of light mesons and glueballs quite well.

We report on a search for gravitational waves from the coalescence of compactbinaries during the third and fourth LIGO science runs. The search focused ongravitational waves generated during the inspiral phase of the binaryevolution. In our analysis, we considered three categories of compact binarysystems, ordered by mass: (i) primordial black hole binaries with masses in therange 0.35 M(sun) < m1, m2 < 1.0 M(sun), (ii) binary neutron stars with massesin the range 1.0 M(sun) < m1, m2 < 3.0 M(sun), and (iii) binary black holeswith masses in the range 3.0 M(sun)< m1, m2 < m_(max) with the additionalconstraint m1+ m2 < m_(max), where m_(max) was set to 40.0 M(sun) and 80.0M(sun) in the third and fourth science runs, respectively. Although thedetectors could probe to distances as far as tens of Mpc, no gravitational-wavesignals were identified in the 1364 hours of data we analyzed. Assuming abinary population with a Gaussian distribution around 0.75-0.75 M(sun), 1.4-1.4M(sun), and 5.0-5.0 M(sun), we derived 90%-confidence upper limit rates of 4.9yr^(-1) L10^(-1) for primordial black hole binaries, 1.2 yr^(-1) L10^(-1) forbinary neutron stars, and 0.5 yr^(-1) L10^(-1) for stellar mass binary blackholes, where L10 is 10^(10) times the blue light luminosity of the Sun.

In this article, we explore the realm of torsional geometries and their relationship to index theorems. We begin by examining the fundamental principles of torsional geometries and their underlying structures. We then delve into the concept of index theorems and their applicability to torsional geometries. Through a series of thorough computations and logical derivations, we demonstrate the validity of several index theorems in the context of torsional geometries. Our results provide valuable insights into the interplay between torsional geometries and index theorems, shedding light on the deeper mathematical structures that govern their behavior. Ultimately, our findings have significant implications for the study of geometric analysis and the pursuit of novel applications in physics and engineering.

This study presents a detailed analysis of the radio emissions from the IMBH in G1. Using high-resolution radio observations collected by a network of radio telescopes, we have revealed the existence of a compact radio source coincident with the position of the IMBH. The radio emissions have characteristics that are consistent with synchrotron radiation produced by relativistic electrons in a magnetic field. Our results suggest that the IMBH in G1 may be actively accreting matter, which could be a valuable probe of the formation and evolution of intermediate-mass black holes in dense stellar environments. Using sophisticated modeling techniques, we estimate the physical properties of the emitting region and propose a plausible mechanism for the origin of the radio emissions. Further multi-wavelength observations and theoretical investigations are necessary to obtain a full understanding of the role of IMBHs in globular clusters.

In this study, we utilize Bolean network modeling to predict the cell cycle sequence of fission yeast. Our approach allow the identification of crucial genes and their interactions, thereby providing insights into the regulatory mechanisms underlying cell cycle progression. By analyzing the dynamic behavior of the Boolean network, we uncover a seuence of cell cycle events that is consistent with experimental observations. Or findings demonstrate the potential of Boolean network modeling as a tool for understanding complex biological processes and forecasting celluar behavior. This approaches may be applied to explore the cell cycle regulation in other organisms, including humans, and contributes to the development of novel therapeutic approaches against cancer and other diseases. Future research may concentrating on integrating this method with other computational models and experimental techniques to further elucidate cell cycling regulation and its dysregulation in disease.

The matrix product ANSATZ (MPA) is a powerful tool for studying quantum multi -system systems. In this article, we apply MPA to the Six-Vertex model, which is the basic model in statistical mechanics. We show that MPA can accurately capture the base state characteristics of six vertex models, and can also understand the excitation of the model. Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) and quasars (QSOs) offer valuable insight into intervening metal absorption systems along the line of sight. The Gamma-Ray Imager (GRI) is a hard X-ray and soft gamma-ray coded-mask telescope mission. It is optimized to study the poorly-explored band between 20 and 300 keV, which is complementary to the hard X-ray instruments on board the Insight-HXMT and NuSTAR missions, and to the soft gamma-ray instruments on board the INTEGRAL mission. This paper describes the GRI mission, the science payload, the observing modes, the performance, and the expected scientific impact.

This paper presents a new iterative method for computing the sign function of a non-Hermitian matrix. The method is based on constructing a Krylov subspace approximation using the Arnoldi algorithm. Crab pulsar giant pulses (GPs), which are exceptionally powerful radio bursts, can provide key insights into pulsar emission mechanisms. Observing in this low-frequency radio domain with the MWA offers a novel perspective on pulsar physics by expanding observations of Crab nanoshots into an understudied portion of parameter space. Studying Crab GPs at these frequencies with the MWA can advance understanding of emission mechanisms in pulsars.

The metal abundance, kinematics, and position makeNGC 1883 a genuine outer disk intermediate-age open cluster. The authors explore whether the observed variation of the Amati relation with redshift is due to a selection effect, whereby GRBs at higher redshift are less detectable and therefore appear different, or to an evolution effect, whereby the physical properties of GRBs change with time. Thesystem includes seven second-order SQUID gradiometers, characterized bymagnetic field resolutions of 1.2 - 2.8 fT/rtHz. It is also equipped with fivesets of coils for 3D Fourier imaging with pre-polarization. Essential technicaldetails of the design are discussed. The system's ULF MRI performance isdemonstrated by multi-channel 3D images of a preserved sheep brain acquired at46 microtesla measurement field with pre-polarization at 40 mT. The imagingresolution is 2.5 mm x 2.5 mm x 5 mm. The ULF MRI images are compared to imagesof the same brain acquired using conventional high-field MRI. Different ways toimprove imaging SNR are discussed.

Given a partially ordered set $P$ there exists the most general Booleanalgebra $F(P)$ which contains $P$ as a generating set, called the {\it freeBoolean algebra} over $P$. We study free Boolean algebras over posets of theform $P=P_0\cup P_1$, where $P_0,P_1$ are well orderings. We call them {\itnearly ordinal algebras}. Answering a question of Maurice Pouzet, we show that for every uncountablecardinal $\kappa$ there are $2^\kappa$ pairwise non-isomorphic nearly ordinalalgebras of cardinality $\kappa$. Topologically, free Boolean algebras over posets correspond to compact0-dimensional distributive lattices. In this context, we classify all closedsublattices of the product $(\omega_1+1)\times(\omega_1+1)$, thus showing thatthere are only $\aleph_1$ many of them. In contrast with the last result, weshow that there are $2^{\aleph_1}$ topological types of closed subsets of theTikhonov plank $(\omega_1+1)\times(\omega+1)$.

Study of interacting electrons in graphene under the renormalized-ring-diagram approximationDuring this paper, we study the interacting electrnos in graphene under the framework of the renormalized-ring-diagram approximation. By introducing a mass term and a static screening potential, we obtain the single-particle Green's function and the self-energy. We find that the self-energy has a logarithmic singularity at scant energies, which is consistent with the Mermin-Wagner theorem. Moreover, we calculate the quasiparticle weight, the effective mass, and the Fermi velocity. Our results show that the interaction between ions renormalizes the Fermi velocity and the effective msas, and it also leads to a decrease in the quasiparticle weight.

This study investigates the systematic uncertainties of hadron parameters extracted using QCD sum rules. QCD sum rules, developed by Shifman, Vainshtein and Zakharov, relate hadronic parameters to the operator product expansion of current correlators. As an example, we apply sum rule techniques to a harmonic oscillator potential model where the exact solution is known. By constructing the operator product expansion to high orders and modeling the continuum contribution, we extract parameters of the ground state hadron. These extracted parameters are then compared to the known exact values from the model. The results indicate that without precise knowledge of the continuum contribution, the standard sum rule procedures do not allow full control over the systematic uncertainties of the extracted hadron parameters.

Consider the family S of irreducible plane curves of degree n with d nodesand k cusps as singularities. Let W be an irreducible component of S. Weconsider the natural rational map from W to the moduli space of curves of genusg=(n-1)(n-2)/2-d-k. We define the "number of moduli of W" as the dimension ofthe image of W with respect to this map. If W has the expected dimension equalto 3n+g-1-k, then the number of moduli of W is at most equal to the min(3g-3,3g-3+\rho-k), dove \rho is the Brill-Neother number of the linear series ofdegree n and dimension 2 on a smooth curve of genus g. We say that W has theexpected number of moduli if the equality holds. In this paper we constructexamples of families of irreducible plane curves with nodes and cusps assingularities having expected number of moduli and with non-positiveBrill-Noether number.

Parallel kinematic machines hired non-serial linkage architectures to enable high stiffness and accuracy. However, their complicated dynamics make kinetostatic optimization challenging. The authors develop a mathematical patterns of the potential and kinetic energy of parallel kinematic machine tools. This model relates the machine geometry and actuation forces to internal power streams and external work. The authors then define objective functions quantifying key kinetostatic potency metrics like stiffness and accelerations. Numerical optimization is applied to synthesize machine designs minimizing these objective functions subject to geometric coercion. The resulting designs enhance kinetostatic properties like reduced mechanical impedance and vivid minimization of internal power flows. Validation of the optimized designs demonstrates up to a 30% reinforced in stiffness over previous industrial machine structures. This methodology provides a useful tool for precision computers builders to design parallel kinematic machines with superior kinetostatic performance for high-speed, high-precision machining requisition.

The rapid growth of online information storage and more and more challenges related to resource discovery have prompted researchers to explore and innovate. This article surveys the use of social annotations as a means to enhance automatic resources. Social annotations refer to the process of collaborating with metadata (such as keywords or descriptions) to promote organizational and retrieval. By using the user's collective wisdom, social annotations provide promising ways to overcome the limitations of traditional automation technology. This research has comprehensively analyzed the various methods of social annotations in the context of resource discovery. It checked the benefits and challenges related to the existing information retrieval system. In addition, this article proposes a novel framework, which combines machine learning algorithms and users' annotations to improve the accuracy and correlation of resource discovery. Finally, a series of experiments were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the framework proposed, proving that its potential has significantly enhanced the discovery of automatic resource in different domains.

The electronic structures, equilibrium geometries, and finite temperature properties of sodium clusters, Na_n, with sizes ranging from 39 to 55 atoms, are investigated using first-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT). By employing a combination of structural optimization and molecular dynamics simulations, we explore the geometric arrangements and stability of these clusters at finite temperatures. The electronic structure calculations reveal the evolution of the cluster's electronic properties as a function of size, exhibiting significant variations in the density of states and band structures. Analysis of the equilibrium geometries shows that cluster structures with diverse geometrical motifs, including icosahedral, decahedral, and fcc-like configurations, are energetically favorable. Furthermore, we investigate the finite temperature properties of these clusters, including their heat capacities, melting points, and structural transformations. Our results demonstrate a non-monotonic trend in the melting points of sodium clusters with varying sizes, reflecting the interplay between surface effects and cohesive energies. The calculated heat capacities exhibit characteristic oscillations as a consequence of vibrational contributions and electronic shell effects. We also discuss the impact of electron correlation effects on the stability and structural properties of these clusters. This comprehensive study sheds light on the fundamental understanding of the electronic and thermal behavior of sodium clusters, providing valuable insights for understanding the properties and applications of nanostructured materials.

This paper presents a comprehensive studying on the quantitative size-dependent structure and strain analysis of CdSe nanoparticles utilizing atomic couple distribution function (PDF) analysis. CdSe nanoparticles are widely employed in optoelectronic devices due to their tunaBle optical properties. However, understanding their structure at the nanoscale is vital for optimizing their performance. By using synchrotron X-ray scattering techniques, the PDFs of CdSe nanoparticles with varying sizes were obtined and analyzed. The analysis revealed that the atomic structure of CdSe nanoparticles exhibits significant size-dependent changes, including bond length distortions and strain variations. Moreover, the strain analysis prov ided insights into the lattice distortion induced by the nanoparticle size. The results highlight the significance of the aomic-scale structural characterization for understanding the properties and pefrormance of CdSe nanoparticles, thereby facilitating their design and application in diverse nanotechnology fields.

Evolutionary Learning proceeds by evolving a population of classifiers, fromwhich it generally returns (with some notable exceptions) the singlebest-of-run classifier as final result. In the meanwhile, Ensemble Learning,one of the most efficient approaches in supervised Machine Learning for thelast decade, proceeds by building a population of diverse classifiers. EnsembleLearning with Evolutionary Computation thus receives increasing attention. TheEvolutionary Ensemble Learning (EEL) approach presented in this paper featurestwo contributions. First, a new fitness function, inspired by co-evolution andenforcing the classifier diversity, is presented. Further, a new selectioncriterion based on the classification margin is proposed. This criterion isused to extract the classifier ensemble from the final population only(Off-line) or incrementally along evolution (On-line). Experiments on a set ofbenchmark problems show that Off-line outperforms single-hypothesisevolutionary learning and state-of-art Boosting and generates smallerclassifier ensembles.

The study of the innermost circumstellar layers around AGB stars is crucialto understand how these envelopes are formed and evolve. The SiO maser emissionoccurs at a few stellar radii from the central star, providing directinformation on the stellar pulsation and on the chemical and physicalproperties of these regions. Our data also shed light on several aspects of theSiO maser pumping theory that are not well understood yet. We aim to determine}the relative spatial distribution of the 43 GHz and 86 GHz SiO maser lines inthe oxygen-rich evolved star R Leo. We have imaged with milliarcsecondresolution, by means of Very Long Baseline Interferometry, the 43 GHz (28SiOv=1, 2 J=1-0 and 29SiO v=0 J=1-0) and 86 GHz (28SiO v=1 J=2-1 and 29SiO v=0J=2-1) masing regions. We confirm previous results obtained in otheroxygen-rich envelopes. In particular, when comparing the 43 GHz emittingregions, the 28SiO v=2 transition is produced in an inner layer, closer to thecentral star. On the other hand, the 86 GHz line arises in a clearly farthershell. We have also mapped for the first time the 29SiO v=0 J=1-0 emission in RLeo. The already reported discrepancy between the observed distributions of thedifferent maser lines and the theoretical predictions is also found in R Leo.

We study a system of two quantum dots connected by a hopping bridge. Both thedots and connecting region are assumed to be in universal crossover regimesbetween Gaussian Orthogonal and Unitary ensembles. Using a diagrammaticapproach appropriate for energy separations much larger than the level spacingwe obtain the ensemble-averaged one- and two-particle Green's functions. Itturns out that the diffuson and cooperon parts of the two-particle Green'sfunction can be described by separate scaling functions. We then use thisinformation to investigate a model interacting system in which one dot has anattractive s-wave reduced Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer interaction, while theother is noninteracting but subject to an orbital magnetic field. We find thatthe critical temperature is {\it nonmonotonic} in the flux through the seconddot in a certain regime of interdot coupling. Likewise, the fluctuationmagnetization above the critical temperature is also nonmonotonic in thisregime, can be either diamagnetic or paramagnetic, and can be deduced from thecooperon scaling function.

Measurable spectra are theoretically very often derived from complicatedmany-body Green's functions. In this way, one calculates much more informationthan actually needed. Here we present an in principle exact approach toconstruct effective potentials and kernels for the direct calculation ofelectronic spectra. In particular, the potential that yields the spectralfunction needed to describe photoemission turns out to be dynamical but {\itlocal} and {\it real}. As example we illustrate this ''photoemissionpotential'' for sodium and aluminium, modelled as homogeneous electron gas, anddiscuss in particular its frequency dependence stemming from the nonlocality ofthe corresponding self-energy. We also show that our approach leads to a veryshort derivation of a kernel that is known to well describe absorption andenergy-loss spectra of a wide range of materials.

The interior structure and evolution of the Sun depends sensitively on the underlying equation of state of solar matter. This paper presents a novel approach to derive the solar equation of state using the path-integral formalism from first principles of quantum statistical mechanics. In the first part of this work, we compute the partition function and configurational integrals for the entire solar plasma using Monte Carlo integration of relevant quantum paths. The resulting free energy and pressure relations reproduce prior equations of state in their domain of validity and address long-standing issues with approximations made in previous models. We systematically investigate deviations from ideality and molecular interactions not captured by standard perturbation theories. Comparisons with helioseismic data and neutrino fluxes suggest our path-integral based equation of state provides an improved description of deep solar interior conditions up to number densities of 1025cm-3 and temperatures of over 106 K. However, limitations of the path-integral approach emerge at higher densities that require further theoretical development. This work lays the foundation for more detailed modeling of solar neutrino production and evolution in the neutrino-emitting solar core.

We consider the problem of quantization of classical soliton integrablesystems, such as the KdV hierarchy, in the framework of a general formalism ofGaudin models associated to affine Kac--Moody algebras. Our experience with theGaudin models associated to finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras suggeststhat the common eigenvalues of the mutually commuting quantum Hamiltonians in amodel associated to an affine algebra should be encoded by affine opersassociated to the Langlands dual affine algebra. This leads us to some concretepredictions for the spectra of the quantum Hamiltonians of the soliton systems.In particular, for the KdV system the corresponding affine opers may beexpressed as Schroedinger operators with spectral parameter, and ourpredictions in this case match those recently made by Bazhanov, Lukyanov andZamolodchikov. This suggests that this and other recently found examples of thecorrespondence between quantum integrals of motion and differential operatorsmay be viewed as special cases of the Langlands duality.

In this artisle, we present a general approach for modeling and controlling few-cycle intense laser interactions with complex atoms. Our approach leverages recent advances in computational power and machine learning algorithms to simulate the interactions between laser pulses and atoms with unprecedented accuracy and efficiency. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by applying it to a variety of complex atomic systems, including those with multiple electron shells and non-zero nuclear spin. We results show that our approach can accurately predict the dynamics of laser-atom interactions on few-cycle timescales, enabling the exploration of new regimes of laser-matter interactive. Ourselves also discuss the potential applications of our approach in fields such as high-harmonic spectroscopy, atomic ionization, and quantum computing.

Aims. We probe the effect of turbulent diffusion on the chemistry at theinterface between a cold neutral medium (CNM) cloudlet and the warm neutralmedium (WNM). Methods. We perform moving grid, multifluid, 1D, hydrodynamicalsimulations with chemistry including thermal and chemical diffusion. Thediffusion coefficients are enhanced to account for turbulent diffusion. Wepost-process the steady-states of our simulations with a crude model ofradiative transfer to compute line profiles. Results. Turbulent diffusionspreads out the transition region between the CNM and the WNM. We find that theCNM slightly expands and heats up: its CH and H$_2$ content decreases due tothe lower density. The change of physical conditions and diffusive transportincrease the H$^+$ content in the CNM which results in increased OH and H$_2$O.Diffusion transports some CO out of the CNM. It also brings H$_2$ into contactwith the warm gas with enhanced production of CH$^+$, H$_3^+$, OH and H$_2$O atthe interface. O lines are sensitive to the spread of the thermal profile inthe intermediate region between the CNM and the WNM. Enhanced molecular contentat the interface of the cloud broadens the molecular line profiles and helpsexciting transitions of intermediate energy. The relative molecular yield arefound higher for bigger clouds. Conclusions. Turbulent diffusion can be thesource of additional molecular production and should be included in chemicalmodels of the interstellar medium (ISM). It also is a good candidate for theinterpretation of observational problems such as warm H$_2$, CH$^+$ formationand presence of H$_3^+$.

Common envelopes form in dynamical time scale mass exchange, when theenvelope of a donor star engulfs a much denser companion, and the core of thedonor plus the dense companion star spiral inward through this dissipativeenvelope. As conceived by Paczynski and Ostriker, this process must beresponsible for the creation of short-period binaries with degeneratecomponents, and, indeed, it has proven capable of accounting for short-periodbinaries containing one white dwarf component. However, attempts to reconstructthe evolutionary histories of close double white dwarfs have proven moreproblematic, and point to the need for enhanced systemic mass loss, eitherduring the close of the first, slow episode of mass transfer that produced thefirst white dwarf, or during the detached phase preceding the final, commonenvelope episode. The survival of long-period interacting binaries with massivewhite dwarfs, such as the recurrent novae T CrB and RS Oph, also presentsinterpretative difficulties for simple energetic treatments of common envelopeevolution. Their existence implies that major terms are missing from usualformulations of the energy budget for common envelope evolution. The mostplausible missing energy term is the energy released by recombination in thecommon envelope, and, indeed, a simple reformulation the energy budgetexplicitly including recombination resolves this issue.

In this paper, we present a comprehensive study of the prompt emission from GRBs, focusing on the production and characteristics of high-energy photons. We review the current theoretical models and observational data that shed light on the mechanisms responsible for the generation and release of these photons. We discuss the leading theoretical models, including synchrotron radiation, inverse Compton scattering, and photosphere emission, which explain the observed spectral properties and time profiles of the high-energy emission. We also discuss the role of magnetic fields, shock acceleration, and particle interactions in shaping the prompt spectra. The prompt emission of high-energy photons is believed to originate from non-thermal processes in the jets generated by the collapse of massive stars or the merger of compact objects. We discuss the challenges associated with studying the prompt emission, including the limitations of the instruments, the observational biases, and the complex interplay between the different components of the burst. Recent advances in space- and ground-based telescopes have greatly enhanced our understanding of the properties of the prompt emission from GRBs. We summarize the key results, such as the spectral evolution, the fluence distribution, and the temporal variability, and we highlight the importance of multi-wavelength observations in constraining the underlying physics. In conclusion, the prompt emission of high-energy photons from GRBs remains an exciting topic of research that combines astrophysics, plasma physics, and high-energy particle physics.

New high-resolution observations reveal that small-scale magnetic fluxconcentrations have a delicate substructure on a spatial scale of 0.1''. Itsbasic structure can be interpreted in terms of a magnetic flux sheet or tubethat vertically extends through the ambient weak-field or field-free atmospherewith which it is in mechanical equilibrium. A more refined interpretation comesfrom new three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic simulations that are capable ofreproducing the corrugated shape of magnetic flux concentrations and theirsignature in the visible continuum. Furthermore it is shown that thecharacteristic asymmetric shape of the contrast profile of facular granules isan effect of radiative transfer across the rarefied atmosphere of the magneticflux concentration. I also discuss three-dimensional radiationmagnetohydrodynamic simulations of the integral layers from the top of theconvection zone to the mid-chromosphere. They show a highly dynamicchromospheric magnetic field, marked by rapidly moving filaments of strongerthan average magnetic field that form in the compression zone downstream andalong propagating shock fronts. The simulations confirm the picture of fluxconcentrations that strongly expand through the photosphere into a morehomogeneous, space filling chromospheric field. Future directions in thesimulation of small-scale magnetic fields are indicated by a few examples ofvery recent work.

This is the third of a series of papers on a new equivariant cohomology thattakes values in a vertex algebra, and contains and generalizes the classicalequivariant cohomology of a manifold with a Lie group action a la H. Cartan. Inthis paper, we compute this cohomology for spheres and show that for any simpleconnected group G, there is a sphere with infinitely many actions of G whichhave distinct chiral equivariant cohomology, but identical classicalequivariant cohomology. Unlike the classical case, the description of thechiral equivariant cohomology of spheres requires a substantial amount of newstructural theory, which we fully develop in this paper. This includes aquasi-conformal structure, equivariant homotopy invariance, and the values ofthis cohomology on homogeneous spaces. These results rely on crucial featuresof the underlying vertex algebra valued complex that have no classicalanalogues.

The Millennium Galaxy Catalogue provides essential data for understanding the properties of galaxies. Through analysis of the B-band attenuation of bulge and disc light, this study investigates the cosmic dust and stellar mass densities implied by the catalogue's data. The study reveals a strong correlation between the B-band attenuation and the galactic inclination angle, with greater attenuation observed in galaxies with higher inclination angles. A significant correlation is also found between the attenuation and the galaxy's distance, with closer galaxies exhibiting higher attenuation. The analysis indicates that the cosmic dust density is higher in regions with higher galaxy densities. Moreover, the study finds a positive correlation between the stellar mass density and the B-band attenuation, implying that galaxies with greater stellar masses have higher attenuation. The study's results offer valuable insights into the properties of galaxies and the role of cosmic dust and stellar mass in shaping their evolution. The findings have important implications for understanding the history of galaxy formation and evolution. Further research is necessary to confirm these findings and explore their broader implications for our understanding of the universe.

This article proposes a cooperative transmission agreement to use multi -user detection and network coding to achieve the efficiency of high spectrum and high diversity. The proposed agreement enables multiple nodes to cooperate and share its resources, thereby improving performance in terms of capacity and reliability. The proposed agreement aims to be used in complex network topology and can adapt to changing channel conditions and network dynamics. This article proposes a wide range of simulation results to prove the effectiveness of the scheme proposed in various cases. The results show that the spectral efficiency and diversity order of these protocols have been significantly improved compared with traditional transmission schemes. This article also discusses the complexity of implementation and highlights the potential of the proposed agreement on the future wireless communication system.

It has been shown that, for the two-qubit Heisenberg XY model, anisotropy andmagnetic field may together be used to produce entanglement for any finitetemperature by adjusting the external magnetic field beyond some finitecritical strength. This interesting result arises from an analysis employingthe Wootters concurrence, a computable measure of entanglement for two-qubitstates. Recently, Mintert {\em et al.} proposed generalizations of Woottersconcurrence for multipartite states. These MKB concurrences possess amathematical property that enables one to understand the origin of thischaracteristic behavior. Here, we first study the effect of anisotropy andmagnetic field on the multipartite thermal entanglement of a four-qubitHeisenberg XY chain using the MKB concurrences. We show that this modelexhibits characteristic behavior similar to that of the two-qubit model. Inaddition, we show that this can again be understood using the same mathematicalproperty. Next, we show that the six-qubit Heisenberg XY chain possessesproperties necessary for it to have the characteristic behavior too. Mostimportantly, it is possible to directly measure the multipartite MKBconcurrences of pure states. This may provide an experimental verification ofour conjecture that for a Heisenberg XY chain of any even number of qubits, itis always possible to obtain non-zero genuine multipartite entanglement at anyfinite temperature by applying a sufficiently large magnetic field.

This study presents spectroscopic observations of the intermediate polar EX Hydrae (EX Hya) during quiescent phases. EX Hya is a cataclysmic variable binary star system consisting of a white dwarf primary and a late-type secondary star. The system exhibits a range of photometric and spectroscopic behaviors, making it an intriguing target for investigation. In this work, we obtained high-resolution optical spectra of EX Hya using the XYZ Observatory's spectrograph. Our observations covered a wavelength range of 400-800 nm, allowing us to analyze various spectral features associated with the system. We performed a thorough analysis of the obtained spectra, focusing on emission lines, absorption features, and their variations over time. We found prominent emission lines of hydrogen Balmer series, helium, and other metal species in the spectra. The line profiles showed complex structures that can be attributed to accretion processes occurring within the system. By comparing our findings with previous studies, we determined the spectroscopic properties of EX Hya during quiescence in more detail. Our results provide further insights into the accretion dynamics and mass transfer mechanisms in cataclysmic variables, shedding light on the evolution of these systems. This investigation serves as a foundation for future studies aiming to explore the behavior of EX Hya during outburst phases and its relationship with other cataclysmic variables.

In this article, we present a detailed analysis and discussion on the number of steady states in a multiple futile cycle. Multiple futile cycles are common motifs in biochemical networks and have been the subject of considerable research interest. Using a rigorous mathematical framework, we formulate the conditions for the existence and determination of steady states within such cycles. Through mathematical modeling and numerical simulations, we demonstrate that the number of steady states can vary depending on the system parameters and kinetic rates. Our findings shed light on the intricate dynamics and regulatory mechanisms underlying multiple futile cycles, providing valuable insights for understanding the behavior of complex biochemical networks.

We study Casimir forces on the partition in a closed box (piston) withperfect metallic boundary conditions. Related closed geometries have generatedinterest as candidates for a repulsive force. By using an optical pathexpansion we solve exactly the case of a piston with a rectangular crosssection, and find that the force always attracts the partition to the nearestbase. For arbitrary cross sections, we can use an expansion for the density ofstates to compute the force in the limit of small height to width ratios. Thecorrections to the force between parallel plates are found to have interestingdependence on the shape of the cross section. Finally, for temperatures in therange of experimental interest we compute finite temperature corrections to theforce (again assuming perfect boundaries).

If the supermassive black hole (SMBH) at the center of our Galaxy grewadiabatically, then a dense "spike" of dark matter is expected to have formedaround it. Assuming that dark matter is composed primarily of weaklyinteracting massive particles (WIMPs), a star orbiting close enough to the SMBHcan capture WIMPs at an extremely high rate. The stellar luminosity due toannihilation of captured WIMPs in the stellar core may be comparable to or evenexceed the luminosity of the star due to thermonuclear burning. The model thuspredicts the existence of unusual stars, i.e. "WIMP burners", in the vicinityof an adiabatically grown SMBH. We find that the most efficient WIMP burnersare stars with degenerate electron cores, e.g. white dwarfs (WD) or degeneratecores with envelopes. If found, such stars would provide evidence for theexistence of particle dark matter and could possibly be used to establish itsdensity profile. In our previous paper we computed the luminosity from WIMPburning for a range of dark matter spike density profiles, degenerate coremasses, and distances from the SMBH. Here we compare our results with theobserved stars closest to the Galactic center and find that they could beconsistent with WIMP burners in the form of degenerate cores with envelopes. Wealso cross-check the WIMP burner hypothesis with the EGRET observed flux ofgamma-rays from the Galactic center, which imposes a constraint on the darkmatter spike density profile and annihilation cross-section. We find that theEGRET data is consistent with the WIMP burner hypothesis. New high precisionmeasurements by GLAST will confirm or set stringent limits on a dark matterspike at the Galactic center, which will in turn support or set stringentlimits on the existence of WIMP burners at the Galactic center.

We report on HST/ACS photometry of the rich intermediate-age star cluster NGC1846 in the Large Magellanic Cloud, which clearly reveals the presence of adouble main sequence turn-off in this object. Despite this, the main sequence,sub-giant branch, and red giant branch are all narrow and well-defined, and thered clump is compact. We examine the spatial distribution of turn-off stars anddemonstrate that all belong to NGC 1846 rather than to any field starpopulation. In addition, the spatial distributions of the two sets of turn-offstars may exhibit different central concentrations and some asymmetries. Byfitting isochrones, we show that the properties of the colour-magnitude diagramcan be explained if there are two stellar populations of equivalent metalabundance in NGC 1846, differing in age by approximately 300 Myr. The absoluteages of the two populations are ~1.9 and ~2.2 Gyr, although there may be asystematic error of up to +/-0.4 Gyr in these values. The metal abundanceinferred from isochrone fitting is [M/H] ~ -0.40, consistent with spectroscopicmeasurements of [Fe/H]. We propose that the observed properties of NGC 1846 canbe explained if this object originated via the tidal capture of two starclusters formed separately in a star cluster group in a single giant molecularcloud. This scenario accounts naturally for the age difference and uniformmetallicity of the two member populations, as well as the differences in theirspatial distributions.

The structure of the chromosphere and transition regions in O and B-type stars is calculated using an updated model that extends previous models for the upper atmospheres of these stars. This model includes a detailed treatment of the formation and destruction of molecules. The model's results are in good agreement with observed spectra of O and B-type stars, confirming the formation of the DACs and SACs regions by the partial ionization of metals. The model reproduces the observed dependence of the ionization structure of the DACs and SACs regions on the effective temperature and surface gravity of the star. Furthermore, the model provides insights into the physical processes determining the structure of the upper atmospheres of O and B-type stars.

The study investigates the formation and collisional evolution of Kuiper Belt Objects (KBOs) in our solar system. By analyzing rotational properties and phase functions of a sample of KBOs, we aim to uncover key insights into their origins and evolutionary processes. Utilizing telescopic observations and sophisticated numerical simulations, we determine the metallicity gradient and ionization fraction within the Kuiper Belt, shedding light on the chemical composition and internal dynamics of these objects. Furthermore, we compare theoretical models with observational data to assess their validity and provide a comprehensive understanding of KBO formation and collisional evolution. Our findings reveal the importance of collisional processes in shaping the current population of KBOs and offer valuable constraints for future studies and theoretical investigations in the field.

User's perception of product, by essence subjective, is a major topic inmarketing and industrial design. Many methods, based on users' tests, are usedso as to characterise this perception. We are interested in three main methods:multidimensional scaling, semantic differential method, and preference mapping.These methods are used to built a perceptual space, in order to position thenew product, to specify requirements by the study of user's preferences, toevaluate some product attributes, related in particular to style (aesthetic).These early stages of the design are primordial for a good orientation of theproject. In parallel, virtual reality tools and interfaces are more and moreefficient for suggesting to the user complex feelings, and creating in this wayvarious levels of perceptions. In this article, we present on an example theuse of multidimensional scaling, semantic differential method and preferencemapping for the subjective assessment of virtual products. These products,which geometrical form is variable, are defined with a CAD model and areproposed to the user with a spacemouse and stereoscopic glasses. Advantages andlimitations of such evaluation is next discussed..

A brief introduction is given to the subject of brane induced gravity. The 5Dexample is discussed in detail. The 4D laws of gravity are obtained on a braneembedded in an infinite volume extra space, where the problem of stabilizationof the volume modulus is absent. The theory has two classically disjointbranches of solutions -- the conventional and self-accelerated one. Theconventional branch gives a perturbatively stable model of a metastablegraviton, with potentially testable predictions within the Solar system. Theself-accelerated branch, on the other hand, provides an existence proof for anidea that the accelerated expansion of the Universe could be due to modifiedgravity. The issue of perturbative stability of the self-accelerated branch isobscured by a breakdown of the conventional perturbative expansion. However, acertain exact non-perturbative solution found in hep-th/0612016 exhibits a netnegative gravitational mass, while this mass is positive on the conventionalbranch. This suggest that the self-accelerated solution must benon-perturbatively unstable. A proposal to overcome this problem in anextension of the original model, that also allows for the quantum gravity scaleto be unrestricted, is briefly discussed.

In this work we study preference systems natural for the Peer-to-Peerparadigm. Most of them fall in three categories: global, symmetric andcomplementary. All these systems share an acyclicity property. As aconsequence, they admit a stable (or Pareto efficient) configuration, where noparticipant can collaborate with better partners than their current ones. Weanalyze the representation of the such preference systems and show that anyacyclic system can be represented with a symmetric mark matrix. This gives amethod to merge acyclic preference systems and retain the acyclicity. We alsoconsider such properties of the corresponding collaboration graph, asclustering coefficient and diameter. In particular, studying the example ofpreferences based on real latency measurements, we observe that its stableconfiguration is a small-world graph.

Gravitational waves from galaxy encounters are a promising new window into the universe's mysteries. These waves are produced when galaxies collide and their massive black holes merge. The detection of these waves has allowed us to study the properties of galaxy encounters in a way that was previously impossible. By analyzing the patterns of these waves, we can gain valuable insights into the formation and evolution of galaxies.

This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the haunting phenomena observed in the halos of the Andromeda and Triangulum galaxies, spilt light on the intricate processes underlying galaxy formation. Utilizing multi-wavelength observations from the Hubble Sp ace Telescope and ground-based observatories, we investigate the panoramic view of these galaxies, unraveling the dynamic interplay between the galactic disks and their surrounding auras. Our study reveals a diverse range of wraiths features emanating from the halos, providing compelling evidence of ongoing accretion and interaction processes. We employ sophisticated data analysis techniques, including spectral decomposition and morphological studies, to disentangle and characterize the constituent components indoors the halos. Additionally, we harness advanced numerical simulations to validate our findings and gain further insights into the mechanisms drive the observed phenomena. Through the integrate of observational and conceptually approaches, we unveil the existence of filamentary structures spanning across the halos, indicative of inflows and outflows of gas. These findings highlight the complex nature of galaxy assembly, as material from the intergalactic meduim is accreted onto the galactic disks, contributing to their growth and evolution. Moreover, we identify the presence of ghostly streams and tidal debris, remnants of past interactions among neighboring supermassive, delineating the intricate web of cosmic interactions. Furthermore, our investigation explores the infleunce of environmental factors on the formation and evolution of the halo structures, accounting for variations in density, temperature, and chemical composition. We quantify the impact of these environmental factors on the morphology, kinematics, and chemical enrichment of the halo gas, providing crucial insig hts into the interconnectedness between quasars and their sruroundings.

This article presents a comprehensive study on the kinetic equation for finite systems of fermions with pairing. Fermionic systems with pairing are of significant interest in various physical and chemical phenomena, such as superconductivity and pairing in atomic nuclei. The kinetic equation plays a crucial role in describing the dynamics and evolution of fermionic systems, providing valuable insights into their behavior. We establish a general framework for formulating the kinetic equation for finite fermionic systems with pairing, taking into account the effects of pairing correlations. By incorporating the appropriate pairing operators and considering the conservation laws, we derive a self-consistent kinetic equation that describes the time evolution of the single-particle occupation probabilities. Furthermore, we discuss the implications of this kinetic equation for studying the dynamics of pairing effects in finite fermionic systems, and we elucidate its potential applications in various fields, such as condensed matter physics and nuclear physics. Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of fermionic systems with pairing and pave the way for further investigations into their complex behavior and properties.

This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the Swift/X-ray Telescope (XRT) data of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) with shallow decay segments (SDSs) in their X-ray afterglow light curves. A sample of 33 GRBs with well-sampled XRT light curves is selected, and the temporal and spectral properties of their SDSs are extracted. The results show that the SDSs can be divided into two distinct groups: the hard SDSs and the soft SDSs. The former have a harder photon index and a higher peak energy, are more likely to be associated with X-ray flares, and have a shorter duration. The latter are likely produced by the synchrotron emission from the reverse shock or the emission from the cocoon.

There is growing concern about what will happen to our digital files and online accounts after we die or become incapacitated. As more of our perpetuity move otta, how can people ensure their digital inheritance and memories are properly cared for? This article proposes a service model for personal digital archives that would allow individuals to designate steering to succeeds their digital assets and selectively switched content with specified colleagues, friends, and family after loss of access. The model aims to address gaps in how individuals can lends executives for their digital belongings beyond their control or lifespan.

We evaluate the doping dependence of the quasiparticle current and lowtemperature superfluid density in two slave-particle theories of the tt't''Jmodel -- the slave-boson theory and doped-carrier theory. In the slave-bosontheory, the nodal quasiparticle current renormalization factor $\alpha$vanishes proportionally to the zero temperature superfluid density $\rho_S(0)$;however, we find that away from the $\rho_S(0) \to 0$ limit $\alpha$ displays amuch weaker doping dependence than $\rho_S(0)$. A similar conclusion applies tothe doped-carrier theory, which differentiates the nodal and antinodal regionsof momentum space. Due to its momentum space anisotropy, the doped-carriertheory enhances the value of $\alpha$ in the hole doped regime, bringing it toquantitative agreement with experiments, and reproduces the asymmetry betweenhole and electron doped cuprate superconductors. Finally, we use thedoped-carrier theory to predict a specific experimental signature of localstaggered spin correlations in doped Mott insulator superconductors which, wepropose, should be observed in STM measurements of underdoped high-Tccompounds. This experimental signature distinguishes the doped-carrier theoryfrom other candidate mean-field theories of high-Tc superconductors, like theslave-boson theory and the conventional BCS theory.

The study of the observational properties of uncommonly long bursts from lowluminosity sources with extended decay times up to several tens of minutes isimportant when investigating the transition from a hydrogen-rich burstingregime to a pure helium regime and from helium burning to carbon burning aspredicted by current burst theories. IGR J17254-3257 is a recently discoveredX-ray burster of which only two bursts have been recorded: an ordinary shorttype I X-ray burst, and a 15 min long burst. An upper limit to its distance isestimated to about 14.5 kpc. The broad-band spectrum of the persistent emissionin the 0.3-100 keV energy band obtained using contemporaneous INTEGRAL andXMM-Newton data indicates a bolometric flux of 1.1x10^-10 erg/cm2/scorresponding, at the canonical distance of 8 kpc, to a luminosity about8.4x10^35 erg/s between 0.1-100 keV, which translates to a mean accretion rateof about 7x10^-11 solar masses per year. The low X-ray persistent luminosity ofIGR J17254-3257 seems to indicate the source may be in a state of low accretionrate usually associated with a hard spectrum in the X-ray range. The nuclearburning regime may be intermediate between pure He and mixed H/He burning. Thelong burst is the result of the accumulation of a thick He layer, while theshort one is a prematurate H-triggered He burning burst at a slightly loweraccretion rate.

The imprint of gravitational distortions from primordial density inhomogeneities in the Oort cloud on the cosmic microwave background anisotropies can provide novel insights into the formation history of our solar system. This study investigates through numerical simulations how density perturbations originating from inflation in the early universe would have impacted the development of structure in the nascent Oort cloud during the epoch of planet formation in the solar nebula. The simulations self-consistently follow the linear growth of adiabatic fluctuations over cosmological timescales and capture their nonlinear evolution within the gravitational potential well of the forming solar system. The results indicate that distortions induced by waves with wavelengths comparable to the size of the Oort cloud at recombination could have left an observable signature in the large-angle CMB temperature anisotropies. Quantitative predictions for the angular power spectrum are presented and avenues for extracting this unique signal from astrophysical foregrounds in upcoming high-precision CMB polarization maps are discussed.

We study the kinetic theory of driven granular gases, taking into accountboth translational and rotational degrees of freedom. We obtain the high-energytail of the stationary bivariate energy distribution, depending on the totalenergy E and the ratio x=sqrt{E_w/E} of rotational energy E_w to total energy.Extremely energetic particles have a unique and well-defined distribution f(x)which has several remarkable features: x is not uniformly distributed as inmolecular gases; f(x) is not smooth but has multiple singularities. The latterbehavior is sensitive to material properties such as the collision parameters,the moment of inertia and the collision rate. Interestingly, there arepreferred ratios of rotational-to-total energy. In general, f(x) is stronglycorrelated with energy and the deviations from a uniform distribution grow withenergy. We also solve for the energy distribution of freely cooling MaxwellMolecules and find qualitatively similar behavior.

In this article, we investigate the impcat of spin-zero particle-photon interactions on light polarization in external magnetic fields. We present a theoretical framework for understanding the effects of these interactions on the polarization state of light in various scenarios, including the presence of magnetic fields. Our analysis reveals that the spin-zero particle-photon interactions can significantly affect the polarization of lights, leading to changes in its oreintation and intensity. We also demonstrate that the strength and direction of the magnetic field can be used to control the degree of polarization alteration. Our findings have important implications for the development of novel optical devices and technologies, and may lead to new insights into the behavior of light in stro ng external fields. Furthermore, this study deepens our understanding of the fundamental interactions between light and matter, and may have potential applications in fields such as quantm computing and communication.

The large-scale Galactic interstellar radiation field (ISRF) is the result ofstellar emission and dust re-processing of starlight. Where the energy densityof the ISRF is high (e.g., the Galactic Centre), the dominant gamma-rayemission in individual supernova remnants (SNRs), such as G0.9+0.1, may comefrom inverse Compton (IC) scattering of the ISRF. Several models of the ISRFexist. The most recent one, which has been calculated by us, predicts asignificantly higher ISRF than the well-used model of Mathis, Mezger, andPanagia. However,comparison with data is limited to local observations. Basedon our current estimate of the ISRF we predict the gamma-ray emission in theSNRs G0.9+0.1 and RXJ1713, and pair-production absorption features above 20 TeVin the spectra of G0.9+0.1, J1713-381, and J1634-472. We discuss how GLAST,along with current and future very high energy instruments, may be able toprovide upper bounds on the large-scale ISRF.

In this article, we investigate the interplay between Frobenius splitting and the geometry of $G$-Schubert varieties, where $G$ is a reductive algebraic group. We begin by introducing the concept of Frobenius splitting, which is a powerful tool in algebraic geometry used to study various geometric objects. We then focus our attention on $G$-Schubert varieties, which are important objects of study in the theory of algebraic groups and flag varieties.We establish a deep connection between Frobenius splitting and the geometry of $G$-Schubert varieties by proving that certain Schubert varieties are Frobenius split. This result has implications for the study of geometric properties of $G$-Schubert varieties, such as their singularities and cohomology. Moreover, we provide explicit criteria for determining when a $G$-Schubert variety is Frobenius split, which allows for a more practical approach to identifying Frobenius splittings in specific cases.Furthermore, we investigate the relationship between Frobenius splitting and the Bruhat order on the set of $G$-Schubert varieties. We show that the Bruhat order is compatible with Frobenius splitting in the sense that any two $G$-Schubert varieties in the same Bruhat interval have the same Frobenius splitting property.Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the geometry of $G$-Schubert varieties and provide valuable insights into the interplay between algebraic geometry and Frobenius splitting. The results presented in this article have applications in various areas of mathematics, including representation theory, algebraic topology, and combinatorics.

This paper proposes a Bayesian approach to the separation of mixed text/image documents, where a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) is used to model the underlying structure of the document. The HMM is trained on a set of labeled document images, and then used to classify each pixel in a new document image as either text or image. The classification results are then used to generate a binary image of the document, which can be used for further processing, such as optical character recognition (OCR). The proposed approach is evaluated on a set of document images, and the results show that it outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and speed.

In this article, we introduced the theorem of relative entropy in the quantum state, which summarized the well -known theorem of Lieb and Ruskai. Our theorem provides a new and general upper limit in the mutual information of the two quantum states to achieve the relative entropy of the two quantum states. We prove that our theorem can be applied to privacy in quantum communication and provides a new privacy for the quantum key distribution. Our results show that our theorem is a powerful tool for studying quantum state and its application in quantum communication. Keywords: Relative entropy, quantum state, privacy, quantum communication

Algebraic Geometry of Gaussian Bayesian NetworksAbstract:In this article, we delve into the intricate interplay between algebraic geometry and Gaussian Bayesian networks. Drawing upon the rich framework of algebraic geometry, we explore the structural properties and underlying mathematics of Gaussian Bayesian networks. By leveraging geometric techniques, we establish a novel perspective on the probabilistic relationships within these networks, shedding light on their fundamental properties. Furthermore, we investigate the algebraic structures that arise in Gaussian Bayesian networks, uncovering connections to concepts such as algebraic varieties and polynomial ideals. Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of Gaussian Bayesian networks and provide valuable insights for their analysis and interpretation.

The Broad-Line Radio Galaxy 3C 445 exhibits an extraordinary X-ray spectrum, which has been the subject of much study and debate in the scientific community. In this article, we present a detailed analysis of the X-ray spectrum of 3C 445, utilizing data from the XMM-Newton and NuSTAR observatories. Our results reveal a complex and varied X-ray emission profile, characterized by a number of distinct features.The X-ray spectrum displays a steep power-law continuum, which is punctuated by a series of deep absorption lines and a highly ionized iron K-shell line. The absorption lines are identified as being due to iron, oxygen, and magnesium, and are found to be variable on timescales of days to weeks. The iron K-shell line is unusually strong, and is suggestive of a high concentration of iron in the vicinity of the supermassive black hole at the galaxy's center.The X-ray emission is also characterized by a number of weaker features, including a soft excess component and a number of narrow emission lines. The soft excess is thought to arise from the thermal emission of the galaxy's interstellar medium, while the narrow emission lines are likely produced by the radiation of the accretion disk.Our analysis also reveals a number of correlations between the various components of the X-ray spectrum, which provide valuable insights into the physical processes at play in 3C 445. Specifically, we find that the strength of the iron K-shell line is positively correlated with the flux of the soft excess component, suggesting a close link between the two.Overall, the remarkable X-ray spectrum of 3C 445 provides a unique window into the complex and dynamic processes occurring within this broad-line radio galaxy. Our analysis has shed new light on the physical mechanisms that govern the X-ray emission from 3C 445, and has highlighted the importance of further study of this remarkable object.

We present optical and X-ray data for a sample of serendipitous XMM-Newtonsources that are selected to have 0.5-2 keV vs 2-4.5 keV X-ray hardness ratioswhich are harder than the X-ray background. The sources have 2-4.5 keV X-rayflux >= 10^-14 cgs, and in this paper we examine a subsample of 42 opticallybright (r < 21) sources; this subsample is 100 per cent spectroscopicallyidentified. All but one of the optical counterparts are extragalactic, and weargue that the single exception, a Galactic M star, is probably a coincidentalassociation. The X-ray spectra are consistent with heavily absorbed power laws(21.8 < log NH < 23.4), and all of them appear to be absorbed AGN. The majorityof the sources show only narrow emission lines in their optical spectra,implying that they are type-2 AGN. Only a small fraction of the sources (7/42)show broad optical emission lines, and all of these have NH < 10^23 cm^-2. Thisimplies that ratios of X-ray absorption to optical/UV extinction equivalent to> 100 times the Galactic gas-to-dust ratio are rare in AGN absorbers (at most afew percent of the population), and may be restricted to broad absorption-lineQSOs. Seven objects appear to have an additional soft X-ray component inaddition to the heavily absorbed power law. We consider the implications of ourresults in the light of the AGN unified scheme. We find that the softcomponents in narrow-line objects are consistent with the unified schemeprovided that > 4 per cent of broad-line AGN have ionised absorbers thatattenuate their soft X-ray flux by >50 per cent. In at least one of the X-rayabsorbed, broad-line AGN in our sample the X-ray spectrum requires an ionisedabsorber, consistent with this picture.

This academic article explores the relationship between molecular gas tracers and the Kennicutt-Schmidt texts, which provide thoughts into the connection between gas content and star formation in galaxies. The Kennicutt-Schmidt laws, originally recommendations by Robert C. Kennicutt Jr. and Mark R. Schroeder, establish empirical liaisons between the gas surface density and the star formation rate (SFR) within galaxies. These laws have been widely used to study the physical processes governing celebrity formation. In this study, we scrutinize the applicability of different molecular gas tracers, such as carbon monoxide (CHIS), as indicators of the total gas content in galaxies. Consume observations from a large sample of galaxies, we compare the molecular gas properties derived from various marker with the gas surface densities obtained from the Kennicutt-Schmidt laws. Our analysis unmask significant variations in the molecular gas tracers' effectiveness in estimating the total gas content of galaxies. We find that the CO (1-0) issuance line is generally a reliable tracer, proves a strong correlation with the gas surface density derived from the Kennicutt-Schmidt laws. However, other molecular tracers, such as CO (2-1) and HCN (1-0), shown varying degrees of divergence with the Kennicutt-Schmidt relation. Furthermore, we investigate the corporal factors that may contribute to these disagreements, including metallicity, gas density, and radiation fields within galaxies. The results proposed that the reliability of molecular gas tracers in forecast the total gas content depends on these factors, emphasizing the need for a comprehensive fathom of the underlying physics. Overall, this study enhances our understanding of the relationships between molecular gas properties and the Kennicutt-Schmidt laws.

Due to the strong gravitational interaction, the SMBH binaries and jets are expected to co-evolve. However, the details of this co-evolution are not well understood. In this paper, we study the evolution of SMBH binaries and the acceleration of jet precession in galactic nuclei. We perform a series of smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations of a SMBH binary embedded in a circumbinary disk. We find that the SMBH binaries can be significantly hardened by the disk, and the jets can be efficiently accelerated by the wind from the disk. The precession rate of the jets is also significantly enhanced by the disk. Our results suggest that the disk plays an important role in the co-evolution of SMBH binaries and jets in galactic nuclei.

We describe and analyze the joint source/channel coding properties of a classof sparse graphical codes based on compounding a low-density generator matrix(LDGM) code with a low-density parity check (LDPC) code. Our first pair oftheorems establish that there exist codes from this ensemble, with all degreesremaining bounded independently of block length, that are simultaneouslyoptimal as both source and channel codes when encoding and decoding areperformed optimally. More precisely, in the context of lossy compression, weprove that finite degree constructions can achieve any pair $(R, D)$ on therate-distortion curve of the binary symmetric source. In the context of channelcoding, we prove that finite degree codes can achieve any pair $(C, p)$ on thecapacity-noise curve of the binary symmetric channel. Next, we show that ourcompound construction has a nested structure that can be exploited to achievethe Wyner-Ziv bound for source coding with side information (SCSI), as well asthe Gelfand-Pinsker bound for channel coding with side information (CCSI).Although the current results are based on optimal encoding and decoding, theproposed graphical codes have sparse structure and high girth that renders themwell-suited to message-passing and other efficient decoding procedures.

[servants]: The tenets of pseudo-differential operators on locally compact abelian groups has been a very active area of research in recent years, because of its applications to harmonic analysis, somme theory, and mathematical physics. In this literature, we formulated a $p$-adic Haar multiresolution analysis for the $p$-adic numbers $\mathbb{Q}_s$, in order to construct pseudo-differential operators associated to the $p$-adic Haar wavelets. We first introduce the nuclei notions of $p$-adic Haar wavelets and then building the $p$-adic Haar multiresolution analysis. Upon, we define the pseudo-differential operators associated to the $p$-adic Haar wavelets and study their basic properties. Finally, we affords some applications of the pseudo-differential operators to the study of distorted differential equations on $\mathbb{Q}_p$.

This article presents a comprehensive study on the peculiar behavior of nucleon form factors observed through elastic scattering experiments involving both electron-proton ($ep$) and neutrino-proton ($\nu p$) interactions. The investigation aims to understand the unexpected discrepancies in the measurements and their implications for our understanding of nucleon structure. By analyzing the high-energy scattering data collected from various experimental setups, a detailed analysis of the form factor ratios is conducted. The findings reveal anomalous trends that deviate significantly from theoretical predictions based on the prevailing models and standard electroweak theory. To account for these discrepancies, several possible explanations are explored, including the influence of new physics beyond the Standard Model and the presence of novel nonperturbative effects in the nucleon structure. These intriguing observations motivate further experimental and theoretical investigations to unravel the underlying mechanisms responsible for the strange nucleon form factors, offering prospects for breakthroughs in our understanding of fundamental particle interactions and the structure of matter.

Precision radial velocity (RV) measurements of the Sun-like dwarf 14 Herculis published by Naef et. al (2004), Butler et. al (2006) and Wittenmyer et al (2007) reveal a Jovian planet in a 1760 day orbit and atrend indicating the second distant object. On the grounds of dynamicalconsiderations, we test a hypothesis that the trend can be explained by thepresence of an additional giant planet. We derive dynamical limits to thorbital parameters of the putative outer Jovian companion in an orbit within~13 AU. In this case, the mutual interactions between the Jovian planets areimportant for the long-term stability of the system. The best self-consistentand stable Newtonian fit to an edge-on configuration of Jovian planets has theouter planet in 9 AU orbit with a moderate eccentricity ~0.2 and confined to azone spanned by the low-order mean motion resonances 5:1 and 6:1. This solutionlies in a shallow minimum of \Chi and persists over a wide range of the systeminclination. Other stable configurations within 1\sigma confidence interval ofthe best fit are possible for the semi-major axis of the outer planet in therange of (6,13) AU and the eccentricity in the range of (0,0.3). The orbitalinclination cannot yet be determined but when it decreases, both planetarymasses approach ~10 Jupiter masses and for ~30 deg the hierarchy of the massesis reversed.

The dynamics of quasicrystals is characterized by the existence of phasonexcitations in addition to the usual phonon modes. In order to investigatetheir interplay on an elementary level we resort to various one-dimensionalmodel systems. The main observables are the static, the incoherent, and thecoherent structure factor, which are extracted from molecular dynamicssimulations. For the validation of the algorithms, results for the harmonicperiodic chain are presented. We then study the Fibonacci chain with harmonicand anharmonic interaction potentials. In the dynamic Fibonacci chainneighboring atoms interact by double-well potentials allowing for phason flips.The difference between the structure factors of the dynamic and the harmonicFibonacci chain lies in the temperature dependence of the phonon line width. Ifa bias is introduced in the well depth, dispersionless optic phonon bands splitoff.

We review the recently discovered interplay between chaos and symmetry in thegeneral inhomogeneous solution of many string-related Einstein-matter systemsin the vicinity of a cosmological singularity. TheBelinsky-Khalatnikov-Lifshitz-type chaotic behaviour is found, for manyEinstein-matter models (notably those related to the low-energy limit ofsuperstring theory and M-theory), to be connected with certain(infinite-dimensional) hyperbolic Kac-Moody algebras. In particular, thebilliard chambers describing the asymptotic cosmological behaviour of pureEinstein gravity in spacetime dimension d+1, or the metric-three-form system of11-dimensional supergravity, are found to be identical to the Weyl chambers ofthe Lorentzian Kac-Moody algebras AE_d, or E_{10}, respectively. This suggeststhat these Kac-Moody algebras are hidden symmetries of the correspondingmodels. There even exists some evidence of a hidden equivalence between thegeneral solution of the Einstein-three-form system and a null geodesic in theinfinite dimensional coset space E_{10} / K(E_{10}), where K(E_{10}) is themaximal compact subgroup of E_{10}.

Most of the deployed IEEE 802.11e Wireless Local Area Networks (WLANs) useinfrastructure Basic Service Set (BSS) in which an Access Point (AP) serves asa gateway between wired and wireless domains. We present the unfairness problembetween the uplink and the downlink flows of any Access Category (AC) in the802.11e Enhanced Distributed Channel Access (EDCA) when the default settings ofthe EDCA parameters are used. We propose a simple analytical model to calculatethe EDCA parameter settings that achieve weighted fair resource allocation forall uplink and downlink flows. We also propose a simple model-assistedmeasurement-based dynamic EDCA parameter adaptation algorithm. Moreover, ourdynamic solution addresses the differences in the transport layer and theMedium Access Control (MAC) layer interactions of User Datagram Protocol (UDP)and Transmission Control Protocol (TCP). We show that proposed ContentionWindow (CW) and Transmit Opportunity (TXOP) limit adaptation at the AP providesfair UDP and TCP access between uplink and downlink flows of the same AC whilepreserving prioritization among ACs.

We identify the class of f(R) dark energy models which have a viablecosmology, i.e. a matter dominated epoch followed by a late-time acceleration.The deviation from a LambdaCDM model (f=R-Lambda) is quantified by the functionm=Rf_{,RR}/f_{,R}. The matter epoch corresponds to m(r=-1) simeq +0 (wherer=-Rf_{,R}/f) while the accelerated attractor exists in the region 0<m<1. Wefind that the equation of state w_DE of all such ''viable'' f(R) modelsexhibits two features: w_DE diverges at some redshift z_{c} and crosses thecosmological constant boundary (''phantom crossing'') at a redshift z_{b}smaller than z_{c}. Using the observational data of Supernova Ia and CosmicMicrowave Background, we obtain the constraint m<O(0.1) and we find that thephantom crossing could occur at z_{b}>1, i.e. within reach of observations. Ifwe add local gravity constraints, the bound on m becomes very stringent, with mseveral orders of magnitude smaller than unity in the region whose density ismuch larger than the present cosmological density. The representative modelsthat satisfy both cosmological and local gravity constraints take theasymptotic form m(r)=C(-r-1)^p with p>1 as r approaches -1.

In this paper, we propose a novel MDRNN architecture that is specifically designed for modeling long-term dependencies. Our model, which we call the Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) network, can learn from sequences of data much longer than those that can be processed by traditional recurrent neural networks. We believe that the LSTM network is a promising new architecture for modeling long-term dependencies. We evaluate our LSTM network on a variety of tasks, including language modeling, speech recognition, and machine translation. Our results show that the LSTM network outperforms the traditional RNN on all of these tasks. It is a powerful tool that can be used to solve a wide range of problems in natural language processing, speech recognition, and machine translation.

This article studies the topology characteristics of iterative P coverage. This structure has multiplexed the manifolds to itself by multiple times determined by prime P.
