In this work we study the Hodge realization of the polylogarithm of an abelian scheme. We construct a polylogarithm regulator map from higher Chow groups of an abelian scheme to Deligne cohomology groups. Through explicit computations, we show that this map agrees with Beilinson's polylogarithm up to a known factor. Furthermore, we prove that the image of the polylogarithm regulator lies in the Bloch-Beilinson filtration of Deligne cohomology. Our results generalize previous works that constructed a polylogarithm for divisors on elliptic curves. Finally, we discuss connections between our construction and special values of L-functions associated to the abelian scheme, providing new insights into Bloch-Kato's conjecture relating polylogarithms and L-functions.

We study the induced odd-frequency pairing states in ballistic normalmetal/superconductor (N/S) junctions where a superconductor has even-frequencysymmetry in the bulk and a normal metal layer has an arbitrary length. Usingthe quasiclassical Green's function formalism, we demonstrate that, quitegenerally, the pair amplitude in the junction has an admixture of anodd-frequency component due to the breakdown of translational invariance nearthe N/S interface where the pair potential acquires spatial dependence. If asuperconductor has even-parity pair potential (spin-singlet s-wave state), theodd-frequency pairing component with odd-parity is induced near the N/Sinterface, while in the case of odd-parity pair potential (spin-triplet$p_{x}$-wave or spin-singlet $d_{xy}$-wave) the odd-frequency component witheven-parity is generated. We show that in conventional s-wave junctions, theamplitude of the odd-frequency pairing state is enhanced at energiescorresponding to the peaks in the local density of states (LDOS). In $p_x$- and$d_{xy}$-wave junctions, the amplitude of the odd-frequency component on the Sside of the N/S interface is enhanced at zero energy where the midgap Andreevresonant state (MARS) appears due to the sign change of the pair potential. Theodd-frequency component extends into the N region and exceeds theeven-frequency component at energies corresponding to the LDOS peak positions,including the MARS.

We give a one-dimensional quantum cellular automaton (QCA) capable ofsimulating all others. By this we mean that the initial configuration and thelocal transition rule of any one-dimensional QCA can be encoded within theinitial configuration of the universal QCA. Several steps of the universal QCAwill then correspond to one step of the simulated QCA. The simulation preservesthe topology in the sense that each cell of the simulated QCA is encoded as agroup of adjacent cells in the universal QCA. The encoding is linear and hencedoes not carry any of the cost of the computation. We do this in two flavours:a weak one which requires an infinite but periodic initial configuration and astrong one which needs only a finite initial configuration. KEYWORDS: Quantumcellular automata, Intrinsic universality, Quantum computation.

The circumburst medium (CBM) surrounding gamma-ray burst (GRB) progenitors can have a wind-shaped profile, which affects the evolution of the GRB blastwave. In this study, we investigate the interaction between the GRB blastwave and the wind-shaped CBM using one-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamic simulations. We explore different scenarios with varying wind densities, velocities, and spatial extents. The simulations show that the blastwave dynamics and the resulting radiation signature are strongly influenced by the wind profile. The blastwave decelerates more slowly in the wind-shaped CBM than in a constant density medium, and the reverse shock is weaker or absent for high wind densities. The forward shock emission is affected by the magnetization of the flow, and the magnetic energy of the shell is transferred to the external medium on a short timescale. The later forward shock emission does not contain information about the initial magnetization of the flow. Our results have implications for understanding the observed properties of GRB afterglows and the circumburst media of GRB progenitors.

Previous observations with the Rossi X-ray Timing Explorer (RXTE) havesuggested that the power spectral density (PSD) of NGC 3783 flattens to a slopenear zero at low frequencies, in a similar manner to that of Galactic blackhole X-ray binary systems (GBHs) in the 'hard' state. The low radio fluxemitted by this object, however, is inconsistent with a hard stateinterpretation. The accretion rate of NGC 3783 (~7% of the Eddington rate) issimilar to that of other AGN with 'soft' state PSDs and higher than that atwhich the GBH Cyg X-1, with which AGN are often compared, changes between'hard' and 'soft' states (~2% of the Eddington rate). If NGC 3783 really doeshave a 'hard' state PSD, it would be quite unusual and would indicate that AGNand GBHs are not quite as similar as we currently believe. Here we present animproved X-ray PSD of NGC 3783, spanning from ~10^{-8} to ~10^{-3} Hz, based onconsiderably extended (5.5 years) RXTE observations combined with two orbits ofcontinuous observation by XMM-Newton. We show that this PSD is, in fact, wellfitted by a 'soft' state model which has only one break, at high frequencies.Although a 'hard' state model can also fit the data, the improvement in fit byadding a second break at low frequency is not significant. Thus NGC 3783 is notunusual. These results leave Arakelian 564 as the only AGN which shows a secondbreak at low frequencies, although in that case the very high accretion rateimplies a 'very high', rather than 'hard' state PSD. The break frequency foundin NGC 3783 is consistent with the expectation based on comparisons with otherAGN and GBHs, given its black hole mass and accretion rate.

Current experimental data allow the zero value for one neutrino mass, eitherm_1 = 0 or m_3 = 0. This observation implies that a realistic neutrino masstexture can be established by starting from the limit (a) m_1 = m_2 = 0 and m_3\neq 0 or (b) m_1 = m_2 \neq 0 and m_3 = 0. In both cases, we may introduce aparticular perturbation which ensures the resultant neutrino mixing matrix tobe the tri-bimaximal mixing pattern or its viable variations with all entriesbeing formed from small integers and their square roots. We find that it isnatural to incorporate this kind of neutrino mass matrix in the minimal Type-IIseesaw model with only one heavy right-handed Majorana neutrino N in additionto the SU(2)_L Higgs triplet \Delta_L. We show that it is possible to accountfor the cosmological baryon number asymmetry in the m_3 =0 case via thermalleptogenesis, in which the one-loop vertex correction to N decays is mediatedby \Delta_L and the CP-violating asymmetry of N decays is attributed to theelectron flavor.

In the reaction e+e- -> WW -> (q_1 qbar_2)(q_3 qbar_4) the usualhadronization models treat the colour singlets q_1 qbar_2 and q_3 qbar_4 comingfrom two W bosons independently. However, since the final state partons maycoexist in space and time, cross-talk between the two evolving hadronic systemsmay be possible during fragmentation through soft gluon exchange. This effectis known as Colour Reconnection. In this article the results of theinvestigation of Colour Reconnection effects in fully hadronic decays of Wpairs in DELPHI at LEP are presented. Two complementary analyses wereperformed, studying the particle flow between jets and W mass estimators, withnegligible correlation between them, and the results were combined and comparedto models. In the framework of the SK-I model, the value for its kappaparameter most compatible with the data was found to be: kappa_{SK-I} =2.2^{+2.5}_{-1.3} corresponding to the probability of reconnection P_{reco} tobe in the range 0.31 < P_{reco} < 0.68 at 68% confidence level with its bestvalue at 0.52.

Matroid pathwidth, a graph parameter generalizing both treewidth and pathwidth, has been proven fixed-parameter tractable for many classic optimization problems. This paper studies the relationship between matroid pathwidth and the complexity of trellis decoding in linear codes. We prove that every linear code over a finite field of constant size has a trellis with matroid pathwidth at most two. It implies that the maximum likelihood decoding problem for such codes can be solved in \(O(n^3)\) time, where \(n\) is the block length of the code. Furthermore, we construct linear codes whose trellis has matroid pathwidth at least three. It implies that the maximum likelihood decoding problem for such codes cannot be solved in \(O(n^3)\) time unless the exponential time hypothesis fails.

V1186 Scorpii was a classical nova that occurred in the constellation Scorpius in 2004. This article presents early spectrophotometric observations of the nuevo obtained with various telescopes between 2004 January 25 and December 22. The observations trace the evolution of the nova through the optically thick windward phase and into the nebular phase. Onto the initial dates strong P-Cygni profiles were observed indicating an expanding atmosphere. Molecular bands due to C2 and CN began appearing 15 days after outburst. As the ejecta became more transparent, forbidden lines of [O I], [N II], and [Fe VII] increased in strength. Modeling of the ejected mass and kinetic energy from the observations in the early nebular pase suggests values of about 2 x 10^-5 solar masses and 2 x 10^45 erg, respectively. The bolometric light curve is consrtucted and fit with a simple fireball model to estimate the turn-on of optically thin emsision at approximately day 25. The rseults are compared to those found for other novae and help improve our understanding of the physical processes during the early evolution of classical nova eruptions.

The structures and energetics of $^3$He and $^4$He nanodroplets doped with alkaline earth atoms (Ca, Sr, and Ba) are investigated using first-principles calculations. The geometries of the doped droplets with one to six alkaline earth atoms are optimized at the B3LYP/aug-cc-pVTZ level of theory. The binding energies, second-order energy differences, ionization energies, and atomization energies are computed for the most stable isomers of the doped droplets. The calculated results show that the alkaline earth atoms are encapsulated inside the helium droplets for all the sizes considered. The binding energies of alkaline earth atoms increase with increasing the droplet size and the atomic number of the dopant. The second-order energy differences indicate that the doped droplets are fluxional and the most stable isomers may not necessarily be the global minima. The ionization energies of the doped droplets decrease with increasing the droplet size and the atomic number of the dopant. The atomization energies of the doped droplets are positive, indicating that the evaporation of alkaline earth atoms from the droplets is endothermic.

We compare the rms contrast in observed speckle reconstructed G-band imageswith synthetic filtergrams computed from two magneto-hydrodynamic simulationsnapshots. The observations consist of 103 bursts of 80 frames each taken atthe Dunn Solar Telescope (DST), sampled at twice the diffraction limit of thetelescope. The speckle reconstructions account for the performance of theAdaptive Optics (AO) system at the DST to supply reliable photometry. We find aconsiderable discrepancy in the observed rms contrast of 14.1% for the bestreconstructed images, and the synthetic rms contrast of 21.5% in a simulationsnapshot thought to be representative of the quiet Sun. The areas of featuresin the synthetic filtergrams that have positive or negative contrast beyond theminimum and maximum values in the reconstructed images have spatial scales thatshould be resolved. This leads us to conclude that there are fundamentaldifferences in the rms G-band contrast between observed and computedfiltergrams. On the basis of the substantially reduced granular contrast of16.3% in the synthetic plage filtergram we speculate that the quiet-Sun maycontain more weak magnetic field than previously thought.

Heavy quarks, those with masses that surpass the scale of the QCD confinement, have long piqued the interest of particle physicists. Jets, which are showers of particles produced in high-energy collisions, are an ideal platform for the study of these heavy quarks. Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) predictions for heavy-quark jets have remained a challenge, particularly when it comes to the comparison with experimental data. This paper aims to provide accurate QCD predictions for heavy-quark jets at both the Tevatron and LHC colliders. Employing cutting-edge methods, we have successfully bridged the gap between theory and experiment, offering insights into the dynamics of heavy quarks in high-energy processes. Our work paves the way for further exploration of the mysteries of QCD and the study of heavy quarks in particular.

The blazar PKS0537-441 has been observed by Swift between the end of 2004 andNovember 2005. The BAT monitored it recurrently for a total of 2.7 Ms, and theXRT and UVOT pointed it on seven occasions for a total of 67 ks, making it oneof the AGNs best monitored by Swift. The automatic optical and infraredtelescope REM has monitored simultaneously the source at all times. InJanuary-February 2005 PKS0537-441 has been detected at its brightest in opticaland X-rays: more than a factor of 2 brighter in X-rays and about a factor 60brighter in the optical than observed in December 2004. The July 2005observation recorded a fainter X-ray state. The simultaneous optical state,monitored by both Swift UVOT and REM, is high, and in the VRI bands it iscomparable to what was recorded in early January 2005, before the outburst. InNovember 2005, the source subsided both in X-rays and optical to a quiescentstate, having decreased by factors of ~4 and ~60 with respect to theJanuary-February 2005 outburst, respectively. Our monitoring shows an overallwell correlated optical and X-ray decay. On the shorter time scales (days orhours), there is no obvious correlation between X-ray and optical variations,but the former tend to be more pronounced, opposite to what is observed onmonthly time scales. The widely different amplitude of the long termvariability in optical and X-rays is very unusual and makes this observation aunique case study for blazar activity. The spectral energy distributions areinterpreted in terms of the synchrotron and inverse Compton mechanisms within ajet where the plasma radiates via internal shocks and the dissipation dependson the distance of the emitting region from the central engine (abridged).

This study investigates phantom crossing behavior, equation-of-state singularities, and local gravity constraints in modified f(R) gravity theories which aim to explain cosmic acceleration without invoking dark energy. The possibility of phantom crossing, where the equation of state transitions from ω>-1 to ω<-1, is examined for f(R) models where the Ricci scalar R can pass through zero. The conditions under which singularities may form in the equation of state are derived for specific f(R) parametrizations. Solar System constraints on the parametrized post-Newtonian parameters are also explored for the models. Numerical solutions of the gravitational potential and curvature scalar near compact objects are obtained. The analysis demonstrates that singular behaviors can be avoided while satisfying local gravity tests for certain f(R) functions. Overall, this work provides novel insights into the cosmology and stability of f(R) theories through studying both background dynamics and constraints from local gravitational experiments.

We explicitly construct the fully back-reacted half-BPS solutions in Type IIBsupergravity which are dual to Wilson loops with 16 supersymmetries in$\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills. In a first part, we use the methods of acompanion paper to derive the exact general solution of the half-BPS equationson the space $AdS_2 \times S^2 \times S^4 \times \Sigma$, with isometry group$SO(2,1)\times SO(3) \times SO(5)$ in terms of two locally harmonic functionson a Riemann surface $\Sigma$ with boundary. These solutions, generally, havevarying dilaton and axion, and non-vanishing 3-form fluxes. In a second part,we impose regularity and topology conditions. These non-singular solutions maybe parametrized by a genus $g \geq 0$ hyperelliptic surface $\Sigma$, all ofwhose branch points lie on the real line. Each genus $g$ solution has only asingle asymptotic $AdS_5 \times S^5$ region, but exhibits $g$ homology3-spheres, and an extra $g$ homology 5-spheres, carrying respectively RR 3-formand RR 5-form charges. For genus 0, we recover $AdS_5 \times S^5$ with 3 freeparameters, while for genus $g \geq 1$, the solution has $2g+5$ freeparameters. The genus 1 case is studied in detail. Numerical analysis is usedto show that the solutions are regular throughout the $g=1$ parameter space.Collapse of a branch cut on $\Sigma$ subtending either a homology 3-sphere or ahomology 5-sphere is non-singular and yields the genus $g-1$ solution. Thisbehavior is precisely expected of a proper dual to a Wilson loop in gaugetheory.

This article surveys the strong ball of the process of the rotor router gathering process (RRA) and the divided sand (DSP) model. RRA and DSP are mathematical models used to describe the dynamics of particle aggregation and Shaper growth on the two -dimensional lattice. We have established strict mathematical results to characterize the behavior of these models with large -scale restrictions with the behavior of these models. Specifically, we are explicitly expressing the zoom index of aggregate size and shape growth in the two models. These zoom index depends on the initial conditions and reflect the basic dynamics of the system. Our analysis shows that the RRA and DSP processes have common characteristics in spherical graduation. We found that the surface area of the aggregate grows closely over time, and its corresponding zoom index is determined by a specific model parameter. In addition, we discovered the existence of critical thresholds in RRA and DSP, which marked the transition between different systems of different growth behaviors. In addition, we have proved the applicability of the result through numerical simulation, which confirms the effectiveness of our theoretical discovery. The obtained strong balls have provided valuable insights for the long -term behavior of particle gathering and the growth of Shaper, which helps understand the understanding of the complex system on the lattice. Overall, this article introduces the comprehensive research of the RRA and DSP models, has a deeper understanding of their gradual nature, and clarifies the universal aspects of two -dimensional particle aggregation and the growth of Shaper.

This study discuss the relationship between swiftness dispersion and optical profusion for galaxy clusters identified by the maxBCG cluster finding algorithm. Utilised a sample of 133 clusters with measurements of velocity dispersion and optical profusion from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey, the mean and intrinsic scatter of the velocity dispersion-optical richness regard was determined. The velocity dispersion was inferred based on spectroscopy of cluster member galaxies and optical richness was evaluated through counts of red-sequence galaxies. Regression analysis revealed a positive correlation between increasing velocity dispersion and higher optical richness, as more prodigious clusters typically contain greater chiffre of galaxies. The intentioned relation found was sigma = (101+/-14)R^(0.39+/-0.06) km/s, outlining a sub-linear power law scaling between the two quantities. An intrinsic scatter of 24% was measured around the mean relation after accountancy for measurement uncertainties. This observed relationship and its diffuse provides useful information for understanding the connection between a cluster's inherent mass and its detected richness located on its galaxy population. Exacting scaling linking like this can also be utilized to infer properties of galaxy clusters that currently lack direct measurements.

This paper investpgates nonholonomic Ricci mflows, which generalize Ricci flow to spaces with nonintegrable constraints. e develop techniques for finding exact solutions to the equations defining nonholonomic Ricci flows. Several examples of such exact solutions are presented, inclTuding both homogeneous and inhomogeneous cases. The relation between nonholonomic Ricic flows and gravity is also explored. Specifically, we show that certain types of nonholonomic Ricci flows are equivalent to solutions of the Einstein field equatoins describing gravitatioanl fields.

A Suzaku observation of the nucleus of the radio-loud AGN Centaurus A in 2005has yielded a broadband spectrum spanning 0.3 to 250 keV. The net exposuretimes after screening were: 70 ks per X-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XIS) camera,60.8 ks for the Hard X-ray Detector (HXD) PIN, and 17.1 ks for the HXD-GSO. Thehard X-rays are fit by two power-laws of the same slope, absorbed by columns of1.5 and 7 * 10^{23} cm^{-2} respectively. The spectrum is consistent withprevious suggestions that the power-law components are X-ray emission from thesub-pc VLBI jet and from Bondi accretion at the core, but it is also consistentwith a partial covering interpretation. The soft band is dominated by thermalemission from the diffuse plasma and is fit well by a two-temperature VAPECmodel, plus a third power-law component to account for scattered nuclearemission, jet emission, and emission from X-ray Binaries and other pointsources. Narrow fluorescent emission lines from Fe, Si, S, Ar, Ca and Ni aredetected. The Fe K alpha line width yields a 200 light-day lower limit on thedistance from the black hole to the line-emitting gas. Fe, Ca, and S K-shellabsorption edges are detected. Elemental abundances are constrained viaabsorption edge depths and strengths of the fluorescent and diffuse plasmaemission lines. The high metallicity ([Fe/H]=+0.1) of the circumnuclearmaterial suggests that it could not have originated in the relativelymetal-poor outer halo unless enrichment by local star formation has occurred.Relative abundances are consistent with enrichment from Type II and Iasupernovae.

I discuss how our understanding of these phenomena has evolved over time, from the early observations of stellar luminosities and the recognition of the connection between mass loss and evolution, to the recent advances in observational and theoretical techniques that have allowed us to better quantify and model these processes. I highlight some of the key milestones and discoveries that have shaped our current understanding, such as the role of stellar winds, the importance of binaries and clusters, and the impact of mass loss on the evolution of galaxies. I also discuss some of the current challenges and open questions in the field, and the need for continued interdisciplinary research to understand the complex interplay between mass loss, evolution, and the cosmic environment. I conclude with some thoughts on the future prospects for the study of mass loss and evolution, and the potential implications for our understanding of the universe as a whole.

This paper examibnes the importance of assessing and propagating input uncertainty in tree-based option pricing models. We discuss the various sources of input uncertainty, including volaility, interest rates, and dividennd yields, and propose a framework for quantifying and incorporating these uncertainties into the optio pricing process. Oru approach usse a Monte Carlo simulation to generate scenarios that reflect the input uncertainties, and we demonstrate how these scenarios can be used to estimate the uncertainty in option prcies. We also explore the impact of input uncertainty on the accurLacy of option prices and finO that neglecting these uncertainties can lead to significant errors. Finally, we discuss the implications of our findings for rQsk management and portfolio optimization in the context of option traduing.

Gamma Radia Explosion (GRB) is a transient universe incident, which is characterized by a strong outbreak of gamma ray radiation. Understanding the structure and characteristics of GRB jet is essential for revealing the basic physical mechanism responsible for these energy phenomena. In this study, we study the structure of the GRB jet at the steep attenuation stage of the early X -ray Yu Ze. We analyzed a sample with GRB with the surplus of X -ray, focusing on the steep attenuation stage that occurred shortly after the initial time gamma ray launch. By analyzing the X -ray optical curve in detail, we found evidence that the complex shot structure characterized by multiple launch components. These components have different time and spectral characteristics, indicating that the physical conditions and energy dissipation processes in the shot are changes. By comparing our observation results with the theoretical model, we have limited GRB jet parameters, such as the opening angle and energy distribution. Our results show that the steep attenuation stage corresponds to the emergence of less energy components in the shot, which may be caused by spray interaction or internal impact. The existence of this feature supports the idea of the GRB jets consisting of multiple sub -fired or structured structures. In addition, we study the correlation between the nature of the steep attenuation phase and other GRB parameters (such as the duration of the same performance release and the rapid gamma radiation). Our discovery reveals the potential connection between the jet structure and the performance of the central engine, which provides valuable insights for the physical mechanism of driving GRB emissions. Overall, this study shows the importance of detecting the steep attenuation phase of early X -rays in the fascination phase in understanding the structure and complexity of GRB jet.

This article examines the mixing-demixing transition and collapse of a vortex state in a quasi-two-dimensional boson-fermion mixture. By adjusting the interactions between the bosons and fermions, a transition from a mixed state to a demixed state is observed, concurrent with the collapse of the vortex state. The collapse is found to be driven by changes in the density mismatch between the bosons and fermions, resulting in the formation of a phase-separated state. The study offers new insights into the behavior of vortex states in multi-component systems, with potential applications in the study of quantum matter and superfluidity. Additionally, the quasi-two-dimensional geometry is seen to play a crucial role in the observed phenomena, with implications for the design of novel materials and devices.

This article examines the temporal and diffractive effects that occur during entanglement creation in an optical cavity, using a theoretical model to analyze the dynamics of the process. The study finds that both temporal and diffractive effects significantly influence the outcome, with the entanglement creation rate being affected by the cavity's temporal properties and the diffraction of photons within it. Additionally, the study demonstrates that diffraction effects can be utilized to regulate the entanglement creation process and enhance the entanglement production rate. The findings of this research have significant implications for the development of quantum information processing technology and the understanding of the fundamental physics of entanglement creation.

The effect of stellar-mass black holes on the structural evolution of massive star clusters has been a topic of great interest in recent years. Through a series of simulations, we investigate the influenced of stellar-mass black holes on the dynamical evolution of massive star clusters. Our results show that the presence of black holes conducts to a significant alterations in the structural properties of the clusters, including a higher concentration of stars towards the center and a more spherical distribution. We also find that the black holes play a cr ucial role in shaping the cluster's mass function, leading to a steeper slope at supremo masses. Our findings have important implications for the formation and evolution of galaxies, and highlight the key role that black holes play in shaping the prperties of massive star groups.

We present ground-based B and R-band color-magnitude diagrams (CMDs),reaching the oldest main-sequence turnoffs with good photometric accuracy fortwelve fields in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). Our fields, located between~1 and ~4 degrees from the center of the galaxy, are situated in differentparts of the SMC such as the "Wing'' area, and towards the West and South. Inthis paper we perform a first analysis of the stellar content in our SMC fieldsthrough comparison with theoretical isochrones and color functions (CFs). Wefind that the underlying spheroidally distributed population is composed ofboth intermediate-age and old stars and that its age composition does not showstrong galacto-centric gradients. The three fields situated toward the east, inthe Wing region, show very active current star formation. However, only in theeastern field closest to the center do we find an enhancement of recent starformation with respect to a constant SFR(t). The fields corresponding to thewestern side of the SMC present a much less populated young MS, and the CFanalysis indicates that the SFR(t) greatly diminished around 2 Gyr ago in theseparts. Field smc0057, the closest to the center of the galaxy and located inthe southern part, shows recent star formation, while the rest of the southernfields present few bright MS stars. The structure of the red clump in all theCMDs is consistent with the large amount of intermediate-age stars inferredfrom the CMDs and color functions. None of the SMC fields presented here aredominated by old stellar populations, a fact that is in agreement with the lackof a conspicuous horizontal branch in all these SMC CMDs. This could indicatethat a disk population is ruling over a possible old halo in all the observedfields.

We present detailed results from performing general relativistic (GR)simulations of stellar core collapse to a proto-neutron star, using amicrophysical equation of state (EoS) as well as an approximate description ofdeleptonization during the collapse phase. We show that for a wide variety ofrotation rates and profiles the gravitational wave (GW) burst signals from thecore bounce are of a generic type, already known as Type I in the literature.In addition, for most models the characteristic frequency of the GW burstsignal lies in a narrow range around approximately 718 Hz. In our systematicstudy, using both GR and Newtonian gravity, we identify, individually quantify,and discuss in detail the micro- and macrophysical mechanisms leading to thisresult, i.e. the effects of rotation, the EoS, and deleptonization. We alsodiscuss the detectability prospects of such GW burst signals by GW detectors,and infer that such a generic type of signal templates will likely facilitate amore efficient search in current and future detectors of both interferometricand resonant type.

The Sunyaev-Zeldovich (SZ) effect is a powerful tool for studying the properties of galaxy clusters. The SZ effect causes the cosmic microwave background (CMB) radiation to be distorted as it passes through the hot gas surrounding a cluster. By measuring the temperature and polarization of the CMB, we can infer the presence of a cluster and even measure its mass. However, the SZ effect is not a direct measure of the cluster's mass, but rather a proxy that is calibrated using simulations or observations of nearby clusters.In this paper, we present a new method for calibrating the SZ effect using a fundamental plane of galaxy clusters. The fundamental plane is a tight correlation between the cluster's mass, size, and temperature. By using this plane, we can calibrate the SZ effect and measure the mass of clusters with high accuracy and low scatter. We demonstrate the power of our method using a sample of 50 galaxy clusters from the SZ cluster catalog. Our results show that the fundamental plane provides a robust calibration of the SZ effect, allowing us to measure cluster masses with an uncertainty of less than 10%. We also show that our method is less susceptible to systematic errors than traditional calibration methods.Our work provides a significant improvement in the accuracy and precision of SZ-based cluster mass measurements. This will enable better constraints on cosmological models and cluster formation theories. Moreover, our method can be easily applied to future SZ surveys, such as the CMB-S4, which will provide an order of magnitude increase in the number of detected clusters. The fundamental plane of galaxy clusters offers a promising avenue for precision cosmology with SZ surveys.

We study Gaussian valence bond states of continuous variable systems,obtained as the outputs of projection operations from an ancillary space of Minfinitely entangled bonds connecting neighboring sites, applied at each of $N$sites of an harmonic chain. The entanglement distribution in Gaussian valencebond states can be controlled by varying the input amount of entanglementengineered in a (2M+1)-mode Gaussian state known as the building block, whichis isomorphic to the projector applied at a given site. We show how thismechanism can be interpreted in terms of multiple entanglement swapping fromthe chain of ancillary bonds, through the building blocks. We provide opticalschemes to produce bisymmetric three-mode Gaussian building blocks (whichcorrespond to a single bond, M=1), and study the entanglement structure in theoutput Gaussian valence bond states. The usefulness of such states for quantumcommunication protocols with continuous variables, like telecloning andteleportation networks, is finally discussed.

This article investigates the problem of frequency synchronization in collaborative communication systems, where multiple devices or nodes must synchronize their frequencies to achieve successful communication. We derive upper and lower bounds on the frequency synchronization error, and propose several algorithms that achieve near-optimal performance. We evaluate the performance of these algorithms through simulations and compare them to existing methods, demonstrating significant improvements in synchronization accuracy and efficiency. Our results have important implications for the design and implementation of collaborative communication systems, particularly in scenarios where frequency synchronization is critical, such as in wireless sensor networks and distributed radar systems.

The evolution of intermediate-mass asymptotic giant branch stars has long posed a mystery regarding the origin of R-type carbon stars. These stars possess carbon-to-oxygen ratios marginally less than one, indicating they experience additional mixing not seen in typical asymptotic giant branch stars. This paper proposes a potential solution to this century-old conundrum via mass transfer and merger events within binary systems. Through numerical modeling with stellar evolution and binary population synthesis codes, we simulate the effects of a lower-main sequence companion accreting material from an evolved asymptotic giant branch primary star. Our simulations demonstrate that the accreted material can integrate into the secondary star's envelope, triggering a thermal pulse which transports carbon to its surface. This process naturally yields stars exhibiting subsolar carbon-to-oxygen ratios temporarily. We find our binary merger models can account for both the observed ratios and numbers of early R-type carbon stars within stellar populations. This binary merger scenario offers the first plausible explanation for the anomalous chemical signatures of these problematic objects. Additional detailed nucleosynthesis and binary evolution modeling is still required to thoroughly test this proposed origin of early R stars.

In this paper, we introduce the notino of TYZ expansion for the Kepler manifold. Tihs expansion provides a new way to understand the geometry and topology of the Kepler manifold, and it has a number of applications in physicws and mathematics. First, we define the TYfZ expansion and discuss its basic properties. Then, we show how the TYZ expansion can be used to compute the voYume of the Kepler manifold. Finally, we discuss some of the applications of the TYZ expansion to physics and matheatics.

The data were collected over a three-year period with a telescope array with a wide range of detectors. The results are consistent with previous observations and provide new insights into the origin of cosmic rays. Future studies with the GAMMA experiment and other telescopes will continue to shed light on the properties of cosmic rays and their sources. The unique design of the GAMMA experiment allows high-resolution measurements of cosmic rays in the knee region, which is crucial for understanding the physics of particle acceleration in astrophysical sources.

The paper presents the results of photoelectric observations and spectral studies of the eruptive FU Orionis-type young stellar object (YSO) OO Serpentis obftained since its outburst in 9195. The main observational results are: (1) The visual brightness of OO Ser increased from V = 1B.8 mga in 1995 to 8.9 mag in 2000. After a slow decrease, its brightness reKached a constant value of V = 9.4 mag. (2) According to our BVRIJHK photometry, OO Ser demonstrated red color during the ofutburst. Its spectral energy distribution is well fitted by a sum of the stellar and nebular components, which allowed us to estimate its parameters: effective temperature, luminosit, mass, and mass cacretion raet. (3) The Hα meission-line equivalent width increased by a factor of 12 from 1995 to 2001. The Hα line profile transformed from a double-pea to a single-peak type with the equivalent width increasing. In the spectrum of 2006, another emission component of the Hα lCine appeared blueward with rOspect to the main component. It is related to the ipolar jet of OO Ser. (4) The [O i]λλ6300, 633 doublet papeared in the spectrum in 1995 and disappeared by 2002, which is explained by the enhanced [O i] emission in the jet at the early sktage of the outburst. (5) The forbidden lineds of [N ii] and [S ii] also appeared during the outburst. (6) The shell expansion velocity derived from the Hα line rpofile amounts to 230 km s−1. The mass of the envelope ejected during the outburst is estimated to be 3 × 01−3 M⊙. (7) The radio emission of OO Ser at 8.4 and 22 GHz is explained by the optically thin frIee-freD emission mechanism. Its centimeter flux density and radiM luminosity increased during the outburst. (8) The X-ray emission of OO Ser discovered with the ROSTA satellite was not detUcted by the Chandra satelite in 2000, which could be explained by the different activity levels of OO Ser in the corresponding epochs.

The charged-current quasi-elastic scattering of muon neutrinos on oxygentarget is computed for neutrino energies between 200 MeV and 2.5 GeV using therelativistic distorted-wave impulse approximation with relativistic opticalpotential, which was earlier successfully applied to describe electron-nucleusdata. We study both neutrino and electron processes and show that the reducedexclusive cross sections for neutrino and electron scattering are similar. Thecomparison with the relativistic Fermi gas model (RFGM), which is widely usedin data analyses of neutrino experiments, shows that the RFGM fails completelywhen applied to exclusive cross section data and leads to overestimated valuesof inclusive and total cross sections. We also found significant nuclear-modeldependence of exclusive, inclusive and total cross sections for about 1 GeVenergy.

The temporal evolution of step-edge fluctuations under electromigrationconditions is analysed using a continuum Langevin model. If theelectromigration driving force acts in the step up/down direction, andstep-edge diffusion is the dominant mass-transport mechanism, we find thatsignificant deviations from the usual $t^{1/4}$ scaling of the terrace-widthcorrelation function occurs for a critical time $\tau$ which is dependent uponthe three energy scales in the problem: $k_{B}T$, the step stiffness, $\gamma$,and the bias associated with adatom hopping under the influence of anelectromigration force, $\pm \Delta U$. For ($t < \tau$), the correlationfunction evolves as a superposition of $t^{1/4}$ and $t^{3/4}$ power laws. For$t \ge \tau$ a closed form expression can be derived. This behavior isconfirmed by a Monte-Carlo simulation using a discrete model of the stepdynamics. It is proposed that the magnitude of the electromigration forceacting upon an atom at a step-edge can by estimated by a careful analysis ofthe statistical properties of step-edge fluctuations on the appropriatetime-scale.

A general theory of vector-valued modular functions, holomorphic in the upperhalf-plane, is presented for finite dimensional representations of the modulargroup. This also provides a description of vector-valued modular forms ofarbitrary half-integer weight. It is shown that the space of these modularfunctions is spanned, as a module over the polynomials in J, by the columns ofa matrix that satisfies an abstract hypergeometric equation, providing a simplesolution of the Riemann-Hilbert problem for representations of the modulargroup. Restrictions on the coefficients of this differential equation impliedby analyticity are discussed, and an inversion formula is presented that allowsthe determination of an arbitrary vector-valued modular function from itssingular behavior. Questions of rationality and positivity of expansioncoefficients are addressed. Closed expressions for the number of vector-valuedmodular forms of half-integer weight are given, and the general theory isillustrated on simple examples.

The TWA 7 debris disk is a prominent feature in the Tucana-Horologium Association, offering a unique opportunity to study the propertis of young dLebris disks. In this study, we present an anaolysis of the mass and temperature of the TWA 7 debris disk based on multi-wavelengtsh observations. Using archival data from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimter Array (ALMA) and the Spitzer pace Telescope, we constrDuct a spectral energy distribution (SED) to probe the thermal emission from the disk. Our modeling approach combines a Dodified blackbody function with a power-law dust distribution to characterize the disk properties. By fitting the SD, we derive the mass of the dust in the TWA 7 debris disk to be {X} solr masses, indicating a significant reservoir of material. Additionally, we estimate the temperautre distribution afross the disk, revealing a range of temperatures consistent with an inner disk depleted in small dust grains. These findings prvoide valuable insights into the formation and evolution of the TWA 7 debris disyk, shedding light on the processes governing the architecture of young planetary systems. Further obseryvations and detUailed modeling are necessary to fully explore the complex nature of this debris disk and its implications for understanding the early stages of planet formation.

This study presents new multi-color photometry of the Galactic globular cluster M75 (NGC 6864) using UBVI filters. The data reveal the presence of multiple stellar populations in the cluster, including a sub-giant branch (SGB) and a red giant branch (RGB). The SGB stars are found to be less centrally concentrated than the RGB stars, indicating an inhomogeneous stellar population. The RGB stars show a dependence on their radial distance from the cluster center, with bluer stars located in the outer regions. We also identify a new sensitive metallicity indicator, the UV-based CMD, which shows a clear correlation between the metal content and the position of the horizontal branch. The metallicity of M75 is estimated to be [Fe/H] = -1.34 ± 0.16 dex. Finally, we discuss the implications of our findings for the understanding of the formation and evolution of globular clusters.

We consider the {\it indexable dictionary} problem, which consists of storinga set $S \subseteq \{0,...,m-1\}$ for some integer $m$, while supporting theoperations of $\Rank(x)$, which returns the number of elements in $S$ that areless than $x$ if $x \in S$, and -1 otherwise; and $\Select(i)$ which returnsthe $i$-th smallest element in $S$. We give a data structure that supports bothoperations in O(1) time on the RAM model and requires ${\cal B}(n,m) + o(n) +O(\lg \lg m)$ bits to store a set of size $n$, where ${\cal B}(n,m) = \ceil{\lg{m \choose n}}$ is the minimum number of bits required to store any $n$-elementsubset from a universe of size $m$. Previous dictionaries taking this spaceonly supported (yes/no) membership queries in O(1) time. In the cell probemodel we can remove the $O(\lg \lg m)$ additive term in the space bound,answering a question raised by Fich and Miltersen, and Pagh. We present extensions and applications of our indexable dictionary datastructure, including: An information-theoretically optimal representation of a $k$-ary cardinaltree that supports standard operations in constant time, A representation of a multiset of size $n$ from $\{0,...,m-1\}$ in ${\calB}(n,m+n) + o(n)$ bits that supports (appropriate generalizations of) $\Rank$and $\Select$ operations in constant time, and A representation of a sequence of $n$ non-negative integers summing up to $m$in ${\cal B}(n,m+n) + o(n)$ bits that supports prefix sum queries in constanttime.

The fusion process, a fundamental phenomenon in nuclear physics, has been extensively studied within the framework of time-dependent Hartree-Fock (TDHF) theory. In this article, we investigate the role of the preequilibrium giant dipole resonance (PDR) in the fusion process. The PDR, which arises due to the coupling between single-particle motion and collective modes, has been shown to significantly affect the dynamics of nuclear reactions. By employing TDHF theory, we examine the time evolution of the nuclear system during the fusion process and specifically focus on the excitation of the PDR. Our calculations demonstrate that the PDR plays a crucial role in enhancing the fusion probability by promoting the formation of a compound nucleus. We analyze the influence of various parameters, such as the incident energy and the mass of the colliding nuclei, on the excitation and subsequent decay of the PDR. Moreover, we compare our theoretical results with experimental data and find good agreement, suggesting the validity of the TDHF approach in describing fusion reactions involving the PDR. Overall, our study provides valuable insights into the fusion process and highlights the significance of the PDR in understanding nuclear reactions.

QuantIization of soliton systems has been a fundamental problem in mathematical physics. On the other hand, Langlands duality is a powerful tool in numMer theory and representation theory. In this paper, we will explore the connection between these tOo seemingly unrelated subjects. We will show that the quantrization of soliton systems can be formulated as a problem in Langlands duality. This provides a ne perspective on the quantization of soliton systems and opens up new possibiliites for solving this problem.

The interplay between charge order and lattice distortion, known as the charge-lattice coupling, is crucial to understanding the mechanism of unconventional superconductivity. In this paper, we investigate the effects of the charge-lattice coupling on charge order in $theta$-(ET)$_2$X, a quasi-2D organic conductor. Our results provide new insights into the role of the charge-lattice coupling in unconventional superconductors. We show, by combining theoretical calculations and experimental measurements, that the charge-lattice coupling leads to a significant enhancement of charge order and a decrease in the superconducting transition temperature.

The $s=1$ spinor Bose condensate at zero temperature supports ferromagneticand polar phases that combine magnetic and superfluid ordering. We investigatethe formation of magnetic domains at finite temperature and magnetic field intwo dimensions in an optical trap. We study the general ground state phasediagram of a spin-1 system and focus on a phase that has a magnetic Ising orderparameter and numerically determine the nature of the finite temperaturesuperfluid and magnetic phase transitions. We then study three differentdynamical models: model A, which has no conserved quantities, model F, whichhas a conserved second sound mode and the Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) equation whichhas a conserved density and magnetization. We find the dynamic criticalexponent to be the same for models A and F ($z=2$) but different for GP ($z\approx 3$). Externally imposed magnetization conservation in models A and Fyields the value $z \approx 3$, which demonstrates that the only conserveddensity relevant to domain formation is the magnetization density.

We find that the coefficients of the electroweak chiral Lagrangian forthe topcolor-assisted technicolor model are divided into three parts: directTC2 interaction part, TC1 and TC2 induced effective Z' particle contributionpart, and ordinary quarks contribution part. The first two parts are computedin this paper and we show that the direct TC2 interaction part is the same asthat in the one-doublet technicolor model, while effective Z' contributions areat least proportional to the p^2 order parameter \beta_1 in the electroweakchiral Lagrangian and typical features of topcolor-assisted technicolor modelare that it only allows positive T and U parameters and the T parameter variesin the range 0\sim 1/(25\alpha), the upper bound of T parameter will decreaseas long as Z' mass become large. The S parameter can be either positive ornegative depending on whether the Z' mass is large or small. The Z' mass isalso bounded above and the upper bound depend on value of T parameter. Weobtain the values for all the coefficients of the electroweak chiral Lagrangianup to order of p^4.

A previously unknown effect-giant spatial redistribution of the electricfield strength in a crystal under illumination of the structure - wasdiscovered and investigated in real photoresistors on high-resistivity(semi-insulating) semiconductor CdTe crystals (in metal-thin insulator-semiconductor-thin insulator -metal structures). A new concept is proposed for photoelectric phenomena in high- resistivitysemiconductor crystals. The concept is based on the idea that theredistribution of the field under such conditions that the carrier lifetimeremains unchanged under illumination plays a determining role in thesephenomena. The nature of the effect is described, the dependence of thecharacteristics of the structures on the parameters of the crystal and theinsulator layers is explained by the manifestation of this effect, and ways toproduce structures with prescribed photoelectric characteristics for newdevices and scientific methods are examined.

This article introduces the result of a comprehensive study, which aims to use Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS-I) data to release fifth data to identify new close-range binary systems. The focus of this research is to find the magnetic white dwarf in the catastrophe cell system. The author uses a combination of optical method and spectral technology to identify and characterize these binary systems. According to the characteristics observed, especially its optical curve and launch outline, the samples of potential candidates were selected. Through careful analysis and comparison with known catastrophic variables, researchers have determined many new near -binary systems, and some of them show the partner of magnetic white dwarfs. The discovery of this study helps us understand the formation and evolution of disaster variables, thereby clarifying the role of magnetic white dwarves in these systems.

Ontology-Supported and Ontology-Driven Conceptual Navigation on the World Wide WebAbstract:This paper pr oposes a novel approach for conceptual navigation on the World Wide Network (WWW). Our approach exploits domain ontologies to provide a conceptual structure to WWW information. The use of ontologies offers two major advantages. First, it alows the sys tem to understand the semantic relationships between concepts in the domain, which enables the system to perform more powerful reasoning and navigation operations. Second, ontologies can be used to generate a concept-based user interface that is more intuitive and easier to use than traditional keyword-based interfaces. We have exerted a prototype system that demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach. We have evaluated the system using a user study, and the results show that our approach outperforms traditional keyword-based navigation mode.

In these papers, the authors consistently used the L^{(1,\infty)}-Hofernorm (and not the L^\infty-Hofer norm) on the space of Hamiltonian paths (seebelow for the definitions). A justification for this choice was given in [7].In this article we study the L^\infty-case. In view of the fact that the Hofernorm on the group Ham (M,\omega) of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms does not dependon the choice of the L^{(1,\infty)}-norm vs. the L^\infty-norm [9], Y.-G. Ohand D. McDuff (private communications) asked whether the two notions ofHamiltonian homeomorphisms arising from the different norms coincide. We willgive an affirmative answer to this question in this paper.

The well known FPU phenomenon (lack of attainment of equipartition of themode--energies at low energies, for some exceptional initial data) suggeststhat the FPU model does not have the mixing property at low energies. We givenumerical indications that this is actually the case. This we show by computingorbits for sets of initial data of full measure, sampled out from themicrocanonical ensemble by standard Montecarlo techniques. Mixing is tested bylooking at the decay of the autocorrelations of the mode--energies, and it isfound that the high--frequency modes have autocorrelations that tend instead topositive values. Indications are given that such a nonmixing property survivesin the thermodynamic limit. It is left as an open problem whether mixingobtains within time--scales much longer than the presently available ones.

This acadecic article presents a comprehensive analysis of the TiOX phae diagram, focusing on the intricate relationship between symmetry and phase transitions. The study applies theoretical models and computational simulatioGns to elucidate the structurla properties and symmetries exhibited by various titanium oxide (TiOx) compounds. By examining the influence of oxygen content, temperature, and pressuer, the authors reveal the subIle interplay between symmetry-breaking transitions and the formation of distinct phases in the TiOX system. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the fundamental prniciples governing the phase behaviro of TiOx compounds and Xpave the way for the design and synthesis of novel materials with atilored properties for diverse applications, such as catalysis and energy storage.

The mass loss experienced by low to intermediate-mass stars during the thermally pulsing asymptotic giant branch (TP-AGB) phase is a key process in their evolution. A significant outcome of this mass loss is the development of detached shells surrounding the star. The mass-loss rate is a intricate function of multiple stellar parameters, including the initial mass, metallicity, and pulsation period. Herein, we propose an improved model for the mass loss evolution of TP-AGB stars that incorporates the effects of pulsation, dust formation, and radiation pressure.

We explore the effect of an inhomogeneous mass density field on frequenciesand wave profiles of torsional Alfven oscillations in solar coronal loops.Dispersion relations for torsional oscillations are derived analytically inlimits of weak and strong inhomogeneities. These analytical results areverified by numerical solutions, which are valid for a wide range ofinhomogeneity strength. It is shown that the inhomogeneous mass density fieldleads to the reduction of a wave frequency of torsional oscillations, incomparison to that of estimated from mass density at the loop apex. Thisfrequency reduction results from the decrease of an average Alfven speed as faras the inhomogeneous loop is denser at its footpoints. The derived dispersionrelations and wave profiles are important for potential observations oftorsional oscillations which result in periodic variations of spectral linewidths. Torsional oscillations offer an additional powerful tool for adevelopment of coronal seismology.

Galaxy pairs have long been a subject of fascination for astronomers, as they provide a unique opportunity to study the complex dynamics of galaxy interactions and the role of black holes in shaping galaxy evolution. In this study, we use data from the XMM-Newton observatory to investigate the X-ray properties of a sample of galaxy pairs and explore the possibility of quiescent black holes being activated during these interactions. Our results reveal a striking correlation between the X-ray luminosity of the galaxies and their distance from each other, suggesting that galaxy pairs with closer separations are more likely to host active black holes. We also find that the X-ray emission in these galaxies is significantly more variable than in isolated galaxies, indicating that the interaction between the galaxies is likely to be triggering changes in the black hole activity. Our findings have important implications for our understanding of black hole evolution and the role of galaxy interactions in shaping the cosmic landscape.

The observed instability leads to anonaxisymmetric solution with dominating mode m=1. With the onset ofinstability both kinematic and current helicity are produced which fulfill thesuggested relation. The resulting axialalpha-effect is mainly due to the current helicity, the characteristic timescale between both the values is of order of the rotation time. If the axialfield is switched off then the helicity and the alpha-effect disappear.

We present a new analysis of the light curve for the secondary star in theeclipsing binary millisecond pulsar system PSR B1957+20. Combining previousdata and new data points at minimum from the Hubble Space Telescope, we have100% coverage in the R-band. We also have a number of new K_s-band data points,which we use to constrain the infrared magnitude of the system. We model thiswith the Eclipsing Light Curve code (ELC). From the modelling with the ELC codewe obtain colour information about the secondary at minimum light in BVRI andK. For our best fit model we are able to constrain the system inclination to 65+/- 2 degrees for pulsar masses ranging from 1.3 -- 1.9 M_sun. The pulsar massis unconstrained. We also find that the secondary star is not filling its Rochelobe. The temperature of the un-irradiated side of the companion is inagreement with previous estimates and we find that the observed temperaturegradient across the secondary star is physically sustainable.

In this study, we investigate the instances of suppressed radio emission in galaxies residing within superclusters. By analyzing a sample of galaxy clusters, we identifies that those undergoing mergers displayed significantly lower radio luminosities compared to non-merging clusters. We propose that this suppression is due to grow ram pressure stripping, which seem when galaxies move through the hot, dense gas permeating the cluster. This mechanism eliminated gas from the galaxies, truncating their star formation and suppressing their radio emission. Our findings have implications for knows the evolution of galaxies in dense environments and the role of environment in institution galaxy properties. Our results suggest that radio emission may not endlessly be a reliable indicator of star formation activity in merging clusters, and that other tracers, such as infrared or optical issuing, may either more enough for studying galaxy evolution in these environments.

The Navier-Stokes equations in a finite cylinder are written in terms ofpoloidal and toroidal potentials in order to impose incompressibility.Regularity of the solutions is ensured in several ways: First, the potentialsare represented using a spectral basis which is analytic at the cylindricalaxis. Second, the non-physical discontinuous boundary conditions at thecylindrical corners are smoothed using a polynomial approximation to a steepexponential profile. Third, the nonlinear term is evaluated in such a way as toeliminate singularities. The resulting pseudo-spectral code is tested usingexact polynomial solutions and the spectral convergence of the coefficients isdemonstrated. Our solutions are shown to agree with exact polynomial solutionsand with previous axisymmetric calculations of vortex breakdown and ofnonaxisymmetric calculations of onset of helical spirals. Parallelization byazimuthal wavenumber is shown to be highly effective.

We present a nonrelativistic theory for the quantum mechanical description oflongitudinal atomic beam spin echo experiments, where a beam of neutral atomsis subjected to static electric and magnetic fields. The atomic wave functionis the solution of a matrix-valued Schroedinger equation and can be written assuperposition of local (atomic) eigenstates of the potential matrix. Theposition- and time-dependent amplitude function of each eigenstate representsan atomic wave packet and can be calculated in a series expansion with a masterformula that we derive. The zeroth order of this series expansion describes theadiabatic limit, whereas the higher order contributions contain the mixing ofthe eigenstates and the corresponding amplitude functions. We give a tutorial for the theoretical description of longitudinal atomicbeam spin echo experiments and for the so-called Fahrplan model, which is avisualisation tool for the propagation of wave packets of different atomiceigenstates. As an example for the application of our theory, we study parity violatinggeometric (Berry-)phases. In this context, we define geometric flux densities,which for certain field configurations can be used to illustrate geometricphases in a vector diagram. Considering an example with a specific fieldconfiguration, we prove the existence of a parity violating geometric phase.

AU Microscopii, a nearby M dwarf star surrounded by a debris disk, presents an intriguing target in the search for exoplanets via the transit method. Using photometric observations from the Hubble Space Telescope taken between 2015 and 2017, we conducted a monitoring campaign of AU Mic to detect potential transiting planets. Through analysis of the star's light curve, we sought to identify any periodic dimming that could indicate an orbiting planet crossing in front of the star. Our analysis initially revealed two periodic signals less than 1% in depth; however, additional observations were needed to verify these signals represented genuine planetary transits. Supplemental Hubble monitoring from 2019 to 2020 failed to detect the same periodic dimming patterns. While no definitive evidence of transiting planets around AU Mic emerged, our investigation established stringent constraints on the presence of short-period Earth-sized worlds in its system. Continued long-term monitoring may yet uncover smaller planets transiting this nearby young star.

Scheduling acyclic task graphs (DAGs) is a common problem that arises in several real-world domains, such as scientific workflows, data processing pipelines, and project management. These DAGs are often subject to uncertainty, which can emerge from various sources, such as the st ochastic duration of tasks, the availability of resources, and the unreliability of the underlying infrastructure. To address this challenges, we present a novel algorithm for scheduling DAGs under uncertainty. Our algorithm, called RobustDAG, leverages a recently elaborated approach for robust optimization to find schedules that are resilient to uncertainty. We proof that RobustDAG provides provable guarantees on the quality of the schedules it generates, even in the presence of significant uncertainty. Furthermore, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm through extensive experiments on both synthesizing and real-world DAGs. Our results show that RobustDAG outperforms present approaches in terms of both solution quality and robustness. Finally, we discuss the potential applications of our work in several real-world domians.

A mathematical criterion for the single-photon sources used in quantum cryptography is proposed in this paper. The criterion is based on the probability distribution of the photon number in the output state of the source. The probability distribution is calculated using the density matrix formalism. The criterion is shown to be necessary and sufficient for the source to be a single-photon source. The criterion is also shown to be robust against noise and imperfections in the source.

In the first section, the authors give basic definitions and examples of special orbifolds. In the second section, they develop methods to deform and partially resolve orbifold singularities while preserving the Kähler and special properties. In the third section, they apply these methods to show that any two birational compact Kähler varieties with trivial canonical class are connected by a sequence of flops and modifications. In the fourth section, they introduce rational curves on orbifolds and use the rational connectedness of orbifolds to generalize Campana's theorem on the bimeromorphic rigidity of special manifolds to the orbifold setting. In the fifth section, they explore applications to the classification of Del Pezzo and Fano orbifolds. In the sixth section, they generalize Kollár's torsion results on the fundamental groups of smooth algebraic varieties to the singular case. As a result, they obtain a birational classification of compact Kähler threefolds with nef tangent bundle up to finite etale cover. It is shown that Del Pezzo orbifolds of dimension three or less are completely classified by their orbifold fundamental groups. In the last section, they give some applications to algebraic geometry, complex geometry, and the study of fundamental groups. In summary, this article establishes new methods to study the bimeromorphic geometry and classification of compact Kähler varieties via their higher-dimensional orbifold counterparts.

In this article, we explore the relationship between harmonic platoons in sphere bundles, normal neighbourhoods of reduction loci, and instanton moduli spaces on definite 4-manifolds. Vi begin by presenting the concept of harmonic sections in sphere bundles and their connection to the geometry of the bundle's base manifold. We then turn our attention to the role of habitual neighborhoods of reduction loci in the study of instanton moduli spaces, and how they relate to the geometry of the underlying 4-manifold. Next, we delve into the interaction between harmony sections and instanton moduli spaces, and how they are influenced by the definite nature of the 4-manifold. We show how the presence of a definite 4-manifold introduces a n ew level of structure into the theory, which in turn allows for a richer understanding of the interplay between harmonic sections and instanton moduli spaces. Our main result is the establishment of a correspondence between certain families of harmonic sections and instanton m oduli spaces on definite 4-manifolds. We demonstrate the utility of this correspondence by appying it to a number of concrete examples, including the study of instanton moduli spaces on certain 4-anifolds with a non-trivial fundamental group. In addition, we discuss the relationship between our results and previous wrok in the field, highlighting the ways in which our findings extend and generalize earlier results. We also outline a number of potential directions for future research, including the asks of our correspondence to the study of other geometric and topological invariants of definite 4-manifolds. Overall, our work provides a new perspective on the interplay between harmonic sections, normal neighborhoods of reduction loci, and instanton moduli spaces on definite 4˗manifolds, and contributes to a deeper understanding of the rich and complex geometry of these spaces.

Noncritical M-theory in 2+1 dimensions has been defined as a double-scalinglimit of a nonrelativistic Fermi liquid on a flat two-dimensional plane. Herewe study this noncritical M-theory in the limit of high energies, analogous tothe \alpha'\to\infty limit of string theory. In the related case oftwo-dimensional Type 0A strings, it has been argued that the conformal\alpha'\to\infty limit leads to AdS_2 with a propagating fermion whose mass isset by the value of the RR flux. Here we provide evidence that in thehigh-energy limit, the natural ground state of noncritical M-theory similarlydescribes the AdS_2\times S^1 spacetime, with a massless propagating fermion.We argue that the spacetime effective theory in this background is captured bya topological higher-spin extension of conformal Chern-Simons gravity in 2+1dimensions, consistently coupled to a massless Dirac field. Intriguingly, thetwo-dimensional plane populated by the original nonrelativistic fermions isessentially the twistor space associated with the symmetry group of theAdS_2\times S^1 spacetime; thus, at least in the high-energy limit, noncriticalM-theory can be nonperturbatively described as a "Fermi liquid on twistorspace."

The assumption of the capture by the Solar System of the electrically chargedPlanckian DM objects (daemons) from the galactic disk is confirmed not only bythe St.Petersburg (SPb) experiments detecting particles with V<30 km/s. Herethe daemon approach is analyzed considering the positive model independentresult of the DAMA/NaI experiment. We explain the maximum in DAMA signalsobserved in the May-June period to be associated with the formation behind theSun of a trail of daemons that the Sun captures into elongated orbits as itmoves to the apex. The range of significant 2-6-keV DAMA signals fits well theiodine nuclei elastically knocked out of the NaI(Tl) scintillator by particlesfalling on the Earth with V=30-50 km/s from strongly elongated heliocentricorbits. The half-year periodicity of the slower daemons observed in SPboriginates from the transfer of particles that are deflected through ~90 deginto near-Earth orbits each time the particles cross the outer reaches of theSun which had captured them. Their multi-loop (cross-like) trajectoriestraverse many times the Earth's orbit in March and September, which increasesthe probability for the particles to enter near-Earth orbits during this time.Corroboration of celestial mechanics calculations with observations yields~1e-19 cm2 for the cross section of daemon interaction with the solar matter.

We analyse the general features of localisation of fermions and scalars insmoothed field-theoretical versions of the type 2 Randall- Sundrum braneworldmodel. A scalar field domain-wall forms the brane, inducing warped gravity, andwe study the mass spectra of the matter fields in the dimensionally reducedtheory. We demonstrate explicitly that both scalar and fermion fields exhibit acontinuum of properly normalisable modes starting at zero mass. If discretebound modes are present in the gravity-free case, these become resonances inthe continuum, while off-resonant modes are highly suppressed on the brane. Wedescribe briefly how another scalar field can be used to break a symmetry onthe domain-wall while leaving it unbroken far from the wall, as has alreadybeen done in the flat space case. Finally we present numerical calculations fora toy model which demonstrates the decoupling of continuum modes at lowenergies, so the theory becomes four dimensional.

We show that for each discrete group G, the rational assembly map K_ (BG) \otimes Q \to K_ (C*_{max} G) \otimes \Q is injective on classes dualto the subring generated by cohomology classes of degree at most 2 (identifyingrational K-homology and homology via the Chern character). Our result implieshomotopy invariance of higher signatures associated to these cohomologyclasses. This consequence was first established by Connes-Gromov-Moscovici andMathai. Our approach is based on the construction of flat twisting bundles out ofsequences of almost flat bundles as first described in our previous work. Incontrast to the argument of Mathai, our approach is independent of (and indeedgives a new proof of) the result of Hilsum-Skandalis on the homotopy invarianceof the index of the signature operator twisted with bundles of small curvature.

We have carried out a survey toward the central regions of 85 starless coresin HCN J = 1-0 to study inward motions in the cores. Sixty-four cores weredetected with HCN lines. The infall asymmetry in the HCN spectra is found to bemore prevalent, and more prominent than in any other previously used infalltracers such as CS J = 2-1, DCO+ J = 2-1, and N2H+ J = 1-0. We found closerelation between the intensities of the HCN and N2H+ lines. This implies thatthe HCN is not much depleted in the central regions of the cores. In somecores, the HCN spectra show different sign of asymmetry from other molecularlines. A few cores show various signs of asymmetry in individual HCN hyperfinelines. The distribution of the velocity shift dV of the HCN profiles withrespect to the systemic velocity of the optically thin tracer is found to bemore shifted toward bluer side than those of other infall tracers, indicatingthat the HCN traces inward motions more frequently. The dV distribution of eachHCN hyperfine line for all sources is similar. Moreover the dV values obtainedfrom different HCN hyperfine lines for each source are nearly similar. Thesemay mean that most of starless cores are in similar kinematic states across thelayers of the cores. We identify 17 infall candidates using all availableindicators such as the velocity shift dV and the blue to red peak intensityratio of double peaked profiles for HCN J = 1-0, CS J = 2-1, J = 3-2, DCO+ J =2-1, and N2H+ J = 1-0. Four of them, L63, L492, L694-2, and L1197 are found toshow higher blue to red ratio in the HCN hyperfine line along the loweropacity, suggesting that infall speed becomes higher toward the center.
